# Viewer Clash Panel — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
>
> **STATUS: PLAN ONLY — IMPLEMENTATION NOT AUTHORIZED.** The milestone owner authorized *Viewer Clash Panel implementation planning only* (2026-09-26). Nothing below may be executed until the owner explicitly authorizes implementation **after an independent Work review of this plan**. No production Panel code, no `clashpanel/` directory, no Panel test and no branch exists. SVF2 live verification, host/OQ-1 integration and any Viewer Adapter / Core / M4 change are likewise **not authorized**. See §"Authorization boundary".
>
> **Internal review:** `docs/reviews/2026-09-26-viewer-clash-panel-implementation-plan-internal-codex-review.md` (convergence tool, **not** an independent gate). **Independent Work review #1** (`…-independent-review.md`, verdict *revise*, 0C/2H/1M/2L) was remediated in a bounded pass; the **bounded independent re-review** (`…-remediation-bounded-independent-rereview.md`, 0C/0H/1M/0L: test-documentation Medium) is remediated by a final bounded pass (T27 now also updates `test/README.md` and `test/acceptance/README.md`; see §"Independent Work review remediation"). **Owner-approved: OD-1(a) and OD-7(a)** — gate G-OD holds no implementation-blocking decision. **Next authorized action: final bounded independent Work re-review of the changed sections.** Implementation, SVF2 verification and OQ-1/host integration remain **not authorized**.

**Goal:** Deliver the owner-accepted Viewer Clash Panel v1 as a recognizable Viewer Clash Detection panel — Test Setup → Run / Status → Filters / Grouping → Result Navigation / List → Selected Clash Actions — on top of the already-accepted Federated Clash Test Core and Viewer Adapter, with **no edit to Core, Adapter, M4, `collision/`, `wwwroot/` or `server.js`**.

**Architecture:** A new top-level layer `clashpanel/` above `clashtest/` and `clashtest/viewer/`, in three parts: a headless, Node-tested **Panel core** (draft → definition, run controller, sealed-result index, filters, Group-by-Element, sorting, pagination, wording, view-model), a **ViewerBridge** that is the only Panel code allowed to mutate the Viewer (markers-only emphasis, guarded isolation, best-effort fit, write-ahead rollback ledger), and a thin **`Autodesk.Viewing.UI.DockingPanel`** presentation shell that renders the view-model and dispatches intents. The Panel consumes the Core only through an injected, narrowed `EnginePort` and reads `registry.bindingFor`; it never registers models, derives identity, wires unload, or invalidates placement (host composition / OQ-1). Every task before the [S]/[H] gates is executable against fakes; live Viewer/SVF2 behaviour is proven only later, under separate authorization.

**Tech Stack:** Node ≥ 22 ESM, `node:test` + `node:assert/strict`, hand-rolled fakes (no jsdom), Playwright + Chromium (already a devDependency) for the DOM suite (own runner `npm run test:clashpanel:dom`, **included in the default gate `npm test`**), the page's own r71 `window.THREE` (injected, never npm `three`) in the ViewerBridge.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-26-viewer-clash-panel-design.md` (**owner-accepted 2026-09-26; governing design baseline**, on `main` = `origin/main` = `6a55b50`). Supporting: `docs/research/2026-09-26-viewer-clash-panel-viewer-api-evidence.md`; reviews `docs/reviews/2026-09-26-viewer-clash-panel-design-{internal-codex-review,independent-review,bounded-independent-rereview}.md`; frozen Core spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-20-federated-clash-test-and-results-design.md`; Core `clashtest/README.md`; Adapter `clashtest/viewer/README.md`; T3 record `docs/research/2026-09-26-federated-clash-test-viewer-adapter-t3-live-acceptance.md` (SVF **non-OTG** only).

## Global Constraints

Every task's requirements implicitly include these (values copied from the spec/repo):

1. **Scope of edits.** Implementation may create/modify only: `clashpanel/**`, `test/clashpanel/**`, `scripts/run-dom-tests.mjs`, the T27 `package.json` `scripts` change — exactly one edited line (`"test"`) and two added lines (`"test:offline"`, `"test:clashpanel:dom"`) — the T27 documentation-only edits to `test/README.md` and `test/acceptance/README.md`, and (at handoff time, per `CLAUDE.md`) `docs/`. **Never** modified: `clashtest/**` (incl. `clashtest/viewer/**`, README rows), `collision/**`, `wwwroot/**`, `server.js`, `routes/**`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `test/clashtest/**`, `test/fixtures/**` (reused read-only), frozen specs and accepted plans. A task that seems to need such an edit STOPS and records a plan contradiction instead (spec §3 "no adapter extension").
2. **Layering (spec §5.1; enforced by the Task 1 guard).** `clashpanel/core/**` imports only siblings (`./*.js`) and, optionally, the public barrel `../../clashtest/index.js`; it contains none of `Autodesk|Viewing|window|document|globalThis.THREE`. `clashpanel/viewer/**` imports only siblings and `../core/constants.js` and receives the Viewer facade, `THREE` and event names **by injection**. `clashpanel/ui/**` is the only place DOM/`Autodesk` may appear. Nothing under `clashtest/` or `collision/` imports `clashpanel/` (`wwwroot/` is not scanned: the host shell, gated H1, is the one place that imports it); nothing under `clashpanel/` imports `clashtest/viewer`, `clashtest/*` internals or `collision/`. The Panel never imports `ENGINE_LIMIT_DEFAULTS` / `RUN_OPTION_DEFAULTS` as if they were effective values (spec §5.2); Core errors are discriminated by `error.name` (spec §13 rule 4), so `core/` normally needs no `clashtest` import at all.
3. **Markers-only (spec PD-16, AC-P19).** No `setThemingColor`, `clearThemingColors`, `getThemingColor` or any theming call anywhere in `clashpanel/**` (static ban in Task 1 + runtime negative controls in Tasks 22/25); foreign theming is never read, cleared or overwritten; Panel-owned overlay meshes are removed deterministically by exact reference from a ledger. No `viewer.impl.*`, no `Autodesk.Viewing.Private.*`; the Panel never changes the Viewer **selection** and never restores the **camera**.
4. **Untrusted text (spec §8.2, AC-P13).** Model names, element names, Core `message`s, error text, diagnostics and `measurementBasis.reason` are inserted into the DOM only via `textContent` (`ui/dom.js`); `innerHTML|outerHTML|insertAdjacentHTML|document.write` are statically banned in `clashpanel/ui/**` (Task 1).
5. **Registration boundary (spec PD-18, AC-P20).** The `EnginePort` handed to `clashpanel/core` exposes exactly `validateTest, startRun, retainResultSet, releaseResultSet, getPersistenceState, getFreshness, assessNoClashClaim, derivations.{summarize,groupBy,filter}, registry.bindingFor` — never `register`, `unregister`, `invalidateModelPlacement`, `wireModelUnload`, `dispose`, `keyOf`. Absent/stale binding ⇒ disabled Run / `unavailable` rows; the Panel never repairs it.
6. **Sealed-result browsing (spec PD-7).** No result list before `done`; during a run only `RunProgress` fractions/counts and the Panel's own elapsed clock are shown — **no ETA, throughput, CPU/RAM/heap/WASM telemetry** (PD-13). No streaming partial browse.
7. **Bounded UI (spec PD-6, §12).** The DOM never renders more than one page (`PAGE_SIZE`); ordered indexes are typed arrays. The Panel's *predicate* passes (record filters, label-index warm-up) are sliced (`LIST_CHUNK_SIZE`) with a scheduler yield and a generation check. Typed-array index construction (fills, group flattening) is linear and the gap/group sorts are comparison sorts; all are synchronous, one-shot-per-user-action passes and, like the three Core derivation captures (spec §7.3), are recorded as **PG-3 measurement items** — the Panel makes no "never blocks" claim (spec §10.1). Page size, debounce, chunk size, cache size and poll interval are **presentation constants** (`core/constants.js`), never exported from the core barrel, never called limits or calibrated (PD-14, AC-P11). No wall-clock assertion anywhere (G-CAL/G-RESP).
8. **Generation guard (spec §5.2, AC-P15).** Every asynchronous completion (`done`, `summarize`, `groupBy`, caveat mask, `getFreshness`, `assessNoClashClaim`, label passes, catalog refresh, filter passes, basis verdict) captures the controller generation at issue time and commits only if it still matches; a superseded run's late `done` releases its own set and displays nothing. Core derivations go through ONE single-flight queue (max 2 concurrent in Core; the Panel uses 1) with one successful computation per `(generation, spec)`.
9. **No `getPairStatus` / `getElementStatus` on any interactive path** (spec §7.5, AC-P4); per-row "unverified" comes only from the cached `caveated` filter mask; per-pair absence statements exist only at run level via `assessNoClashClaim` + the Panel-recomputed gap list.
10. **Soft fails closed (spec PD-17, AC-P18).** Soft is available iff exactly one model participates or `ModelCatalog.measurementBasis(P)` is `verified`; anything else (incl. missing method, throw, timeout, malformed) ⇒ unavailable with the fixed explanation; Hard always stays available; display-unit conversion never substitutes for a basis; the gap unit label lives in the single constant `GAP_UNIT_LABEL` (OD-13 Part 2).
11. **One canonical default gate covers both suites (independent Work review H2).** From T27, `npm test` = `npm run test:offline && npm run test:clashpanel:dom`: the offline suite (`test:offline` = `node scripts/run-tests.mjs`, collects only `*.test.mjs`, never launches Chromium; no `*.test.mjs` imports `playwright`) and then the real-browser DOM suite (`*.dom.mjs`, collected only by `scripts/run-dom-tests.mjs`). Either half failing — or Chromium missing — fails `npm test` (never a silent skip), so the default command cannot stay green while the DockingPanel/UI suite is broken. No script invokes `npm test` (no recursion; T27's `domIsolation.test.mjs` proves it); `test:clashpanel:dom` stays available for targeted runs. Before T27 there is no DOM suite and `npm test` ≡ the offline suite. No live server, no APS credentials, no SVF2 content in either suite. **Owner-visible consequence:** the default gate now needs Playwright's Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium`, already needed by `test:acceptance`); this reverses the older "plain `npm test` never needs a browser" prose, so T27 updates `test/README.md` and `test/acceptance/README.md` in the same commit (Findings 8) and guards the wording with an offline test.
12. **Green at every commit.** RED exists only inside a task's own steps (write failing test → see it fail → implement → see it pass). Each task's committed checkpoint leaves the repository's default gate green — **`npm test`**: for T1–T26 that is the offline suite only (`npm test` ≡ `node scripts/run-tests.mjs`; either command may be run), for T27–T33 it is the offline suite AND the DOM suite, and `npm test` is THE checkpoint command; no task commits red scaffolding. Guards that need production files use the `scaffold.test.mjs` list (Task 1), which grows in the task that adds each module.
13. **Baseline to preserve:** the full offline suite (`node scripts/run-tests.mjs` = `npm run test:offline`) at `6a55b50` = **2,972 total / 2,971 pass / 0 fail / 1 pre-existing todo** (handoff, independently reproduced; re-measured at plan time — see Verification log). The total only ever grows; re-measure at implementation start and use that figure. The sandbox may add the known three local-ephemeral-port `EPERM` failures (`test/performance/m4/spike-server.test.mjs`); they are not Panel regressions.
14. **Commits** are Conventional Commits `type(clashpanel): subject`, end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` and contain **no** `Claude-Session:` trailer (user's global rule). Commit only after implementation has been authorized (this plan itself is never committed by the planning task unless the owner asks).
15. **Format neutrality (spec PD-15, §2.1).** No `isOTG`/model-format branching anywhere in the Panel; there is no format selector. SVF2/OTG is the required v1 target, but nothing SVF2-specific is verified by this plan's executable tasks — every test uses fakes or SVF-agnostic real Core over synthetic worlds. Historical Adapter/T3 evidence (SVF non-OTG) is never cited as SVF2 evidence.
16. **Host-composition boundary (spec §5.1).** Model loading (as SVF2), `modelKey`/`modelVersion` derivation, `registry.register`, re-registration after reload, `wireModelUnload`, `invalidateModelPlacement`, the measurement-basis verdict, static routes, extension/toolbar registration are host duties (gated [H]); the Panel package documents the contract it consumes (Task 32 README) and stops.
17. **No `elementCount`** (`provenance.models[].elementCount`, G-EC) is consumed or displayed (static ban in Task 1, AC-P12).

## Plan-level technical decisions (not product decisions; reversible in review)

* **PL-1 DOM tests are real-browser** (Playwright + Chromium via `page.route`, no server, no live Viewer), with its **own runner**, because the spec forbids a fake DOM and jsdom is absent; the offline suite (`test:offline`) stays Chromium-free, but the DOM suite is **part of the default gate `npm test`** (independent Work review H2). Feasibility was probed in this sandbox (module serving + inert `textContent`).
* **PL-2 Error discrimination by `error.name`**, so `clashpanel/core` needs no `clashtest` import.
* **PL-3 Port completions (clarifications of spec §5.2/§9, not contradictions):** `ModelCatalog` also exposes `displayNameFor(modelKey)`, `keyOfModel(model)` and a `loaded` flag on entries (the spec already requires a name map that outlives unload, a `WeakMap<Model,modelKey>`, and readiness); the `ViewerBridge` port also exposes `checkIsolationPrerequisite()`, `readAggregateSelection()` (read-only, for "Use current selection") and `onModelLeft()` (the Panel's own `BEFORE_MODEL_UNLOAD` + `MODEL_REMOVED` listener, spec §11.2).
* **PL-4 No-clash gap list is recomputed Panel-side** from sealed `outcome`+`ledger` because `assessNoClashClaim` does not return which conjunct failed (differential test against Core in T11).
* **PL-5 Overlay API** is the public `viewer.overlays.*` facade (mesh-first), not `viewer.impl.*` — the spec's "overlay scene" wording maps to it (the existing extension's proven path).

## Findings from repository verification (code is authoritative; none forces a design change)

1. `RunSummary.resultSet` can be `null` (Run.js O7 deviation) — the Panel must show the unexpected-failure headline and no list (T8/T11/T17).
2. `assessNoClashClaim` exposes no failed-conjunct list (PL-4).
3. Barrel `getFreshness(set,{registry,enumerator?,ctx?})` differs from `engine.getFreshness(runIdOrSet,{signal?})`; the Panel uses only the engine form.
4. First `state` event reports `planning`/`enumerating`; no event at `queued`; `persistence` events may follow `terminal`; `progress` is never emitted (T8).
5. `retainResultSet` requires persistence `saved` (residency matrix, T9).

## Review Focus

Failure modes and inputs the spec implies but that no requirement-driven task would otherwise exercise, most likely first. Each is pinned by a test **inside the owning task** (marked "Review Focus pin" there).

1. **Double-click on Run (or `RUN_START` twice in one tick).** Expected: exactly one `startRun`; the second is silently ignored, no second admission-error banner — Task 16.
2. **Two loaded models with the same display name** (Viewer models frequently share a file name). Expected: every place a model name appears (setup checklist, row chips, model filter, group labels) stays distinguishable via a deterministic short-key suffix, while unique names are untouched; blank names fall back to `Model <short key>` — Task 15.
3. **A model unloads or is hidden while a run is still in progress.** Expected: no Viewer mutation (nothing is displayed yet), the run seals normally, no exception, freshness is re-checked, and afterwards the affected rows are `unavailable` while list/counts/filters/grouping still work; the `BEFORE_MODEL_UNLOAD` + `MODEL_REMOVED` pair is idempotent — Task 18 (and Task 20 against the real engine).
4. **Editing the setup during or after a run.** Expected: the running/displayed run is unaffected, "Setup changed" is shown, and edit-then-revert followed by Run reuses the same `definitionKey` (revision monotone, `resultId`s stable) — Tasks 16/17.
5. **Very long unbroken names (10,000 characters, no spaces)** in model names, element labels, group labels, banners, validation messages and Run details. Expected: inert text, no horizontal overflow of the panel or any row, DOM size unchanged versus short names — Task 30 (real browser).

**Known residuals carried to the gates (recorded, not test pins).** (a) If a user hides Viewer nodes *during* a Panel-owned isolation session whose prior state was empty, the restoring `setAggregateIsolation([])` reveals them — implemented exactly per spec §9.5 (hidden-state is checked at session start only); whether `getAggregateHiddenNodes()` reports nodes hidden by the Panel's own isolation is unknown → G2. (b) `ClearOutcome.isolation` `'failed'` vs `'skipped-external'` wording depends on the live behaviour of `getAggregateIsolation` → G2. (c) World-space correctness of `getNodeBox` (outline overlays), the aggregate `fitToView` union bounds, `BufferGeometry#setFromPoints` in the page's r71 THREE, and whether the base `DockingPanel.initialize()` builds its own title bar → G2. (d) The real `BEFORE_MODEL_UNLOAD` / `MODEL_REMOVED` ordering for one model → G2. (e) `waitingForOtherRun` is a hedge (Core publishes nothing between admission and plan adoption) — the wording never asserts it. (f) `enumeration-failed` is opaque; the Panel offers only likely causes (spec §13). (g) Result counts, latency, memory and the synchronous Result-Set capture pause of the three Core derivations are unmeasured → G3 / PG-3.

| `ViewerApi` | `eventNames`; aggregate fit is `fitToView(list, undefined, immediate)` (list in the FIRST slot; evidence §2.3) | single event-name injection point; corrects the catalog's earlier slot order |
| Core-facing helpers | `explainNoClashGaps` (Panel recomputation), `explainNoClashGaps(set,{freshness?,claim?})`, `mapAdmissionError(error,{heldRunId})`, `runHeadline({…,resultSet})`, `emptyStatement` returns `null` for non-empty sets | `assessNoClashClaim` exposes no failed conjunct; `DIGEST_VERSION` is not in the barrel |
| Run state | extra `runId`, `stopRequested`, `lastSeq`; a `poll` event drives `waitingForOtherRun`; residency reports pending/failed/skipped as `held-unsaved` | stale-event guard; Core publishes nothing between admission and plan adoption |
| `INTENT` / payloads | `SETUP_TOGGLE_COLLAPSED`; payload shapes fixed in `core/intents.js` (`FILTER_MODEL {value:string[]}`, `NAV_PAGE {page}` 0-based, …) | Setup must be re-expandable; UI/controller must agree |
| `Banner` / ViewModel | `Banner.action {label, intent}`; `vm.run.diagnostics`; `vm.run.details` (spec §8.4); `dispatch(DIAGNOSTICS_COPY)` resolves the diagnostics string | otherwise `RUN_RELEASE_AND_RETRY` / confirm-clear / Copy diagnostics / Run details are unreachable from the UI |
| UI | `createPanelShell({Autodesk, parentContainer, controller, …})` (no Viewer reference); `createClashPanel.dispose()` rejects with `AggregateError` after all cleanup steps ran | AC-P21; no failing step may strand another |
| Lifecycle (internal review) | `controller.dispose()` cancels the active run and resolves only after that run's `done` settled, its set was released and the bridge disposed (never rejects; idempotent; a host that must not wait calls `engine.dispose()`); `createClashPanel.dispose()` awaits it | a resolved dispose must mean Core slot + Viewer resources are released (Codex plan review H-2) |
| Residency (internal review) | a failed release keeps a `stuck` entry retried on the next Run/Clear/dispose; `release()` returns `stuckCount`; after an explicit discard confirmation the old set is released **before** `startRun` (single-slot Core admission), ordinary replacement stays admission-first | a failed lease release must not strand a slot; Core admission with `maxResidentResultSets: 1` |
| Setup validation (internal review) | pre-run `binding-stale` finding when `binding.model !== catalogEntry.model` (both directions) | "stale binding disables Run" needs an operational witness (Codex plan review H-1) |
| Filters/list (internal review) | caveated mask is `pending | ready | unavailable`; `runFilterPass` returns `'mask-missing'` (never an empty match set) and the controller shows `FILTER_MASK_UNAVAILABLE_TEXT`; `navNeighbor` honors `navScope` only for an expanded group | a failed Core derivation must not read as "zero unverified clashes" |
| ViewerBridge (internal review) | `fitSides(viewerApi, sides, isCurrent)` guards every camera call; a failed isolation restore / failed mesh removal keep their ledger records for retry; isolation pre-image is read immediately before the write-ahead record; overlay scene names are per-instance; scene creation is write-ahead and a scene is never removed under a Panel mesh | stale work must not touch the Viewer; cleanup failures must keep recovery state (Codex plan review, bridge slice) |
| UI (internal review) | DockingPanel construction is transactional (no orphaned container); radio names are per panel; the model filter shows "Multiple models (n)" | Codex plan review, UI slice |
| Claim gate (independent Work review H1) | `emptyStatement` requires `claim.allowed === true` ∧ `freshness.state === 'current'` over ONE pair (a missing half ⇒ pending); T17 commits `freshness`+`claim` together only when both reads of the same check completed and withdraws the held claim when a re-check starts; `viewModel.claimGateOf` hands over only a settled pair | `getFreshness` and `assessNoClashClaim` each recompute live freshness; an `allowed` claim could be worded next to a stale badge |
| Default test gate (independent Work review H2) | `npm test` = `npm run test:offline && npm run test:clashpanel:dom`; `test:offline` = the old `node scripts/run-tests.mjs`; `domIsolation.test.mjs` gains a wiring + no-recursion guard and two README guards (7 tests) | the default command must not stay green while the DockingPanel/UI suite is broken |
| Test infrastructure | DOM harness origin `https://panel.test` (secure context for `crypto.randomUUID`); real-browser suite with its own runner but included in the default `npm test` gate (H2); one Viewer fake, one Core-exact controller harness | PL-1; avoids duplicate fakes drifting |

**Code-vs-spec facts recorded (code authoritative):** a Stop while the only unit is in flight seals `cancelled` with `coverage:'full'` (spec §7.2 implies partial) — the Panel reads the sealed axis and never infers it; Core rejects a `selectionB` that is the *same object* as `selectionA` (self-clash definitions are deep-copied by `buildDefinition`); a scripted witness with an unknown `kind` makes a real run seal `failed` with `unit:internal-error` (use `surface-crossing`); real-engine runs under Node need no injected clock/yield; the spec §8.3 sentence "No clashes match the current filters" contains the phrase AC-P2 bans in bare form, so the wording matrix allows exactly that sentence plus the two §7.5 claim sentences.

### Task 1: Layering guard, scaffold, and presentation constants

**Tier:** [A] format-agnostic headless

**Files:**
- Create: `test/clashpanel/support/layering.mjs`
- Create: `test/clashpanel/layering.test.mjs`
- Create: `test/clashpanel/scaffold.test.mjs`
- Create: `clashpanel/core/constants.js`
- Test: `test/clashpanel/core/constants.test.mjs`

**Scope note:** the guard mirrors `test/clashtest/viewer/support/layering.mjs` (same `stripComments` / `importSpecifiers` mechanism) but resolves every specifier to a repo-relative path and applies **per-subtree** allow-lists (`core`, `viewer`, `ui`, `index`), so `ui/render/x.js -> ../dom.js` and `core/x.js -> ../../clashtest/index.js` are judged by where they land, not by their spelling. `clashpanel/core/constants.js` is created in this task so the real-tree tests are non-vacuous from the first commit (the layering test asserts `files.length > 0`). The scaffold test lists `EXPECTED_MODULES`; **every later task that creates a `clashpanel/**/*.js` file appends it to that array in the same task** (the test also fails on an unlisted file, so a forgotten entry is caught immediately). **AC-P11 hand-off:** `core/index.js` does not exist until Task 19, so this task pins only what exists (the exact export list of `constants.js`, no limit/calibration wording). **Task 19 MUST add** the barrel assertion "`Object.keys(coreIndex)` shares no name with `constants.js`", and **Task 32** the same for `clashpanel/index.js`.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing from production code (Node built-ins `node:path`, `node:fs` in tests only).
- Produces (test support, `test/clashpanel/support/layering.mjs`): `stripComments(source): string`, `importSpecifiers(source): string[]`, `resolveSpecifier(fromRel: string, spec: string): string | null`, `subtreeOf(rel: string): 'core'|'viewer'|'ui'|'index'|null`, `placementProblem(rel: string): string | null`, `violations(rel: string, source: string): { imports: string[], globals: string[], banned: string[] }`, `importsClashpanel(source: string): string[]`, `ALLOWED_IMPORTS`, `GLOBAL_BANS`, `IDENTIFIER_BANS`, `VIEWER_BANS`, `UI_BANS`, `CLEAN`.
- Produces (production): `clashpanel/core/constants.js` — exactly the names in the shared catalog: `PAGE_SIZE, FILTER_DEBOUNCE_MS, LIST_CHUNK_SIZE, LABEL_CACHE_MAX, READINESS_POLL_MS, DERIVATION_BUSY_RETRY_MS, DERIVATION_BUSY_MAX_RETRIES, BASIS_VERDICT_TIMEOUT_MS, GAP_UNIT_LABEL, GAP_DECIMALS, SOFT_UNAVAILABLE_TEXT`.

**Depends on:** none (first task).

```js
// test/clashpanel/layering.test.mjs
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, relative, sep } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import {
  CLEAN, importSpecifiers, importsClashpanel, placementProblem, resolveSpecifier, stripComments, subtreeOf, violations,
} from './support/layering.mjs';

const ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../', import.meta.url));
const SKIP = new Set(['node_modules', 'vendor', '.git']);
const walk = (dir) => (existsSync(dir) ? readdirSync(dir).flatMap((n) => {
  if (SKIP.has(n)) return [];
  const p = join(dir, n);
  return statSync(p).isDirectory() ? walk(p) : [p];
}) : []);
const rel = (f) => relative(ROOT, f).split(sep).join('/');

const CORE = 'clashpanel/core/draft.js';
const VIEWER = 'clashpanel/viewer/ViewerBridge.js';
const UI = 'clashpanel/ui/ClashDockingPanel.js';
const RENDER = 'clashpanel/ui/render/setup.js';
const INDEX = 'clashpanel/index.js';
const imp = (spec) => `import a from '${spec}';`;

test('checker: finds static, multi-line, re-export, star, side-effect and dynamic specifiers', () => {
  const src = [
    "import a from './a.js';",
    "export { b } from './b.js';",
    "export * from './c.js';",
    "import './d.js';",
    "import {\n  e,\n  f,\n} from './e.js';",
    "import{g}from'./g.js';",
    "const m = await import('./h.js');",
  ].join('\n');
  assert.deepEqual(importSpecifiers(src).sort(), ['./a.js', './b.js', './c.js', './d.js', './e.js', './g.js', './h.js']);
});

test('checker: ignores specifiers and identifiers that occur only in comments', () => {
  const src = "// import x from '../viewer/x.js'\n/* window Autodesk setThemingColor elementCount */ export const a = 1;";
  assert.deepEqual(violations(CORE, src), CLEAN);
});

test('checker: resolveSpecifier maps relative specifiers to repo-relative paths and leaves others null', () => {
  assert.equal(resolveSpecifier(CORE, '../../clashtest/index.js'), 'clashtest/index.js');
  assert.equal(resolveSpecifier(RENDER, '../dom.js'), 'clashpanel/ui/dom.js');
  assert.equal(resolveSpecifier(RENDER, '../../core/intents.js'), 'clashpanel/core/intents.js');
  assert.equal(resolveSpecifier(CORE, './x.js'), 'clashpanel/core/x.js');
  assert.equal(resolveSpecifier(CORE, 'node:fs'), null);
  assert.equal(resolveSpecifier(CORE, '/clashpanel/core/x.js'), null);
});

test('checker: subtreeOf and placementProblem classify every path', () => {
  assert.equal(subtreeOf('clashpanel/core/draft.js'), 'core');
  assert.equal(subtreeOf('clashpanel/viewer/isolation.js'), 'viewer');
  assert.equal(subtreeOf('clashpanel/ui/dom.js'), 'ui');
  assert.equal(subtreeOf('clashpanel/ui/render/setup.js'), 'ui');
  assert.equal(subtreeOf('clashpanel/index.js'), 'index');
  for (const bad of ['clashpanel/foo.js', 'clashpanel/core/sub/x.js', 'clashpanel/viewer/render/x.js', 'clashpanel/ui/render/deep/x.js', 'clashpanel/other/x.js']) {
    assert.equal(subtreeOf(bad), null, bad);
    assert.match(placementProblem(bad), /not in a known clashpanel subtree/, bad);
  }
  assert.equal(placementProblem('clashpanel/README.md'), null);
  for (const bad of ['clashpanel/core/x.mjs', 'clashpanel/core/x.ts', 'clashpanel/notes.md', 'clashpanel/ui/x.css', 'clashpanel/core/x.cjs']) {
    assert.match(placementProblem(bad), /only \.js modules and the root README\.md/, bad);
  }
});

test('core rule: allows siblings and the clashtest barrel only (negative controls for everything else)', () => {
  for (const ok of ['./draft.js', './constants.js', '../../clashtest/index.js']) {
    assert.deepEqual(violations(CORE, imp(ok)), CLEAN, ok);
```

```js
// test/clashpanel/scaffold.test.mjs
// Presence guard for the production modules that exist at each checkpoint. Each task that creates a module
// clashpanel/<path>.js appends <path>.js to EXPECTED_MODULES in the SAME task (so this file is RED inside a task
// before the module exists and GREEN at that task's commit; it is never committed red). The second test fails on a
// module that exists but is not listed, so a forgotten entry cannot slip through.
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { existsSync, readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, relative, sep } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const DIR = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../clashpanel/', import.meta.url));
const EXPECTED_MODULES = [
  'core/constants.js',
];

const walk = (dir) => readdirSync(dir).flatMap((n) => {
  const p = join(dir, n);
  return statSync(p).isDirectory() ? walk(p) : [p];
});

test('scaffold: every production module created so far exists', () => {
  for (const name of EXPECTED_MODULES) assert.ok(existsSync(join(DIR, name)), `clashpanel/${name} is missing`);
});

test('scaffold: no clashpanel/**/*.js file exists that the scaffold does not list', () => {
  const found = walk(DIR).filter((f) => f.endsWith('.js')).map((f) => relative(DIR, f).split(sep).join('/')).sort();
  assert.deepEqual(found, [...EXPECTED_MODULES].sort());
});
```

```js
// test/clashpanel/support/layering.mjs
// Layering guard for clashpanel/ (spec 5.1, AC-P10/AC-P11/AC-P12/AC-P13/AC-P19 static parts). Mirrors
// test/clashtest/viewer/support/layering.mjs (stripComments / importSpecifiers), but every specifier is resolved to a
// repo-relative path and judged against a PER-SUBTREE allow-list, so an import is judged by where it lands.
import { posix } from 'node:path';

const SEG = '[A-Za-z0-9_-]+';

/** Allowed import TARGETS (repo-relative, resolved) per subtree. Anything else is a violation. */
export const ALLOWED_IMPORTS = Object.freeze({
  core: [new RegExp(`^clashpanel/core/${SEG}\\.js$`), /^clashtest\/index\.js$/],
  viewer: [new RegExp(`^clashpanel/viewer/${SEG}\\.js$`), /^clashpanel\/core\/constants\.js$/],
  ui: [
    new RegExp(`^clashpanel/ui/${SEG}\\.js$`), new RegExp(`^clashpanel/ui/render/${SEG}\\.js$`),
    /^clashpanel\/core\/(constants|intents)\.js$/,
  ],
  index: [
    /^clashpanel\/core\/index\.js$/, new RegExp(`^clashpanel/viewer/${SEG}\\.js$`), new RegExp(`^clashpanel/ui/${SEG}\\.js$`),
  ],
});

/** core + viewer only: the headless layers never see a Viewer/DOM global (AC-P10). `globalThis.setTimeout` etc. stay legal. */
export const GLOBAL_BANS = Object.freeze([
  ['Autodesk', /\bAutodesk\b/], ['Viewing', /\bViewing\b/], ['window', /\bwindow\b/], ['document', /\bdocument\b/],
  ['globalThis.THREE', /\bglobalThis\s*\.\s*THREE\b/], ['globalThis[]', /\bglobalThis\s*\[/],
]);

/** every subtree: no Viewer theming (PD-16, AC-P19), no private Viewer API, no element counts (G-EC, AC-P12). */
export const IDENTIFIER_BANS = Object.freeze([
  ['theming', /ThemingColor/],                                         // set/clear/getThemingColor(s)
  ['Private.', /\bPrivate\./],
  ['viewer.impl', /\.\s*impl\b|\[\s*['"`]impl['"`]\s*\]/],
  ['elementCount', /elementCount/],
  ['non-literal import()', /\bimport\s*\(\s*(?!['"])/],
  ['require()', /\brequire\s*\(/],
]);

/** viewer only: the injected THREE is r71, whose Vector3 has no setScalar (use .set(x, y, z)). */
export const VIEWER_BANS = Object.freeze([['setScalar', /\bsetScalar\b/]]);

/** ui + index only: text is inserted with textContent, never as markup (AC-P13). */
export const UI_BANS = Object.freeze([
  ['innerHTML', /\binnerHTML\b/], ['outerHTML', /\bouterHTML\b/], ['insertAdjacentHTML', /\binsertAdjacentHTML\b/],
  ['document.write', /\bdocument\s*\.\s*write/], ['createContextualFragment', /\bcreateContextualFragment\b/],
  ['DOMParser', /\bDOMParser\b/],
]);

export const CLEAN = Object.freeze({ imports: [], globals: [], banned: [] });

export function stripComments(source) {
  return source.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, '').replace(/(^|[^:'"`\\])\/\/[^\n]*/g, '$1');
}

export function importSpecifiers(source) {
  const out = [];
  const patterns = [
    /(?:^|[\n;])\s*(?:import|export)\b[^'"`;]*?\bfrom\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"]/g,   // import x from / export {..} from / export * from
    /(?:^|[\n;])\s*import\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"]/g,                               // import 'x'
    /\bimport\(\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"]\s*\)/g,                                    // import('x')
  ];
  for (const re of patterns) for (const m of source.matchAll(re)) out.push(m[1]);
  return [...new Set(out)];
}

/** Relative specifier -> repo-relative posix path; anything that is not `./` or `../` (bare, absolute, URL) -> null. */
export function resolveSpecifier(fromRel, spec) {
  if (!spec.startsWith('./') && !spec.startsWith('../')) return null;
  return posix.normalize(posix.join(posix.dirname(fromRel), spec));
}

/** 'core' | 'viewer' | 'ui' | 'index' for a recognised clashpanel/**.js path, else null. */
export function subtreeOf(rel) {
  if (rel === 'clashpanel/index.js') return 'index';
  if (new RegExp(`^clashpanel/core/${SEG}\\.js$`).test(rel)) return 'core';
  if (new RegExp(`^clashpanel/viewer/${SEG}\\.js$`).test(rel)) return 'viewer';
  if (new RegExp(`^clashpanel/ui/(?:render/)?${SEG}\\.js$`).test(rel)) return 'ui';
  return null;
}

/** null when `rel` may exist under clashpanel/; otherwise the reason it may not. */
export function placementProblem(rel) {
  if (rel === 'clashpanel/README.md') return null;
  if (!rel.endsWith('.js')) return `${rel}: clashpanel/ holds only .js modules and the root README.md`;
  return subtreeOf(rel) === null ? `${rel}: not in a known clashpanel subtree (core, viewer, ui, ui/render, index.js)` : null;
}

export function violations(rel, source) {
  const out = { imports: [], globals: [], banned: [] };
  const subtree = subtreeOf(rel);
  const code = stripComments(source);
  if (subtree !== null) {
    for (const spec of importSpecifiers(code)) {
      const resolved = resolveSpecifier(rel, spec);
      if (resolved === null || !ALLOWED_IMPORTS[subtree].some((re) => re.test(resolved))) out.imports.push(spec);
    }
  }
  const bans = [
    ...(subtree === 'core' || subtree === 'viewer' ? GLOBAL_BANS : []),
    ...IDENTIFIER_BANS,
    ...(subtree === 'viewer' ? VIEWER_BANS : []),
    ...(subtree === 'ui' || subtree === 'index' ? UI_BANS : []),
  ];
  for (const [name, re] of bans) {
    if (!re.test(code)) continue;
    if (GLOBAL_BANS.some(([n]) => n === name)) out.globals.push(name);
    else out.banned.push(name);
  }
  return out;
}

/** Reverse guard: every specifier (relative or absolute) in `source` that names the clashpanel tree. */
export function importsClashpanel(source) {
  return importSpecifiers(stripComments(source)).filter((s) => /(^|\/)clashpanel(\/|$)/.test(s));
}
```

**Scope note:** the Task 3 fakes do not exist yet, so these tests use small INLINE stubs (a manual timer scheduler, hand-rolled catalogs, a `Proxy` engine). `narrowEnginePort` is the structural half of AC-P20: it hands the controller an object with **exactly** the catalog's members, so `register`, `unregister`, `keyOf`, `notifyPlacementChanged`, `invalidateModelPlacement`, `dispose` (and every other engine method) are unreachable by construction. `readBasisVerdict` is the fail-closed reader behind PD-17/AC-P18: it never rejects for a host misbehavior, every failure class maps to a distinct fixed reason, and a host `reason` is carried as a plain string only (never parsed, never interpreted as markup). **Additive to the catalog:** `generation.onBump(cb) -> unsubscribe` (Task 7's queue uses it to abort promptly) and `scheduler.assertScheduler(s)`; every catalog name and signature is unchanged.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `BASIS_VERDICT_TIMEOUT_MS` from `./constants.js` (Task 1). Real engine surface (read from `clashtest/engine.js` `ENGINE_METHODS` and the frozen `engine` at `:1359`): `engine.{validateTest,startRun,retainResultSet,releaseResultSet,getPersistenceState,getFreshness,assessNoClashClaim}`, `engine.derivations.{summarize,groupBy,filter}`, `engine.registry.bindingFor`.
- Produces:
  - `scheduler.js`: `createDefaultScheduler(): Scheduler`, `assertScheduler(s): Scheduler` (`Scheduler = { now(): number, setTimeout(fn, ms): handle, clearTimeout(handle): void, yield(): Promise<void> }`).
  - `generation.js`: `createGeneration(): { current(): number, bump(): number, isCurrent(g: number): boolean, onBump(cb: (n: number) => void): () => void }`.
  - `ports.js`: `narrowEnginePort(engine): EnginePort` (frozen; throws `TypeError` naming the first missing member), `readBasisVerdict(catalog, modelKeys: string[], { scheduler, timeoutMs = BASIS_VERDICT_TIMEOUT_MS }): Promise<BasisVerdict>` (never rejects for host behavior; rejects `TypeError` only for a programmer error: non-array `modelKeys` or a malformed scheduler), `assertCatalogPort(catalog): catalog` (requires `list, displayNameFor, keyOfModel, onChange`; `measurementBasis` is deliberately optional, a missing one is fail-closed data, not a structural error), `assertBridgePort(bridge): bridge` (requires `present, clear, dispose, checkIsolationPrerequisite, readAggregateSelection, onModelLeft`), `BASIS_FAILURE_REASONS` (frozen `{ missing, threw, rejected, timeout, malformed }`, fixed strings).

```js
test('default scheduler: setTimeout fires once and clearTimeout cancels', async () => {

  await new Promise((resolve) => { s.setTimeout(() => { fired += 1; resolve(); }, 0); });
  assert.equal(fired, 1);
  let cancelled = 0;
```

```js
// test/clashpanel/core/generation.test.mjs
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { createGeneration } from '../../../clashpanel/core/generation.js';

test('generation: starts at 0, bump returns the new value, current tracks it', () => {
  const g = createGeneration();
  assert.equal(g.current(), 0);
  assert.equal(g.bump(), 1);
  assert.equal(g.bump(), 2);
  assert.equal(g.current(), 2);
});

test('generation: isCurrent is true only for the live value (monotone, never reused)', () => {
  const g = createGeneration();
  const first = g.current();
  g.bump();
  assert.equal(g.isCurrent(first), false);
  assert.equal(g.isCurrent(g.current()), true);
  assert.equal(g.isCurrent('1'), false);
  assert.equal(g.isCurrent(undefined), false);
  assert.equal(g.isCurrent(NaN), false);
});

test('generation: independent instances do not share state; the object is frozen', () => {
  const a = createGeneration();
  const b = createGeneration();
  a.bump();
  assert.equal(b.current(), 0);
  assert.ok(Object.isFrozen(a));
});

test('generation.onBump: listeners run synchronously with the new value, in registration order', () => {
  const g = createGeneration();
  const seen = [];
  g.onBump((n) => seen.push(['a', n]));
  g.onBump((n) => seen.push(['b', n]));
  g.bump();
  assert.deepEqual(seen, [['a', 1], ['b', 1]]);
});

test('generation.onBump: unsubscribe works, a throwing listener never breaks bump or its neighbours, non-functions throw', () => {
  const g = createGeneration();
  const seen = [];
  const off = g.onBump(() => seen.push('gone'));
  g.onBump(() => { throw new Error('listener'); });
  g.onBump(() => seen.push('kept'));
  off();
  assert.equal(g.bump(), 1);
  assert.deepEqual(seen, ['kept']);
  assert.throws(() => g.onBump('nope'), TypeError);
});

test('generation.onBump: a listener that unsubscribes itself during a bump does not skip the others', () => {
  const g = createGeneration();
  const seen = [];
  const off = g.onBump(() => { seen.push('self'); off(); });
  g.onBump(() => seen.push('other'));
  g.bump();
  g.bump();
  assert.deepEqual(seen, ['self', 'other', 'other']);
});
```

```js
// test/clashpanel/core/ports.test.mjs
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import {
  BASIS_FAILURE_REASONS, assertBridgePort, assertCatalogPort, narrowEnginePort, readBasisVerdict,
} from '../../../clashpanel/core/ports.js';
import { BASIS_VERDICT_TIMEOUT_MS } from '../../../clashpanel/core/constants.js';

import { createEngineWorld } from '../../clashtest/support/index.mjs';

// ---- inline stubs (Task 3 provides the shared fakes) -----------------------------------------------------------------
function manualScheduler() {
  let nextId = 1;
  const timers = new Map();
  const delays = [];
  return {
    now: () => 0,
    setTimeout(fn, ms) { const id = nextId; nextId += 1; timers.set(id, fn); delays.push(ms); return id; },
    clearTimeout(id) { timers.delete(id); },
    yield: async () => {},
    fire() { const fns = [...timers.values()]; timers.clear(); for (const fn of fns) fn(); },
    pending: () => timers.size,
    delays,
  };
}
const catalogWith = (measurementBasis) => ({ measurementBasis });
const read = (catalog, keys = ['a', 'b'], opts = {}) => readBasisVerdict(catalog, keys, { scheduler: manualScheduler(), ...opts });

const PORT_METHODS = ['validateTest', 'startRun', 'retainResultSet', 'releaseResultSet', 'getPersistenceState', 'getFreshness', 'assessNoClashClaim'];
function stubEngine(over = {}) {
  const calls = [];
  const spy = (name, ret) => function spyFn(...args) { calls.push({ name, args, self: this }); return ret; };
  const engine = {
    calls,
    validateTest: spy('validateTest', { issues: [], issuesTruncated: false }),
    startRun: spy('startRun', { runId: 'r1' }),
    retainResultSet: spy('retainResultSet', { release() {} }),
    releaseResultSet: spy('releaseResultSet', undefined),
    getPersistenceState: spy('getPersistenceState', null),
    getFreshness: spy('getFreshness', Promise.resolve({ state: 'current', reasons: [] })),
    assessNoClashClaim: spy('assessNoClashClaim', Promise.resolve({ allowed: false })),
    derivations: { summarize: spy('summarize', 1), groupBy: spy('groupBy', 2), filter: spy('filter', 3) },
    registry: { bindingFor: spy('bindingFor', null) },
    ...over,
  };
  return engine;
}

// ---- narrowEnginePort (AC-P20, structural half) ------------------------------------------------------------------------
test('narrowEnginePort: exposes EXACTLY the catalog members and is deeply frozen', () => {
  const port = narrowEnginePort(stubEngine());
  assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(port).sort(), [...PORT_METHODS, 'derivations', 'registry'].sort());
  assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(port.derivations).sort(), ['filter', 'groupBy', 'summarize']);
  assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(port.registry), ['bindingFor']);
  for (const o of [port, port.derivations, port.registry]) assert.ok(Object.isFrozen(o));
});

test('narrowEnginePort: forwards arguments and results unchanged and keeps the engine as `this`', () => {
  const engine = stubEngine();
  const port = narrowEnginePort(engine);
  const def = { testId: 't' };
  assert.deepEqual(port.startRun(def, { persist: false }), { runId: 'r1' });
  port.registry.bindingFor('mA');
  port.derivations.groupBy({ set: 1 }, ['element'], { signal: null });
  assert.deepEqual(engine.calls.map((c) => c.name), ['startRun', 'bindingFor', 'groupBy']);
  assert.deepEqual(engine.calls[0].args, [def, { persist: false }]);
  assert.equal(engine.calls[0].self, engine);
  assert.equal(engine.calls[1].self, engine.registry);
  assert.equal(engine.calls[2].self, engine.derivations);
});

test('narrowEnginePort: a synchronous engine throw propagates unchanged (startRun failures are typed errors)', () => {
  const boom = Object.assign(new Error('capacity'), { name: 'ResultCapacityError' });
  const port = narrowEnginePort(stubEngine({ startRun() { throw boom; } }));
  assert.throws(() => port.startRun({}), (e) => e === boom);

test('narrowEnginePort: a missing member throws TypeError naming it', () => {
  for (const name of PORT_METHODS) {
    const engine = stubEngine();
    delete engine[name];
    assert.throws(() => narrowEnginePort(engine), (e) => e instanceof TypeError && e.message.includes(`engine.${name}`), name);
  }
  for (const name of ['summarize', 'groupBy', 'filter']) {
    const engine = stubEngine();
    delete engine.derivations[name];
    assert.throws(() => narrowEnginePort(engine), (e) => e instanceof TypeError && e.message.includes(`derivations.${name}`), name);
  }
  assert.throws(() => narrowEnginePort(stubEngine({ registry: {} })), /registry\.bindingFor/);
  assert.throws(() => narrowEnginePort(stubEngine({ registry: undefined })), /registry\.bindingFor/);
  assert.throws(() => narrowEnginePort(null), TypeError);
  assert.throws(() => narrowEnginePort(undefined), TypeError);
});

test('AC-P20: a Proxy engine that throws on register/unregister/keyOf/invalidateModelPlacement/dispose proves the narrow port never touches them', () => {
  const FORBIDDEN = new Set(['register', 'unregister', 'keyOf', 'notifyPlacementChanged', 'invalidateModelPlacement', 'dispose', 'retryPersist', 'rerun', 'getResultSet', 'saveTest']);
  const touched = [];
  const guard = (target, owner) => new Proxy(target, {
    get(t, prop, receiver) {
      touched.push(`${owner}.${String(prop)}`);
      if (FORBIDDEN.has(prop)) throw new Error(`forbidden access: ${owner}.${String(prop)}`);
      return Reflect.get(t, prop, receiver);
    },
  });
  const engine = stubEngine();
  const raw = guard({ ...engine, derivations: guard(engine.derivations, 'derivations'), registry: guard(engine.registry, 'registry') }, 'engine');
  const port = narrowEnginePort(raw);
  for (const m of PORT_METHODS) port[m]({});
  port.registry.bindingFor('k');
  for (const m of ['summarize', 'groupBy', 'filter']) port.derivations[m]({});
  assert.deepEqual([...new Set(touched)].filter((t) => FORBIDDEN.has(t.split('.')[1])), []);
  assert.deepEqual(new Set(touched.filter((t) => t.startsWith('registry.'))), new Set(['registry.bindingFor']));
  assert.deepEqual(new Set(touched.filter((t) => t.startsWith('derivations.'))), new Set(['derivations.summarize', 'derivations.groupBy', 'derivations.filter']));
});

    assert.equal(port.registry.bindingFor('mA').modelKey, 'mA');
    assert.ok(port.validateTest({}).issues.length > 0);
    assert.equal(port.dispose, undefined);
    assert.equal(port.invalidateModelPlacement, undefined);
    assert.equal(port.registry.register, undefined);
    assert.equal(port.registry.unregister, undefined);
    assert.equal(port.registry.keyOf, undefined);
  } finally {
    await engine.dispose();
  }
});
```

```js
// clashpanel/core/scheduler.js
// The injected timer/yield port (spec 5.2). Every debounce, backoff, timeout and chunked pass in the Panel core goes
// through a Scheduler so tests never depend on wall-clock time. The default is the only place a global timer is read.
/** @typedef {{ now(): number, setTimeout(fn: () => void, ms: number): unknown, clearTimeout(h: unknown): void, yield(): Promise<void> }} Scheduler */

/** @returns {Scheduler} */
export function createDefaultScheduler() {
  return Object.freeze({
    now: () => globalThis.performance.now(),
    setTimeout: (fn, ms) => globalThis.setTimeout(fn, ms),
    clearTimeout: (handle) => globalThis.clearTimeout(handle),
    yield: () => new Promise((resolve) => { globalThis.setTimeout(resolve, 0); }),
  });
}

export function assertScheduler(scheduler) {
  for (const name of ['now', 'setTimeout', 'clearTimeout', 'yield']) {
    if (typeof scheduler?.[name] !== 'function') throw new TypeError(`scheduler.${name} is required`);
  }
  return scheduler;
}
```

```js
// clashpanel/core/generation.js
// One monotonically increasing generation per displayed run (spec 5.2 "Controller generation"). Every asynchronous
// completion captures `current()` when issued and commits only while `isCurrent(captured)` still holds. `onBump` is an
// additive helper so a consumer (the derivation queue) can abort supported work promptly instead of polling.
export function createGeneration() {
  let n = 0;
  const listeners = new Set();
  return Object.freeze({
    current: () => n,
    bump() {
      n += 1;
      for (const listener of [...listeners]) {
        try { listener(n); } catch { /* a listener must never break a bump or its neighbours */ }
      }
      return n;
    },
    isCurrent: (g) => g === n,
    onBump(listener) {
      if (typeof listener !== 'function') throw new TypeError('generation.onBump: listener must be a function');
      listeners.add(listener);
      return () => { listeners.delete(listener); };
    },
  });
}
```

```js
// clashpanel/core/ports.js
// The three host-facing ports of the Panel core (spec 5.2). Nothing here calls Viewer or DOM code; the engine and the
// catalog are injected. Registration is host composition (PD-18): the narrowed engine has NO register/unregister/
// keyOf/invalidateModelPlacement/dispose, so the controller cannot call them (AC-P20).
import { BASIS_VERDICT_TIMEOUT_MS } from './constants.js';
import { assertScheduler } from './scheduler.js';

const ENGINE_METHODS = Object.freeze([
  'validateTest', 'startRun', 'retainResultSet', 'releaseResultSet', 'getPersistenceState', 'getFreshness', 'assessNoClashClaim',
]);
const DERIVATION_METHODS = Object.freeze(['summarize', 'groupBy', 'filter']);

/** Fixed, host-independent reasons for every fail-closed basis outcome (never contain host or error text). */
export const BASIS_FAILURE_REASONS = Object.freeze({
  missing: 'The host did not provide a measurement-basis check.',
  threw: 'The measurement-basis check failed.',
  rejected: 'The measurement-basis check was rejected.',
  timeout: 'The measurement-basis check did not answer in time.',
  malformed: 'The measurement-basis check returned an unrecognized answer.',
});

function need(owner, ownerName, name) {
  if (typeof owner?.[name] !== 'function') throw new TypeError(`narrowEnginePort: ${ownerName}.${name} is required`);
}
const forward = (owner, name) => (...args) => owner[name](...args);

/**
 * EnginePort = { validateTest, startRun, retainResultSet, releaseResultSet, getPersistenceState, getFreshness,
 *                assessNoClashClaim, derivations: { summarize, groupBy, filter }, registry: { bindingFor } }.
 * NOTHING else. Members are looked up lazily on the engine at call time (so a host may swap an implementation), but
 * only the names above are ever read.
 */
export function narrowEnginePort(engine) {
  if (engine === null || (typeof engine !== 'object' && typeof engine !== 'function')) {
    throw new TypeError('narrowEnginePort: engine is required');
  }
  for (const name of ENGINE_METHODS) need(engine, 'engine', name);
  const { derivations, registry } = engine;
  for (const name of DERIVATION_METHODS) need(derivations, 'engine.derivations', name);
  need(registry, 'engine.registry', 'bindingFor');
  return Object.freeze({
    ...Object.fromEntries(ENGINE_METHODS.map((name) => [name, forward(engine, name)])),
    derivations: Object.freeze(Object.fromEntries(DERIVATION_METHODS.map((name) => [name, forward(derivations, name)]))),
    registry: Object.freeze({ bindingFor: forward(registry, 'bindingFor') }),
  });
}

const unverified = (reason) => Object.freeze({ state: 'unverified', reason });

function settleWithTimeout(raw, scheduler, timeoutMs) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    let done = false;
    let handle;
    const finish = (result) => {
      if (done) return;
      done = true;
      if (handle !== undefined) scheduler.clearTimeout(handle);
      resolve(result);
    };
    handle = scheduler.setTimeout(() => finish({ kind: 'timeout' }), timeoutMs);
    Promise.resolve(raw).then((value) => finish({ kind: 'value', value }), () => finish({ kind: 'rejected' }));
  });
}

/** A recognised verdict as a fresh frozen object with ONLY its own fields, or null when the shape is not recognised. */
function normalizeVerdict(v) {
  if (v === null || typeof v !== 'object') return null;
  let state;
  let basisKey;
  let reason;
  try { ({ state, basisKey, reason } = v); } catch { return null; }
  if (state === 'verified') {
    return typeof basisKey === 'string' && basisKey.length > 0 ? Object.freeze({ state, basisKey }) : null;
  }
  if (state === 'unverified' || state === 'incompatible') {
    return typeof reason === 'string' && reason.length > 0 ? Object.freeze({ state, reason }) : null;
  }
  return null;
}

/**
 * BasisVerdict = {state:'verified', basisKey} | {state:'unverified'|'incompatible', reason}. FAIL CLOSED: a missing
 * method, a throw, a rejection, a timeout or any other shape becomes {state:'unverified', reason: <fixed text>}. Never
 * rejects for host behavior. The host's `reason` is returned as a plain string and is never interpreted.
 */
export async function readBasisVerdict(catalog, modelKeys, { scheduler, timeoutMs = BASIS_VERDICT_TIMEOUT_MS } = {}) {
  if (!Array.isArray(modelKeys)) throw new TypeError('readBasisVerdict: modelKeys must be an array');
  assertScheduler(scheduler);
  const wait = Number.isFinite(timeoutMs) && timeoutMs >= 0 ? timeoutMs : BASIS_VERDICT_TIMEOUT_MS;
  try {
    if (typeof catalog?.measurementBasis !== 'function') return unverified(BASIS_FAILURE_REASONS.missing);
    let raw;
    try { raw = catalog.measurementBasis([...modelKeys]); } catch { return unverified(BASIS_FAILURE_REASONS.threw); }
    const settled = await settleWithTimeout(raw, scheduler, wait);
    if (settled.kind === 'timeout') return unverified(BASIS_FAILURE_REASONS.timeout);
    if (settled.kind === 'rejected') return unverified(BASIS_FAILURE_REASONS.rejected);
    return normalizeVerdict(settled.value) ?? unverified(BASIS_FAILURE_REASONS.malformed);
  } catch {
    return unverified(BASIS_FAILURE_REASONS.threw);
  }
}

function assertMembers(target, owner, names, label) {
  for (const name of names) {
    if (typeof target?.[name] !== 'function') throw new TypeError(`${label}: ${owner}.${name} is required`);
  }
  return target;
}

/** Structural check of the host ModelCatalog. `measurementBasis` is optional here: its absence is fail-closed data. */
export function assertCatalogPort(catalog) {
  return assertMembers(catalog, 'catalog', ['list', 'displayNameFor', 'keyOfModel', 'onChange'], 'assertCatalogPort');
}

export function assertBridgePort(bridge) {
  return assertMembers(bridge, 'bridge',
    ['present', 'clear', 'dispose', 'checkIsolationPrerequisite', 'readAggregateSelection', 'onModelLeft'], 'assertBridgePort');
}
```

**Scope note:** these files are support modules (no `test()` calls, not `*.test.mjs`); only `support.test.mjs` is collected. It tests the DOUBLES, because a double with the wrong behavior silently invalidates every later task. Tasks 22-26 (viewer layer) reuse `fakeViewer.mjs` / `fakeThree.mjs` / `createFakeViewerApi` unchanged; if one of them strictly needs a new capability it appends an option with a preserving default (barrel rule 1) and says so in its own Scope note. **Fidelity rules the doubles enforce (all verified against the code, catalog 1):** `engine.startRun` is synchronous and its handle emits only `state`/`unit`/`persistence` events (persistence may follow the terminal event; `done` and `persisted` never reject; `resultSet` may be `null`); residency is strict (`ResultSetRetainedError` while leased, `UnsavedResultSetError` unless `{acknowledgeUnsaved:true}`, non-resident release is a no-op); reading `register/unregister/keyOf/notifyPlacementChanged/invalidateModelPlacement/dispose/...` on the raw fake **throws and is recorded** (AC-P20); the viewer's overlay API is MESH FIRST / scene name second (a non-string name throws), aggregate isolation has the verified full-replace semantics, every theming method throws exactly `theming forbidden` (AC-P19); `THREE.Vector3` has no `setScalar` (r71). The hand-built sealed sets use the REAL result/ledger/provenance shapes (built from `test/clashtest/support/resultSetFixtures.mjs` helpers) and are cross-checked against the REAL `createDerivationContext` (`groupBy`, `filter`, `summarize`), so a fake engine fed by them returns exactly what the real one would for the same set. // fakeScheduler

```js
test('fake scheduler: virtual time only moves in advance(); timers fire oldest first, ties in scheduling order', async () => {
  const s = createFakeScheduler({ start: 100 });
  const fired = [];
  s.setTimeout(() => fired.push('b@20'), 20);
  s.setTimeout(() => fired.push('a@10'), 10);
  s.setTimeout(() => fired.push('c@20'), 20);
  assert.equal(s.now(), 100);
  await s.advance(9);
  assert.deepEqual(fired, []);
  await s.advance(1);
  assert.deepEqual(fired, ['a@10']);
  assert.equal(s.now(), 110);
  await s.advance(10);
  assert.deepEqual(fired, ['a@10', 'b@20', 'c@20']);
  assert.equal(s.pendingTimers(), 0);
});

test('fake scheduler: clearTimeout cancels; delays are recorded; timers scheduled by a fired timer inside the window also fire', async () => {
  const s = createFakeScheduler();
  const fired = [];
  const h = s.setTimeout(() => fired.push('cancelled'), 5);
  s.clearTimeout(h);
  s.setTimeout(() => { fired.push('first'); s.setTimeout(() => fired.push('chained'), 5); }, 5);
  await s.advance(10);
  assert.deepEqual(fired, ['first', 'chained']);
  assert.deepEqual(s.delays, [5, 5, 5]);
  await assert.rejects(s.advance(-1), RangeError);
});

test('fake scheduler: yield() is counted, runs yieldHook(n), and holdYields() blocks until release', async () => {
  const s = createFakeScheduler();
  const seen = [];
  s.yieldHook = (n) => { seen.push(n); };
  await s.yield();
  await s.yield();
  assert.equal(s.yieldCount, 2);
  assert.deepEqual(seen, [1, 2]);
  s.yieldHook = null;
  const hold = s.holdYields();
  let resumed = false;
  const p = s.yield().then(() => { resumed = true; });
  await flush();
  assert.equal(resumed, false);
  hold.release();
  await p;
  assert.equal(resumed, true);
});

test('fake catalog: list() returns fresh copies; mutators change state but only fire() notifies', () => {
  const c = createFakeCatalog({ models: [{ modelKey: 'k1', displayName: 'Arch' }, { modelKey: 'k2', displayName: 'Struct', loaded: false }] });
  let changes = 0;
  const off = c.onChange(() => { changes += 1; });
  const list = c.list();
  assert.deepEqual(list.map((e) => [e.modelKey, e.displayName, e.loaded]), [['k1', 'Arch', true], ['k2', 'Struct', false]]);
  list[0].loaded = false;
  assert.equal(c.list()[0].loaded, true);
  c.setLoaded('k2', true);
  assert.equal(changes, 0);
  c.fire();
  assert.equal(changes, 1);
  assert.equal(c.list()[1].loaded, true);
  off();
  c.fire();
  assert.equal(changes, 1);
  assert.equal(c.listenerCount(), 0);
});

test('fake catalog: display names and model->key mappings OUTLIVE removal; unknown ones answer null', () => {
  const c = createFakeCatalog({ models: [{ modelKey: 'k1', displayName: 'Arch' }] });
  const model = c.modelOf('k1');
  c.removeModel('k1');
  assert.deepEqual(c.list(), []);
  assert.equal(c.displayNameFor('k1'), 'Arch');
  assert.equal(c.keyOfModel(model), 'k1');
  assert.equal(c.displayNameFor('nope'), null);
  assert.equal(c.keyOfModel({}), null);
});

test('fake catalog: addModel with a known key replaces the entry (a reload = new Model object); a null key is an unidentified model', () => {
  const c = createFakeCatalog({ models: [{ modelKey: 'k1', displayName: 'Arch' }] });
  const before = c.modelOf('k1');
  const after = c.addModel({ modelKey: 'k1', displayName: 'Arch v2' });
  assert.notEqual(before, after);
  assert.equal(c.list().length, 1);
  assert.equal(c.list()[0].displayName, 'Arch v2');
  c.addModel({ modelKey: null, displayName: 'Mystery' });
  assert.deepEqual(c.list().map((e) => e.modelKey), ['k1', null]);
  assert.throws(() => c.setLoaded('missing', true), /no model/);
});

test('fake catalog: measurementBasis records a copy of the keys, supports value/function/promise, and can be omitted entirely', async () => {
  const c = createFakeCatalog({ models: [] });
  const keys = ['a', 'b'];
  assert.deepEqual(c.measurementBasis(keys), { state: 'verified', basisKey: 'fake-basis' });
  keys.push('x');
  assert.deepEqual(c.calls.measurementBasis, [['a', 'b']]);
  c.setBasis((ks) => ({ state: 'unverified', reason: `n=${ks.length}` }));
  assert.deepEqual(c.measurementBasis(['a']), { state: 'unverified', reason: 'n=1' });
  c.setBasis(Promise.resolve({ state: 'incompatible', reason: 'r' }));
  assert.deepEqual(await c.measurementBasis(['a']), { state: 'incompatible', reason: 'r' });
  assert.equal('measurementBasis' in createFakeCatalog({ omitMeasurementBasis: true }), false);
});

const sealedFor = (runId) => makeSealedSet({ runId, results: manyResults(2) });

test('fake engine: startRun is synchronous, returns a handle with the real members, and records the call', () => {
  const engine = createFakeEngine();
  const def = { testId: 't', revision: 1 };
  const h = engine.startRun(def, { persist: true });
  for (const m of ['runId', 'getSnapshot', 'subscribe', 'cancel', 'done', 'persisted']) assert.ok(m in h, m);
  assert.equal(h.runId, 'run-1');
  assert.equal(engine.startRun(def).runId, 'run-2');
  assert.deepEqual(engine.calls.startRun[0], { def, opts: { persist: true } });
  assert.equal(engine.lastHandle.runId, 'run-2');
  assert.deepEqual(h.getSnapshot(), { ...h.getSnapshot(), status: 'queued', phase: 'queued', fractionProcessed: null });
});

test('fake engine: events are state/unit/persistence only; listener errors are swallowed; subscribe validates and unsubscribes', () => {
  const h = createFakeEngine().startRun({});
  const seen = [];
  assert.throws(() => h.subscribe('nope'), TypeError);
  const off = h.subscribe((e) => seen.push(e));
  h.subscribe(() => { throw new Error('listener boom'); });
  h.emitState({ status: 'planning', phase: 'enumerating' });
  h.emitUnit({ status: 'running', phase: 'executing' });
  h.emitPersistence({ state: 'saved' });
  assert.deepEqual(seen.map((e) => e.type), ['state', 'unit', 'persistence']);
  assert.deepEqual(seen.map((e) => e.seq), [1, 2, 3]);
  assert.equal(h.getSnapshot().status, 'running');
  assert.equal('status' in seen[2], false);
  off();
  h.emitState({ status: 'running', phase: 'executing' });
  assert.equal(seen.length, 3);
  assert.equal(h.listenerCount(), 1);
});

test('fake engine: finish() emits the terminal state event, resolves done once with resultSet (null allowed), and persisted follows persistence', async () => {
  const engine = createFakeEngine();
  const h = engine.startRun({});
  const events = [];
  h.subscribe((e) => events.push(e));
  const set = sealedFor(h.runId);
  const summary = await h.finish({ status: 'completed', resultSet: set });
  assert.deepEqual(summary, { runId: 'run-1', status: 'completed', resultSet: set, persistence: { state: 'saved', timedOut: false, attempt: 1 } });
  assert.deepEqual(events[0], { type: 'state', seq: 1, status: 'completed', phase: 'terminal', terminal: true, persistence: { state: 'saved', timedOut: false, attempt: 1 } });
  assert.deepEqual(await h.persisted, { state: 'saved' });
  assert.equal(await h.finish({ status: 'failed' }), summary);
  const g = engine.startRun({});
  assert.equal((await g.finish({ status: 'failed' })).resultSet, null);
});

test('fake engine: a pending persistence settles later via finishPersisted, independent of done, and updates getPersistenceState', async () => {
  const engine = createFakeEngine();
  const h = engine.startRun({});
  await h.finish({ resultSet: sealedFor(h.runId), persistence: { state: 'pending', timedOut: true, attempt: 1 } });
  assert.equal(engine.getPersistenceState(h.runId).state, 'pending');
  let settled = false;
  h.persisted.then(() => { settled = true; });
  await flush();
  assert.equal(settled, false);
  h.finishPersisted({ state: 'saved' });
  assert.deepEqual(await h.persisted, { state: 'saved' });
  assert.equal(engine.getPersistenceState(h.runId).state, 'saved');
  const f = engine.startRun({});
  await f.finish({ resultSet: sealedFor(f.runId), persistence: { state: 'failed', error: new Error('disk') } });
  assert.equal((await f.persisted).state, 'failed');
  assert.equal(engine.getPersistenceState(f.runId).state, 'failed');
});

test('fake engine: cancel() records the reason, moves a running run to cancelling, returns done, and can auto-finish', async () => {
  const engine = createFakeEngine();
  const h = engine.startRun({});
  h.emitState({ status: 'running', phase: 'executing' });
  const p = h.cancel('user');
  assert.deepEqual(h.cancelCalls, ['user']);
  assert.equal(h.getSnapshot().status, 'cancelling');
  await h.finish({ status: 'cancelled', resultSet: null, persistence: { state: 'skipped', reason: 'seal-failed' } });
  assert.equal((await p).status, 'cancelled');
  assert.deepEqual(h.cancelCalls, ['user']);
  await h.cancel('after terminal');
  assert.deepEqual(h.cancelCalls, ['user', 'after terminal']);
});

test('fake engine: failNextStartRun throws synchronously once (the typed-error admission failures)', () => {
  const engine = createFakeEngine();
  const err = Object.assign(new Error('capacity'), { name: 'ResultCapacityError' });
  engine.failNextStartRun(err);
  assert.throws(() => engine.startRun({}), (e) => e === err);
  assert.equal(engine.startRun({}).runId, 'run-1');
  assert.equal(engine.calls.startRun.length, 2);
});

test('fake engine: residency is strict like the real engine (lease blocks release, unsaved needs acknowledgement, non-resident is a no-op)', async () => {
  const engine = createFakeEngine();
  const h = engine.startRun({});
  await h.finish({ resultSet: sealedFor(h.runId) });
  const lease = engine.retainResultSet(h.runId);
  assert.throws(() => engine.releaseResultSet(h.runId), ResultSetRetainedError);
  lease.release();
  lease.release();
  assert.equal(engine.leases[0].releaseCalls, 2);
  engine.releaseResultSet(h.runId);
  assert.deepEqual(engine.residentRunIds(), []);
  engine.releaseResultSet('never-existed');
  assert.throws(() => engine.retainResultSet('never-existed'), ResultNotResidentError);
  const u = engine.startRun({});
  await u.finish({ resultSet: sealedFor(u.runId), persistence: { state: 'failed', error: new Error('x') } });
  assert.throws(() => engine.retainResultSet(u.runId), UnsavedResultSetError);
  assert.throws(() => engine.releaseResultSet(u.runId), UnsavedResultSetError);
  engine.releaseResultSet(u.runId, { acknowledgeUnsaved: true });
  assert.deepEqual(engine.residentRunIds(), []);
  engine.failNextRelease(new Error('release boom'));
  assert.throws(() => engine.releaseResultSet('x'), /release boom/);
});

test('fake engine spies: auto mode resolves the default; hold() defers until call.resolve/reject; rejectNext scripts errors', async () => {
  const engine = createFakeEngine();
  assert.deepEqual(await engine.getFreshness('run-1'), { state: 'current', reasons: [] });
  engine.spies.groupBy.setResult((set, facets) => ({ facets, groups: [] }));
  assert.deepEqual(await engine.derivations.groupBy({}, ['element']), { facets: ['element'], groups: [] });
  engine.spies.summarize.hold();
  const p = engine.derivations.summarize({}, { signal: null });
  await flush();
  assert.equal(engine.spies.summarize.pending().length, 1);
  engine.spies.summarize.calls[0].resolve({ totalResults: 7 });
  assert.deepEqual(await p, { totalResults: 7 });
  engine.spies.filter.rejectNext(new DerivationBusyError({ limit: 2 }));
  await assert.rejects(engine.derivations.filter({}, []), (e) => e.name === 'DerivationBusyError');
  assert.deepEqual((await engine.derivations.filter({}, [])).matches, []);
});

test('fake engine spies: an AbortSignal rejects with the real abort error class (derivations vs reads) and an already-aborted signal rejects at once', async () => {
  const engine = createFakeEngine();
  engine.spies.groupBy.hold();
  engine.spies.getFreshness.hold();
  const c1 = new AbortController();
  const c2 = new AbortController();
  const g = engine.derivations.groupBy({}, ['element'], { signal: c1.signal });
  const f = engine.getFreshness('run-1', { signal: c2.signal });
  c1.abort();
  c2.abort();
  await assert.rejects(g, (e) => e instanceof DerivationAbortedError);
  await assert.rejects(f, (e) => e instanceof ReadAbortedError);
  await assert.rejects(engine.derivations.summarize({}, { signal: AbortSignal.abort() }), DerivationAbortedError);
});

test('fake engine: derivationStats tracks in-flight and the maximum concurrency across all three derivations', async () => {
  const engine = createFakeEngine();
  for (const k of ['summarize', 'groupBy', 'filter']) engine.spies[k].hold();
  const ps = [engine.derivations.summarize({}), engine.derivations.groupBy({}, []), engine.derivations.filter({}, [])];
  assert.deepEqual(engine.derivationStats(), { inFlight: 3, maxInFlight: 3, total: 3 });
  for (const k of ['summarize', 'groupBy', 'filter']) engine.spies[k].calls[0].resolve({});
  await Promise.all(ps);
  assert.deepEqual(engine.derivationStats(), { inFlight: 0, maxInFlight: 3, total: 3 });
});

const req = (over = {}) => ({ sides: [{ model: {}, dbId: 1 }], options: { focus: true, isolate: false, marker: true }, ...over });

test('fake bridge: auto mode resolves default outcomes derived from the request options and the prerequisite', async () => {
  const bridge = createFakeBridge();
  assert.deepEqual(await bridge.present(req()), { superseded: false, fitted: true, isolated: false, marked: true, notes: [] });
  assert.equal((await bridge.present(req({ options: { focus: false, isolate: true, marker: false } }))).isolated, true);
  bridge.setPrerequisite({ available: false, reason: 'hidden nodes' });
  assert.equal((await bridge.present(req({ options: { focus: false, isolate: true, marker: false } }))).isolated, false);
  assert.deepEqual(bridge.checkIsolationPrerequisite(), { available: false, reason: 'hidden nodes' });
  assert.deepEqual(await bridge.clear(), { isolation: 'none', markersRemoved: 0, notes: [] });
  assert.equal(bridge.calls.present.length, 3);
});

test('fake bridge: holdAll() defers every call so a test can resolve interleavings; failNext rejects', async () => {
  const bridge = createFakeBridge().holdAll();
  const p1 = bridge.present(req());
  const p2 = bridge.present(req());
  const c = bridge.clear();
  await flush();
  assert.equal(bridge.pending('present').length, 2);
  bridge.calls.present[1].resolve({ superseded: false, fitted: true, isolated: false, marked: true, notes: [] });
  bridge.calls.present[0].resolve({ superseded: true, fitted: false, isolated: false, marked: false, notes: [] });
  bridge.calls.clear[0].resolve();
  assert.equal((await p1).superseded, true);
  assert.equal((await p2).superseded, false);
  assert.equal((await c).isolation, 'none');
  bridge.autoAll();
  bridge.failNext('present', new Error('viewer refused'));
  await assert.rejects(bridge.present(req()), /viewer refused/);
});

test('fake bridge: dispose() is idempotent; every later call is a recorded non-mutating no-op returning disposed', async () => {
  const bridge = createFakeBridge();
  let left = 0;
  bridge.onModelLeft(() => { left += 1; });
  await bridge.dispose();
  await bridge.dispose();
  assert.equal(bridge.disposed, true);
  assert.equal(bridge.calls.dispose.length, 1);
  assert.equal((await bridge.present(req())).disposed, true);
  assert.equal((await bridge.clear()).disposed, true);
  assert.equal(bridge.calls.present.length, 0);

});
```
