```js
// clashpanel/core/draft.js
// The setup form as pure data, and its mapping to a Core ClashTestDefinition (spec 6.1, PD-8, OD-9). Nothing here reads a
// clock, an id source or a global: the controller mints ids and decides when to adopt the draft `prepareRun` returns.
const MAX_NAME = 256;                                   // Core schema bound for `name` (1-256), not an option default
const DECIMAL = /^[+-]?(?:\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?$/;
const SIDE_KEY = Object.freeze({ A: 'setA', B: 'setB' });
const CONTROL_LABEL = Object.freeze({ setA: 'Set A', setB: 'Set B' });

const emptySide = () => ({ modelKeys: [], elements: {} });
const uniqueSorted = (xs) => [...new Set(xs)].sort();
function normalizeIds(ids) {
  const out = new Set();
  for (const id of ids) {
    if (typeof id === 'number' && Number.isSafeInteger(id) && id >= 0) out.add(id === 0 ? 0 : id);   // -0 -> 0, matching Core
  }
  return [...out].sort((a, b) => a - b);
}

// Own-property definition (never assignment): a model key such as "__proto__" must stay data, not become a prototype.
const putOwn = (target, key, value) => Object.defineProperty(target, key, { value, enumerable: true, writable: true, configurable: true });

function freezeSide(side) {
  if (Object.isFrozen(side)) return side;          // produced by an earlier freezeDraft: reuse, no O(n) recopy per keystroke
  const elements = {};
  for (const [k, ids] of Object.entries(side.elements)) putOwn(elements, k, Object.freeze([...ids]));
  return Object.freeze({ modelKeys: Object.freeze([...side.modelKeys]), elements: Object.freeze(elements) });
}
function freezeDraft(d) {
  return Object.freeze({
    ...d, setA: freezeSide(d.setA), setB: freezeSide(d.setB),
    lastRun: d.lastRun === null || Object.isFrozen(d.lastRun) ? d.lastRun : Object.freeze({ ...d.lastRun }),
  });
}

export function createDraft({ testId, testNumber = 1 } = {}) {
  if (typeof testId !== 'string' || testId.length === 0) throw new TypeError('createDraft: testId must be a non-empty string');
  return freezeDraft({
    testId, revision: 1, name: `Clash test ${testNumber}`, mode: 'hard', clearance: '', selfClash: false,
    setA: emptySide(), setB: emptySide(), lastRun: null, testCounter: testNumber,
  });
}

function normalizeElements(elements) {
  const out = {};
  for (const key of Object.keys(elements).sort()) {
    const ids = Array.isArray(elements[key]) ? normalizeIds(elements[key]) : [];
    if (ids.length > 0) putOwn(out, key, ids);
  }
  return out;
}

const sameJson = (a, b) => JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b);

/** Pure reducer. An invalid or no-op action returns the SAME draft object (identity), so callers can skip notifying. */
export function draftReduce(draft, action) {
  const set = (patch) => freezeDraft({ ...draft, ...patch });
  switch (action?.type) {
    case 'name':
      return typeof action.value === 'string' && action.value !== draft.name ? set({ name: action.value }) : draft;
    case 'mode':
      return (action.value === 'hard' || action.value === 'soft') && action.value !== draft.mode ? set({ mode: action.value }) : draft;
    case 'clearance':
      return typeof action.value === 'string' && action.value !== draft.clearance ? set({ clearance: action.value }) : draft;
    case 'selfClash':
      return typeof action.value === 'boolean' && action.value !== draft.selfClash ? set({ selfClash: action.value }) : draft;
    case 'toggleModel': {
      const key = SIDE_KEY[action.side];
      if (key === undefined || typeof action.modelKey !== 'string' || action.modelKey.length === 0) return draft;
      const side = draft[key];
      const modelKeys = side.modelKeys.includes(action.modelKey)
        ? side.modelKeys.filter((k) => k !== action.modelKey) : uniqueSorted([...side.modelKeys, action.modelKey]);
      return set({ [key]: { ...side, modelKeys } });
    }
    case 'setElements': {
      const key = SIDE_KEY[action.side];
      if (key === undefined || action.elements === null || typeof action.elements !== 'object' || Array.isArray(action.elements)) return draft;
      const elements = normalizeElements(action.elements);
      return sameJson(elements, draft[key].elements) ? draft : set({ [key]: { ...draft[key], elements } });
    }
    case 'newTest':
      return typeof action.testId === 'string' && action.testId.length > 0
        ? createDraft({ testId: action.testId, testNumber: draft.testCounter + 1 }) : draft;
    default:
      return draft;
  }
}

/** One entry per model key: `{kind:'model'}` wins over `{kind:'elements'}` for the same model; sorted by modelKey. */
export function selectionEntriesOf(side) {
  const models = new Set(side.modelKeys);
  const keys = new Set(models);
  for (const [k, ids] of Object.entries(side.elements)) if (normalizeIds(ids).length > 0) keys.add(k);
  return [...keys].sort().map((modelKey) => (models.has(modelKey)
    ? { kind: 'model', modelKey }
    : { kind: 'elements', modelKey, dbIds: normalizeIds(side.elements[modelKey]) }));
}

function parseClearance(text) {
  const t = text.trim();
  if (t === '') return { code: 'clearance-required', text: 'Enter a clearance for Soft mode.' };
  const n = DECIMAL.test(t) ? Number(t) : NaN;
  if (!Number.isFinite(n)) return { code: 'clearance-invalid', text: 'Clearance must be a number.' };
  if (!(n > 0)) return { code: 'clearance-not-positive', text: 'Clearance must be greater than zero.' };
  return { value: n };
}

function deepFreeze(value) {
  if (value !== null && typeof value === 'object' && !Object.isFrozen(value)) {
    Object.freeze(value);
    for (const k of Object.keys(value)) deepFreeze(value[k]);
  }
  return value;
}

export function buildDefinition(draft) {
  const problems = [];
  const name = draft.name.trim();
  if (name.length === 0) problems.push({ control: 'name', code: 'name-required', text: 'Enter a name for this test.' });
  else if (name.length > MAX_NAME) problems.push({ control: 'name', code: 'name-too-long', text: `Test name must be ${MAX_NAME} characters or fewer.` });
  const soft = draft.mode === 'soft';
  let clearance;
  if (soft) {
    const parsed = parseClearance(draft.clearance);
    if (parsed.value === undefined) problems.push({ control: 'clearance', code: parsed.code, text: parsed.text });
    else clearance = parsed.value;
  }
  const entriesA = selectionEntriesOf(draft.setA);
  const entriesB = draft.selfClash ? entriesA : selectionEntriesOf(draft.setB);
  if (entriesA.length === 0) problems.push({ control: 'setA', code: 'selection-empty', text: `${CONTROL_LABEL.setA} is empty — choose a model or use the current selection.` });
  if (!draft.selfClash && entriesB.length === 0) problems.push({ control: 'setB', code: 'selection-empty', text: `${CONTROL_LABEL.setB} is empty — choose a model or use the current selection.` });
  if (problems.length > 0) return { definition: null, problems };
  const copy = (entries) => ({ entries: entries.map((e) => ({ ...e, ...(e.dbIds ? { dbIds: [...e.dbIds] } : {}) })) });
  const definition = {
    schemaVersion: 1, testId: draft.testId, revision: draft.revision, name,
    selectionA: copy(entriesA), selectionB: copy(entriesB), mode: soft ? 'clearance' : 'volume-overlap',
    ...(soft ? { clearance } : {}),
  };
  return { definition: deepFreeze(definition), problems: [] };
}

function canonical(value) {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(canonical);
  if (value !== null && typeof value === 'object') return Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(value).sort().map((k) => [k, canonical(value[k])]));
  return value;
}
function canonicalSelection(selection) {
  if (!Array.isArray(selection?.entries)) return canonical(selection);
  const entries = selection.entries.map((e) => (Array.isArray(e.dbIds) ? { ...e, dbIds: normalizeIds(e.dbIds) } : { ...e }));
  entries.sort((a, b) => (a.modelKey < b.modelKey ? -1 : a.modelKey > b.modelKey ? 1 : (a.kind < b.kind ? -1 : a.kind > b.kind ? 1 : 0)));
  return canonical({ ...selection, entries });
}

/** Canonical compare key over ALL definition fields including `name`, excluding `revision` (spec 6.1). */
export function definitionKey(definition) {
  const { revision, selectionA, selectionB, ...rest } = definition;
  void revision;
  return JSON.stringify(canonical({ ...rest, selectionA: canonicalSelection(selectionA), selectionB: canonicalSelection(selectionB) }));
}

/**
 * Spec 6.1 "Draft identity lifecycle": the revision is bumped ONLY when the normalized definition (name included)
 * differs from the previous RUN's; it is monotone and never reused (edit-and-revert bumps again but yields the same
 * definitionKey). Pure: the caller adopts the returned draft after startRun returned a handle.
 */
export function prepareRun(draft) {
  const first = buildDefinition(draft);
  if (first.definition === null) return { draft, definition: null, problems: first.problems };
  const key = definitionKey(first.definition);
  const bump = draft.lastRun !== null && draft.lastRun.definitionKey !== key;
  const revision = bump ? draft.revision + 1 : draft.revision;
  const next = freezeDraft({ ...draft, revision, lastRun: { definitionKey: key, revision } });
  return { draft: next, definition: bump ? buildDefinition(next).definition : first.definition, problems: [] };
}
```

### Task 5: Setup validation (issue-path mapping and advisory pre-checks)

**Tier:** [A] format-agnostic headless

**Files:**
- Create: `clashpanel/core/setupValidation.js`
- Modify: `test/clashpanel/scaffold.test.mjs` (`EXPECTED_MODULES` gains `core/setupValidation.js`)
- Test: `test/clashpanel/core/setupValidation.test.mjs`

**Scope note:** `validateSetup` is the single place that decides "Run is allowed" for the Setup region (spec 6.2). Order: (1) the Panel's own `buildDefinition` problems, (2) `engine.validateTest` issues, authoritative and only run when a definition could be built, each mapped to a control by its RFC 6901 path, (3) advisory pre-checks per participating model (registered, bound, NOT STALE, loaded), (4) the Soft-availability finding. Every finding blocks Run. The Core `message` is inserted as TEXT after a control-level prefix (`"Set A: <message>"`), never interpreted; hostile text is a test case. Registration is READ-ONLY (PD-18/AC-P20): the only registry member touched is `registry.bindingFor`, and `catalog.measurementBasis` is NOT called here (Task 6 evaluates Soft availability; the result is passed in). No numeric pre-check against any engine limit is made (spec 5.2): `too-many-elements` etc. come only from `validateTest`. A model yields at most ONE finding (order: not registered, then `binding-stale`, then still loading). Staleness (spec 6.2/11) is object identity: `binding.model !== catalogEntry.model` in either direction (catalog already has the reloaded Model while the registry binds the old one, or the reverse); the Panel only reads `bindingFor(...)` and never repairs it, the host re-registers and the catalog's `onChange` re-runs validation, and in a self-clash only Set A's models are checked and Set B issues are folded into Set A (Set B is hidden and identical).

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `buildDefinition(draft)`, `selectionEntriesOf(side)` (Task 4); `SOFT_UNAVAILABLE_TEXT` (Task 1); an `EnginePort` subset `{ validateTest(def) -> {issues:[{path,code,message}], issuesTruncated}, registry: { bindingFor(modelKey) -> binding|null } }` (Task 2; real: `clashtest/engine.js` `validateTest`, `registry.bindingFor`); a `ModelCatalog` `{ list() -> [{modelKey|null, displayName, model, loaded}], displayNameFor(key) -> string|null }` (spec 5.2); `softAvailability = { available: boolean, explanation: string|null, pending?: boolean }` (Task 6 output shape).
- Produces (`clashpanel/core/setupValidation.js`):
  - `controlForIssuePath(path: string): { control: 'name'|'mode'|'clearance'|'setA'|'setB'|'general' }`.
  - `participatingModelKeys(draft): string[]` (sorted union of both sides' model keys; Set A only for a self-clash).
  - `validateSetup({ draft, engine, catalog, softAvailability }): SetupValidation` with `SetupValidation = { state: 'ready'|'blocked', findings: [{ control: string, code: string, text: string }], issuesTruncated: boolean, definition: object|null }` (`definition` is non-null only when `state === 'ready'`). Panel-owned finding codes: `model-not-registered`, `binding-stale`, `model-loading`, `soft-unavailable`, `soft-checking`, `validation-unavailable` (plus the Task 4 problem codes and Core's issue codes verbatim).

**Depends on:** Tasks 1, 2, 3 (fakes in tests), 4.

```js
// clashpanel/core/setupValidation.js
// Region 1 validation (spec 6.2): Panel problems -> engine.validateTest issues (authoritative, mapped by RFC 6901 path)
// -> advisory pre-checks (registered, bound, loaded) -> Soft availability. Registration is READ-ONLY (PD-18): only
// `registry.bindingFor` is called. Nothing here checks a numeric engine limit (spec 5.2).
import { SOFT_UNAVAILABLE_TEXT } from './constants.js';
import { buildDefinition, selectionEntriesOf } from './draft.js';

const LABEL = Object.freeze({
  name: 'Test name', mode: 'Mode', clearance: 'Clearance', setA: 'Set A', setB: 'Set B', general: 'Test definition',
});
const HEAD_TO_CONTROL = Object.freeze({
  name: 'name', mode: 'mode', clearance: 'clearance', selectionA: 'setA', selectionB: 'setB',
});

/** '/clearance' -> clearance, '/selectionA/...' -> setA, '/selectionB/...' -> setB, '/name' -> name, '/mode' -> mode, else general. */
export function controlForIssuePath(path) {
  if (typeof path !== 'string' || !path.startsWith('/')) return { control: 'general' };
  const head = path.split('/')[1];
  return { control: Object.hasOwn(HEAD_TO_CONTROL, head) ? HEAD_TO_CONTROL[head] : 'general' };
}

export function participatingModelKeys(draft) {
  const keys = selectionEntriesOf(draft.setA).map((e) => e.modelKey);
  if (!draft.selfClash) keys.push(...selectionEntriesOf(draft.setB).map((e) => e.modelKey));
  return [...new Set(keys)].sort();
}

const asText = (v) => (typeof v === 'string' ? v : '');

function coreFindings(issues, selfClash) {
  const out = [];
  const seen = new Set();
  for (const raw of issues) {
    const path = typeof raw?.path === 'string' ? raw.path : '';
    let { control } = controlForIssuePath(path);
    if (selfClash && control === 'setB') control = 'setA';        // Set B is hidden and identical in a self-clash
    const code = typeof raw?.code === 'string' && raw.code.length > 0 ? raw.code : 'unknown';
    const message = asText(raw?.message);
    const text = message.length > 0 ? `${LABEL[control]}: ${message}` : `${LABEL[control]} is not valid.`;
    const id = `${control}\u0000${code}\u0000${text}`;
    if (seen.has(id)) continue;
    seen.add(id);
    out.push({ control, code, text });
  }
  return out;
}

function nameOf(catalog, key) {
  try {
    const name = catalog.displayNameFor(key);
    return typeof name === 'string' && name.length > 0 ? name : key;
  } catch { return key; }
}

function modelFindings({ draft, engine, catalog }) {
  let list;
  try { list = catalog.list(); } catch { list = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(list)) list = [];
  const sideA = new Set(selectionEntriesOf(draft.setA).map((e) => e.modelKey));
  const out = [];
  for (const key of participatingModelKeys(draft)) {
    const entry = list.find((e) => e && e.modelKey === key);
    let binding = null;
    try { binding = engine.registry.bindingFor(key); } catch { binding = null; }
    const control = sideA.has(key) ? 'setA' : 'setB';
    if (!entry || binding === null || binding === undefined) {
      out.push({ control, code: 'model-not-registered', text: `Model ${nameOf(catalog, key)} is not registered.` });
    } else if (binding.model !== entry.model) {
      // stale in either direction: the catalog and the registry disagree on WHICH Model object this key names
      // (a reload the host has not re-registered yet, or a registry ahead of the catalog). Never repaired here (PD-18).
      out.push({ control, code: 'binding-stale', text: `Model ${nameOf(catalog, key)} was reloaded and is not registered yet.` });
    } else if (entry.loaded !== true) {
      out.push({ control, code: 'model-loading', text: `Model ${nameOf(catalog, key)} is still loading.` });
    }
  }
  return out;
}

function softFinding(draft, softAvailability) {
  if (draft.mode !== 'soft' || participatingModelKeys(draft).length === 0) return [];
  if (softAvailability && softAvailability.available === true) return [];
  if (softAvailability && softAvailability.pending === true) {
    return [{ control: 'mode', code: 'soft-checking', text: 'Checking whether Soft (clearance) is available…' }];
  }
  const text = typeof softAvailability?.explanation === 'string' && softAvailability.explanation.length > 0
    ? softAvailability.explanation : SOFT_UNAVAILABLE_TEXT;
  return [{ control: 'mode', code: 'soft-unavailable', text }];
}

export function validateSetup({ draft, engine, catalog, softAvailability }) {
  const built = buildDefinition(draft);
  const findings = built.problems.map(({ control, code, text }) => ({ control, code, text }));
  let issuesTruncated = false;
  if (built.definition !== null) {
    let result = null;
    try { result = engine.validateTest(built.definition); } catch { result = null; }
    if (result === null || typeof result !== 'object' || !Array.isArray(result.issues)) {
      findings.push({ control: 'general', code: 'validation-unavailable', text: 'The clash engine could not validate this test.' });
    } else {
      issuesTruncated = Boolean(result.issuesTruncated);
      findings.push(...coreFindings(result.issues, draft.selfClash));
    }
  }
  findings.push(...modelFindings({ draft, engine, catalog }), ...softFinding(draft, softAvailability));
  const ready = findings.length === 0;
  return { state: ready ? 'ready' : 'blocked', findings, issuesTruncated, definition: ready ? built.definition : null };
}
```

### Task 6: Soft availability (fail-closed common measurement basis)

**Tier:** [A] format-agnostic headless

**Files:**
- Create: `clashpanel/core/softAvailability.js`
- Modify: `test/clashpanel/scaffold.test.mjs` (`EXPECTED_MODULES` gains `core/softAvailability.js`)
- Test: `test/clashpanel/core/softAvailability.test.mjs`

**Scope note:** PD-17/AC-P18. Soft (clearance) compares one raw threshold with raw world-space distances, so it is meaningful only when every participating model shares a **verified** common measurement basis. The rule is exactly: available iff |P| = 1 (a single model has nothing to compare, and the catalog is **not consulted**) or the host's `measurementBasis(P)` verdict is `verified`; anything else (unverified, incompatible, missing method, throw, rejection, timeout, malformed) is unavailable with the fixed sentence `SOFT_UNAVAILABLE_TEXT` followed by the verdict's `reason` as PLAIN text (never markup, never rewritten, never described as "approximate"). `P = 0` (nothing selected) is "not available, no explanation": the empty selection is reported by Set validation instead. **Display units never enter this decision** (OD-13): a catalog that offers `unitLabel`/`getUnitScale` is ignored, pinned by a negative control that counts the calls. Hard is unaffected by construction: this module is only about Soft, and `validateSetup` (Task 5) ignores Soft availability for a Hard draft; the last test composes both to pin AC-P18 end to end. Evaluating on every participant change (not only in Soft mode) so the UI can disable the Soft segment is the controller's job (Task 16).

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `readBasisVerdict(catalog, modelKeys, { scheduler, timeoutMs }): Promise<BasisVerdict>` and `BASIS_FAILURE_REASONS` (Task 2); `SOFT_UNAVAILABLE_TEXT`, `BASIS_VERDICT_TIMEOUT_MS` (Task 1); in tests `createFakeScheduler`, `createFakeCatalog` (Task 3), `validateSetup` (Task 5), `createDraft/draftReduce` (Task 4).
- Produces (`clashpanel/core/softAvailability.js`): `evaluateSoftAvailability({ participants: string[], catalog, scheduler, timeoutMs = BASIS_VERDICT_TIMEOUT_MS }): Promise<{ available: boolean, verdict: BasisVerdict|null, explanation: string|null }>` (frozen result; `participants` de-duplicated and sorted before use; rejects `TypeError` only for a non-array/non-string `participants`, never for host behavior).

**Depends on:** Tasks 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (the composition test).

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

```js
// clashpanel/core/softAvailability.js
// Spec 6.2 step 4 / PD-17: Soft is available iff |P| = 1 or the host's measurement-basis verdict is `verified`;
// otherwise it is unavailable with a FIXED explanation plus the verdict reason as plain text. Display units are never
// consulted (a label or a conversion cannot make an unverified basis valid, OD-13).
import { BASIS_VERDICT_TIMEOUT_MS, SOFT_UNAVAILABLE_TEXT } from './constants.js';
import { readBasisVerdict } from './ports.js';

export async function evaluateSoftAvailability({ participants, catalog, scheduler, timeoutMs = BASIS_VERDICT_TIMEOUT_MS } = {}) {
  if (!Array.isArray(participants) || !participants.every((k) => typeof k === 'string')) {
    throw new TypeError('evaluateSoftAvailability: participants must be an array of model keys');
  }
  const keys = [...new Set(participants)].sort();
  if (keys.length === 0) return Object.freeze({ available: false, verdict: null, explanation: null });
  if (keys.length === 1) return Object.freeze({ available: true, verdict: null, explanation: null });
  const verdict = await readBasisVerdict(catalog, keys, { scheduler, timeoutMs });
  if (verdict.state === 'verified') return Object.freeze({ available: true, verdict, explanation: null });
  const reason = typeof verdict.reason === 'string' ? verdict.reason : '';
  return Object.freeze({ available: false, verdict, explanation: reason.length > 0 ? `${SOFT_UNAVAILABLE_TEXT} ${reason}` : SOFT_UNAVAILABLE_TEXT });
}
```

### Task 7: Derivation queue (single-flight, priority, busy retry, generation supersession)

**Tier:** [A] format-agnostic headless

**Files:**
- Create: `clashpanel/core/derivationQueue.js`
- Modify: `test/clashpanel/scaffold.test.mjs` (`EXPECTED_MODULES` gains `core/derivationQueue.js`)
- Test: `test/clashpanel/core/derivationQueue.test.mjs`

**Scope note:** the engine allows at most two concurrent derivations per engine and rejects the excess immediately with `DerivationBusyError` (frozen-Core fact; effective limit unreadable, spec 5.2). The controller therefore runs every Core derivation (`summarize`, the `caveated` mask, `groupBy`) through ONE queue: one job in flight, lowest `priority` first (FIFO on ties), each job given a real `AbortSignal`. **Semantics (all pinned below):** (1) a job starts in a microtask after `submit` so same-tick submissions are ordered by priority, not arrival; (2) a generation bump (via `generation.onBump`, and defensively by `isCurrent` at submit/pump/settle) aborts the running job's signal, drops queued jobs, and resolves them `{status:'superseded'}` **immediately**; a job that ignores the abort still ends `superseded` (its late value is dropped); (3) the slot stays occupied until an aborted job actually settles, so at most one job is ever in flight (a job that never settles would stall later generations: recorded as a Review-Focus item, a Core derivation aborts promptly by contract); (4) `DerivationBusyError` (detected by `error.name`, no class import) retries the SAME job after `DERIVATION_BUSY_RETRY_MS` through the injected scheduler up to `DERIVATION_BUSY_MAX_RETRIES` times, then `{status:'error'}`; a bump during the backoff cancels the timer; (5) identical `(generation, key)` submissions share ONE promise and one successful computation (a completed `ok` is served from cache; an `error` is forgotten so a resubmit retries); stale-generation cache entries are pruned (superseded results are not retained); (6) any other rejection or a synchronous throw is `{status:'error', error}`. `generation.onBump` is the additive helper introduced in Task 2.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `DERIVATION_BUSY_RETRY_MS`, `DERIVATION_BUSY_MAX_RETRIES` (Task 1); `assertScheduler` (Task 2); a `generation` with `current()`, `isCurrent(g)` and (optionally) `onBump(cb) -> unsubscribe` (Task 2 `createGeneration`); a `Scheduler` (`setTimeout`, `clearTimeout`) (Task 2/3). Tests use `createGeneration`, `createFakeScheduler`, `createDeferred`, `flush`, and the real `DerivationBusyError` / `DerivationAbortedError` from `clashtest/index.js`.
- Produces (`clashpanel/core/derivationQueue.js`): `createDerivationQueue({ scheduler, generation }): DerivationQueue` (frozen) with
  - `submit({ key: string, priority: number, job: (signal: AbortSignal) => any }): Promise<{ status: 'ok', value } | { status: 'superseded' } | { status: 'error', error }>` (never rejects; `TypeError` thrown synchronously for a malformed argument),
  - `dispose(): void` (idempotent; aborts everything; later submits resolve `superseded`),
  - `stats(): { pending: number, running: boolean, cached: number }` (diagnostic, used by tests).

**Depends on:** Tasks 1, 2, 3.

// test/clashpanel/core/derivationQueue.test.mjs
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { createDerivationQueue } from '../../../clashpanel/core/derivationQueue.js';
import { createGeneration } from '../../../clashpanel/core/generation.js';
import { DERIVATION_BUSY_MAX_RETRIES, DERIVATION_BUSY_RETRY_MS } from '../../../clashpanel/core/constants.js';
import { DerivationAbortedError, DerivationBusyError } from '../../../clashtest/index.js';
import { createDeferred, createFakeScheduler, flush } from '../support/index.mjs';

function setup() {
  const scheduler = createFakeScheduler();
  const generation = createGeneration();
  const queue = createDerivationQueue({ scheduler, generation });
  const log = [];
  let inFlight = 0;
  let maxInFlight = 0;
  /** A deferred job: records start order, its AbortSignal, and the maximum concurrency ever observed. */
  const job = (name) => {
    const d = createDeferred();
    const j = {
      name, calls: 0, signal: null, d,
      run(signal) {
        j.calls += 1; j.signal = signal; log.push(`start:${name}`);
        inFlight += 1; maxInFlight = Math.max(maxInFlight, inFlight);
        return d.promise.finally(() => { inFlight -= 1; });
      },
    };
    return j;
  };
  return { scheduler, generation, queue, log, job, maxInFlight: () => maxInFlight };
}
const submit = (queue, j, priority = 0, key = j.name) => queue.submit({ key, priority, job: j.run });
const busy = () => new DerivationBusyError({ limit: 2 });

test('single flight: jobs run one at a time, in submission order for equal priority, and resolve ok with their values', async () => {
  const { queue, log, job, maxInFlight } = setup();
  const [a, b, c] = [job('a'), job('b'), job('c')];
  const ps = [submit(queue, a), submit(queue, b), submit(queue, c)];
  await flush();
  assert.deepEqual(log, ['start:a']);
  a.d.resolve(1);
  await flush();
  assert.deepEqual(log, ['start:a', 'start:b']);
  b.d.resolve(2);
  await flush();
  c.d.resolve(3);
  assert.deepEqual(await Promise.all(ps), [{ status: 'ok', value: 1 }, { status: 'ok', value: 2 }, { status: 'ok', value: 3 }]);
  assert.equal(maxInFlight(), 1);
  assert.deepEqual(queue.stats(), { pending: 0, running: false, cached: 3 });
});

test('priority: lower number first, FIFO on ties, including jobs submitted in the SAME tick', async () => {
  const s = setup();
  const [low, high] = [s.job('low'), s.job('high')];
  const p1 = submit(s.queue, low, 5);
  const p2 = submit(s.queue, high, 1);
  await flush();
  assert.deepEqual(s.log, ['start:high']);
  high.d.resolve('h');
  await flush();
  low.d.resolve('l');
  await Promise.all([p1, p2]);

  const t = setup();
  const blocker = t.job('blocker');
  const rest = [t.job('low'), t.job('high'), t.job('mid1'), t.job('mid2')];
  const pb = submit(t.queue, blocker, 0);
  await flush();
  const prios = { low: 5, high: 1, mid1: 3, mid2: 3 };
  const ps = rest.map((j) => submit(t.queue, j, prios[j.name]));
  blocker.d.resolve(0);
  for (const j of ['high', 'mid1', 'mid2', 'low']) {
    await flush();
    rest.find((x) => x.name === j).d.resolve(j);
  }
  await Promise.all([pb, ...ps]);
  assert.deepEqual(t.log, ['start:blocker', 'start:high', 'start:mid1', 'start:mid2', 'start:low']);
});

test('a duplicate submit of a queued key shares the promise and can only RAISE its priority', async () => {
  const s = setup();
  const [blocker, x, y] = [s.job('blocker'), s.job('x'), s.job('y')];
  const pb = submit(s.queue, blocker);
  await flush();
  const px = submit(s.queue, x, 9);
  const py = submit(s.queue, y, 5);
  assert.equal(submit(s.queue, x, 0), px);
  assert.equal(submit(s.queue, x, 99), px);
  blocker.d.resolve(0);
  await flush();
  assert.deepEqual(s.log, ['start:blocker', 'start:x']);
  x.d.resolve(0);
  await flush();
  y.d.resolve(0);
  await Promise.all([pb, px, py]);
});

test('generation bump aborts the RUNNING job (real AbortSignal), drops queued jobs unstarted, and resolves both superseded at once', async () => {
  const s = setup();
  const [running, queued] = [s.job('running'), s.job('queued')];
  const p1 = submit(s.queue, running);
  const p2 = submit(s.queue, queued);
  await flush();
  assert.equal(running.signal.aborted, false);
  s.generation.bump();
  assert.equal(running.signal.aborted, true);
  assert.deepEqual(await p1, { status: 'superseded' });
  assert.deepEqual(await p2, { status: 'superseded' });
  assert.equal(queued.calls, 0);
  assert.equal(s.queue.stats().pending, 0);
  assert.equal(s.queue.stats().cached, 0);
  running.d.reject(new DerivationAbortedError());
  await flush();
});

test('a job that ignores the abort and later resolves (or rejects) still yields superseded: its result is dropped', async () => {
  const s = setup();
  const ok = s.job('ok');
  const p = submit(s.queue, ok);
  await flush();
  s.generation.bump();
  ok.d.resolve('late value');
  assert.deepEqual(await p, { status: 'superseded' });
  const bad = s.job('bad');
  const q = submit(s.queue, bad);
  await flush();
  s.generation.bump();
  bad.d.reject(new Error('late failure'));
  assert.deepEqual(await q, { status: 'superseded' });
});

test('the slot stays occupied until an aborted job settles: a new-generation job waits, and at most one job is ever in flight', async () => {
  const s = setup();
  const zombie = s.job('zombie');
  const next = s.job('next');
  const pz = submit(s.queue, zombie);
  await flush();
  s.generation.bump();
  assert.deepEqual(await pz, { status: 'superseded' });
  const pn = submit(s.queue, next);
  await flush();
  assert.equal(next.calls, 0);
  assert.equal(s.queue.stats().running, true);
  zombie.d.resolve('ignored abort');
  await flush();
  assert.equal(next.calls, 1);
  next.d.resolve('fresh');
  assert.deepEqual(await pn, { status: 'ok', value: 'fresh' });
  assert.equal(s.maxInFlight(), 1);
});

test('DerivationBusyError: the same job is retried after the configured backoff through the scheduler, then succeeds (one successful computation)', async () => {
  const s = setup();
  let attempts = 0;
  const p = s.queue.submit({
    key: 'g', priority: 0,
    job: () => { attempts += 1; if (attempts <= 3) throw busy(); return Promise.resolve('finally'); },
  });
  await flush();
  assert.equal(attempts, 1);
  for (let i = 1; i <= 3; i += 1) {
    assert.equal(s.scheduler.pendingTimers(), 1);
    await s.scheduler.advance(DERIVATION_BUSY_RETRY_MS - 1);
    assert.equal(attempts, i);
    await s.scheduler.advance(1);
    assert.equal(attempts, i + 1);
  }
  assert.deepEqual(await p, { status: 'ok', value: 'finally' });
  assert.deepEqual(s.scheduler.delays, [DERIVATION_BUSY_RETRY_MS, DERIVATION_BUSY_RETRY_MS, DERIVATION_BUSY_RETRY_MS]);
});

test('busy retries are bounded: 1 + DERIVATION_BUSY_MAX_RETRIES attempts, then {status:"error"} carrying the busy error; detection is by error.name', async () => {
  const s = setup();
  let attempts = 0;
  const plain = Object.assign(new Error('busy'), { name: 'DerivationBusyError' });
  const p = s.queue.submit({ key: 'g', priority: 0, job: () => { attempts += 1; return Promise.reject(plain); } });
  for (let i = 0; i < DERIVATION_BUSY_MAX_RETRIES + 1; i += 1) await s.scheduler.advance(DERIVATION_BUSY_RETRY_MS);
  const r = await p;
  assert.equal(attempts, 1 + DERIVATION_BUSY_MAX_RETRIES);
  assert.equal(r.status, 'error');
  assert.equal(r.error, plain);
  assert.equal(s.scheduler.pendingTimers(), 0);
});

test('a non-busy failure is NOT retried; a synchronous throw and a plain rejection both become {status:"error"} with the same error object', async () => {
  const s = setup();
  const boom = new Error('boom');
  let calls = 0;
  const r1 = await s.queue.submit({ key: 'throws', priority: 0, job: () => { calls += 1; throw boom; } });
  const r2 = await s.queue.submit({ key: 'rejects', priority: 0, job: () => { calls += 1; return Promise.reject(boom); } });
  assert.deepEqual([r1.status, r1.error === boom, r2.status, r2.error === boom, calls], ['error', true, 'error', true, 2]);
  assert.equal(s.scheduler.delays.length, 0);
  const notBusy = await s.queue.submit({ key: 'aborted', priority: 0, job: () => Promise.reject(new DerivationAbortedError()) });
  assert.equal(notBusy.status, 'error');
});

test('a bump during the busy backoff cancels the timer, does not retry, and resolves superseded', async () => {
  const s = setup();
  let attempts = 0;
  const p = s.queue.submit({ key: 'g', priority: 0, job: () => { attempts += 1; throw busy(); } });
  await flush();
  assert.equal(s.scheduler.pendingTimers(), 1);
  s.generation.bump();
  assert.equal(s.scheduler.pendingTimers(), 0);
  assert.deepEqual(await p, { status: 'superseded' });
  await s.scheduler.advance(10 * DERIVATION_BUSY_RETRY_MS);
  assert.equal(attempts, 1);
  const p2 = s.queue.submit({ key: 'h', priority: 0, job: () => Promise.resolve('next') });
  assert.deepEqual(await p2, { status: 'ok', value: 'next' });
});

test('a scheduler that throws while arming the backoff yields {status:"error"} (no unhandled rejection) and frees the slot', async () => {
  const s = setup();
  const boomScheduler = { ...s.scheduler, now: s.scheduler.now, setTimeout() { throw new Error('timer down'); }, clearTimeout() {}, yield: s.scheduler.yield };
  const queue = createDerivationQueue({ scheduler: boomScheduler, generation: createGeneration() });
  const r = await queue.submit({ key: 'g', priority: 0, job: () => { throw busy(); } });
  assert.equal(r.status, 'error');
  assert.match(r.error.message, /timer down/);
  assert.deepEqual(await queue.submit({ key: 'h', priority: 0, job: () => 1 }), { status: 'ok', value: 1 });
});

test('dedupe per (generation, key): same promise, one computation, cached ok served again; an error is forgotten; a new generation recomputes', async () => {
  const s = setup();
  let calls = 0;
  const spec = { key: 'summary', priority: 0, job: () => { calls += 1; return Promise.resolve(calls); } };
  const p1 = s.queue.submit(spec);
  const p2 = s.queue.submit({ ...spec, priority: 3 });
  assert.equal(p1, p2);
  assert.deepEqual(await p1, { status: 'ok', value: 1 });
  assert.equal(s.queue.submit(spec), p1);
  assert.deepEqual(await s.queue.submit(spec), { status: 'ok', value: 1 });
  assert.equal(calls, 1);
  const other = await s.queue.submit({ ...spec, key: 'mask' });
  assert.deepEqual(other, { status: 'ok', value: 2 });
  let fails = 0;
  const flaky = { key: 'flaky', priority: 0, job: () => { fails += 1; return fails === 1 ? Promise.reject(new Error('once')) : Promise.resolve('good'); } };
  assert.equal((await s.queue.submit(flaky)).status, 'error');
  assert.deepEqual(await s.queue.submit(flaky), { status: 'ok', value: 'good' });
  s.generation.bump();
  assert.deepEqual(await s.queue.submit(spec), { status: 'ok', value: 3 });
  assert.equal(calls, 3);
});

```js
// clashpanel/core/derivationQueue.js
// Single-flight sequential queue for Core derivations (spec 5.2 "Derivation scheduling"). One job in flight, lowest
// priority number first, generation-aware: a bump aborts the running job and drops queued ones. DerivationBusyError
// (detected by name; the class is never imported) is retried through the injected scheduler, bounded.
import { DERIVATION_BUSY_MAX_RETRIES, DERIVATION_BUSY_RETRY_MS } from './constants.js';
import { assertScheduler } from './scheduler.js';

const SUPERSEDED = Object.freeze({ status: 'superseded' });

function isBusy(error) {
  try { return error !== null && typeof error === 'object' && error.name === 'DerivationBusyError'; } catch { return false; }
}

export function createDerivationQueue({ scheduler, generation } = {}) {
  assertScheduler(scheduler);
  for (const name of ['current', 'isCurrent']) {
    if (typeof generation?.[name] !== 'function') throw new TypeError(`createDerivationQueue: generation.${name} is required`);
  }
  const entries = new Map();     // `${generation}\0${key}` -> entry (pending, running, or a cached ok)
  const pending = [];
  let running = null;
  let disposed = false;
  let order = 0;
  let pumpScheduled = false;

  const forget = (entry) => { if (entries.get(entry.cacheKey) === entry) entries.delete(entry.cacheKey); };
  function settle(entry, result) {
    if (entry.settled) return;
    entry.settled = true;
    entry.resolve(result);
    if (result.status !== 'ok') forget(entry);        // an error or a supersession is never served from the cache
  }
  function supersede(entry) {
    entry.superseded = true;
    const at = pending.indexOf(entry);
    if (at >= 0) pending.splice(at, 1);
    if (entry.controller !== null) { try { entry.controller.abort(); } catch { /* an abort listener must not break the queue */ } }
    if (entry.backoff !== null) {
      const { handle, wake } = entry.backoff;
      entry.backoff = null;
      scheduler.clearTimeout(handle);
      wake();
    }
    settle(entry, SUPERSEDED);
  }
  function sweepStale() {
    for (const [key, entry] of [...entries]) {
      if (generation.isCurrent(entry.generation)) continue;
      if (entry.settled) entries.delete(key); else supersede(entry);
    }
  }

  async function run(entry) {
    entry.controller = new AbortController();
    let outcome = SUPERSEDED;
    try {
      for (;;) {
        if (entry.superseded || disposed) { outcome = SUPERSEDED; break; }
        let attempt;
        try { attempt = { ok: true, value: await entry.job(entry.controller.signal) }; } catch (error) { attempt = { ok: false, error }; }
        if (entry.superseded || disposed || !generation.isCurrent(entry.generation)) { outcome = SUPERSEDED; break; }
        if (attempt.ok) { outcome = { status: 'ok', value: attempt.value }; break; }
        if (isBusy(attempt.error) && entry.retries < DERIVATION_BUSY_MAX_RETRIES) {
          entry.retries += 1;
          await new Promise((wake) => {
            entry.backoff = { wake, handle: scheduler.setTimeout(() => { entry.backoff = null; wake(); }, DERIVATION_BUSY_RETRY_MS) };
          });
          continue;
        }
        outcome = { status: 'error', error: attempt.error };
        break;
      }
    } catch (error) {
      outcome = { status: 'error', error };            // e.g. the scheduler itself threw while arming the backoff
    } finally {
      entry.backoff = null;
      running = null;
      settle(entry, outcome);
      pump();
    }
  }

  function pump() {
    if (running !== null || disposed) return;
    sweepStale();
    if (pending.length === 0) return;
    let best = 0;
    for (let i = 1; i < pending.length; i += 1) {
      const a = pending[i];
      const b = pending[best];
      if (a.priority < b.priority || (a.priority === b.priority && a.order < b.order)) best = i;
    }
    [running] = pending.splice(best, 1);
    void run(running);
  }
  function schedulePump() {
    if (pumpScheduled) return;
    pumpScheduled = true;
    queueMicrotask(() => { pumpScheduled = false; pump(); });
  }

  function submit({ key, priority, job } = {}) {
    if (typeof key !== 'string' || key.length === 0) throw new TypeError('derivationQueue.submit: key must be a non-empty string');
    if (typeof priority !== 'number' || Number.isNaN(priority)) throw new TypeError('derivationQueue.submit: priority must be a number');
    if (typeof job !== 'function') throw new TypeError('derivationQueue.submit: job must be a function');
    if (disposed) return Promise.resolve(SUPERSEDED);
    sweepStale();
    const g = generation.current();
    const cacheKey = `${g}\u0000${key}`;
    const existing = entries.get(cacheKey);
    if (existing !== undefined) {
      if (pending.includes(existing) && priority < existing.priority) existing.priority = priority;
      return existing.promise;
    }
    let resolve;
    const promise = new Promise((res) => { resolve = res; });
    order += 1;
    const entry = {
      cacheKey, key, generation: g, priority, order, job, promise, resolve,
      settled: false, superseded: false, controller: null, backoff: null, retries: 0,
    };
    entries.set(cacheKey, entry);
    pending.push(entry);
    schedulePump();
    return promise;
  }

  const unsubscribe = typeof generation.onBump === 'function' ? generation.onBump(() => sweepStale()) : () => {};

  function dispose() {
    if (disposed) return;
    disposed = true;
    unsubscribe();
    for (const entry of [...entries.values()]) if (!entry.settled) supersede(entry);
    entries.clear();
    pending.length = 0;
  }

  return Object.freeze({ submit, dispose, stats: () => ({ pending: pending.length, running: running !== null, cached: entries.size }) });
}
```

### Task 8: Run state machine

**Tier:** [A] format-agnostic headless

**Files:**
- Create: `clashpanel/core/runMachine.js`
- Modify: `test/clashpanel/scaffold.test.mjs` (append `'core/runMachine.js'` to `EXPECTED_MODULES`)
- Test: `test/clashpanel/core/runMachine.test.mjs`

**Scope note:** a pure reducer; the controller (T16) owns the handle, subscribes, and feeds it `admitted` / `core-event` (+ `handle.getSnapshot()`) / `poll` / `stop-requested` / `done` / `admission-failed`. Core cannot distinguish "binding/enumerating" from "queued behind another consumer's run" (both publish only a `queued` snapshot, spec §19-1), so `waitingForOtherRun` is a **hedge**: it is set when a `poll` (controller re-reads `getSnapshot()` on its `READINESS_POLL_MS` timer while `preparing`) still reads `queued` after admission; the view text must say "may be waiting for another run" (T19). Real-engine tests below prove the reducer consumes what Core actually emits (verified at plan time: `state{planning,enumerating}` → `unit{running,executing}` → `state{completed,finalizing}` → `persistence` → `state{…,terminal:true}`; `cancelling` on a running cancel; queued cancel seals `cancelled` with 0 results).

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Core shapes only (no import in production code) — `RunHandle.getSnapshot()` fields and `state`/`unit`/`persistence` events (`clashtest/run/Run.js` `commitAndEmit`/`openFinalizeWindow`/`requestCancel`); `RunSummary{runId,status,resultSet|null,persistence}`. Test-only: `createClashTestEngine` (`clashtest/index.js`), `createEngineWorld` (`test/clashtest/support/engineWorld.mjs`), `createScriptedExecutor` (`…/scriptedExecutor.mjs`), `createFakeClock` (`…/fakeClock.mjs`).
- Produces: `RUN_PHASE`; `initialRunState(): RunState` (`{phase, runId, progress, startedAtMs, terminal, admissionError, waitingForOtherRun, stopRequested, lastSeq}`, frozen); `reduceRun(state, event): RunState`; `canRun(state)`; `canStop(state)`; `isRunActive(state)` (helper). `progress = {fraction, unitsEvaluated, unitsTotal, unitsFailedOrSkipped, resultsFound, caveatCount}` — no ETA/rate key (PD-13).

  assert.equal(canStop(s), false);
  assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(s).sort(),
    ['admissionError', 'lastSeq', 'phase', 'progress', 'runId', 'startedAtMs', 'stopRequested', 'terminal', 'waitingForOtherRun']);
  assert.ok(Object.isFrozen(s));
});

test('§7.1 table: every Panel state is entered from the real Core signal', () => {
  const rows = [
    // [label, events after admission, expected phase]
    ['admitted (queued snapshot, no event)', [], RUN_PHASE.PREPARING],
    ['first state event planning/enumerating', [core(ev('state', 1, 'planning', 'enumerating'))], RUN_PHASE.PLANNING],
    ['unit event running/executing', [core(ev('state', 1, 'planning', 'enumerating')), core(ev('unit', 2, 'running', 'executing'))], RUN_PHASE.RUNNING],
    ['cancelling', [core(ev('unit', 2, 'running', 'executing')), core(ev('state', 3, 'cancelling', 'executing'))], RUN_PHASE.STOPPING],
    ['sealed: terminal status + finalizing', [core(ev('unit', 2, 'running', 'executing')), core(ev('state', 3, 'completed', 'finalizing'))], RUN_PHASE.FINALIZING],
    ['terminal event before done', [core(ev('state', 3, 'completed', 'finalizing')), core(ev('state', 5, 'completed', 'terminal', { terminal: true, persistence: saved }))], RUN_PHASE.FINALIZING],
  ];
  for (const [label, events, expected] of rows) assert.equal(fold(events).phase, expected, label);
  const done = fold([{ type: 'done', summary: { status: 'completed', resultSet: { results: [] }, persistence: saved } }]);
  assert.equal(done.phase, RUN_PHASE.DONE);
  assert.equal(canRun(done), true);
  assert.equal(canStop(done), false);
});

test('Stop is enabled in every non-terminal state and moves to stopping (finalizing stays finalizing)', () => {
  const states = {
    preparing: admitted(),
    planning: fold([core(ev('state', 1, 'planning', 'enumerating'))]),
    running: fold([core(ev('unit', 2, 'running', 'executing'))]),
    finalizing: fold([core(ev('state', 3, 'cancelled', 'finalizing'))]),
  };
  for (const [label, s] of Object.entries(states)) {
    assert.equal(canStop(s), true, `${label}: Stop enabled`);
    assert.equal(canRun(s), false, `${label}: Run disabled while our run is non-terminal`);
    const after = reduceRun(s, { type: 'stop-requested' });
    assert.equal(after.stopRequested, true);
    assert.equal(after.phase, label === 'finalizing' ? RUN_PHASE.FINALIZING : RUN_PHASE.STOPPING, label);
    assert.equal(canStop(after), true, `${label}: a second Stop stays enabled (Core absorbs it)`);
  }
  assert.equal(reduceRun(initialRunState(), { type: 'stop-requested' }).phase, RUN_PHASE.IDLE);
});

test('a requested Stop is never visually undone by a later planning/unit event', () => {
  const s = fold([{ type: 'stop-requested' }, core(ev('state', 1, 'planning', 'enumerating')), core(ev('unit', 2, 'running', 'executing'))]);
  assert.equal(s.phase, RUN_PHASE.STOPPING);
  assert.equal(fold([core(ev('state', 4, 'cancelled', 'finalizing'))], s).phase, RUN_PHASE.FINALIZING);
});

test('done → terminal for completed/cancelled/failed/invalidated; a Stop that sealed failed shows failed', () => {
  for (const status of ['completed', 'cancelled', 'failed', 'invalidated']) {
    const s = fold([{ type: 'stop-requested' }, { type: 'done', summary: { status, resultSet: { results: [] }, persistence: saved } }]);
    assert.equal(s.phase, RUN_PHASE.DONE);
    assert.deepEqual({ ...s.terminal }, { status, persistence: saved, resultSetPresent: true });
  }
});

test('resultSet:null (fallback seal failed) ⇒ terminal.resultSetPresent === false', () => {
  const s = fold([{ type: 'done', summary: { status: 'failed', resultSet: null, persistence: { state: 'skipped', timedOut: false, attempt: 0, reason: 'seal-failed' } } }]);
  assert.equal(s.terminal.resultSetPresent, false);
  assert.equal(s.terminal.status, 'failed');
});

test('persistence events (even after terminal), progress events and stale seqs never transition', () => {
  const fin = fold([core(ev('state', 3, 'completed', 'finalizing'))]);
  assert.equal(reduceRun(fin, { type: 'core-event', event: { type: 'persistence', state: 'saved', timedOut: false, attempt: 1, seq: 4 } }), fin);
  assert.equal(reduceRun(fin, { type: 'core-event', event: { type: 'progress', seq: 9, status: 'running', phase: 'executing' } }), fin);
  assert.equal(reduceRun(fin, core(ev('unit', 2, 'running', 'executing'))), fin, 'seq 2 <= lastSeq 3');
  const done = fold([{ type: 'done', summary: { status: 'completed', resultSet: { results: [] }, persistence: saved } }], fin);
  assert.equal(reduceRun(done, { type: 'core-event', event: { type: 'persistence', state: 'failed', timedOut: false, attempt: 1, seq: 6 } }), done);
});

test('admission failure keeps idle (or the previous done) and records the error by name', () => {
  const err = Object.assign(new Error('result capacity 4 exhausted'), { name: 'ResultCapacityError', cap: 4, active: [], retained: ['r0'], held: [] });
  const idle = reduceRun(initialRunState(), { type: 'admission-failed', error: err });
  assert.equal(idle.phase, RUN_PHASE.IDLE);
  assert.equal(idle.admissionError.name, 'ResultCapacityError');
  assert.deepEqual(idle.admissionError.retained, ['r0']);
  const prevDone = fold([{ type: 'done', summary: { status: 'completed', resultSet: { results: [] }, persistence: saved } }]);
  const after = reduceRun(prevDone, { type: 'admission-failed', error: err });
  assert.equal(after.phase, RUN_PHASE.DONE, 'previous results/state preserved');
  assert.equal(after.terminal, prevDone.terminal);
  assert.equal(reduceRun(after, { type: 'admitted', snapshot: snap({ runId: 'r2' }), atMs: 5 }).admissionError, null);
  const running = fold([core(ev('unit', 2, 'running', 'executing'))]);
  assert.equal(reduceRun(running, { type: 'admission-failed', error: err }), running, 'ignored while our run is active');
});

test('waitingForOtherRun: set only when a POLL after admission still reads queued; cleared by the first state event', () => {
  const a = admitted();
  assert.equal(a.waitingForOtherRun, false, 'the admission snapshot itself never sets it');
  const w = reduceRun(a, { type: 'poll', snapshot: snap(), atMs: 2000 });
  assert.equal(w.waitingForOtherRun, true);
  assert.equal(w.phase, RUN_PHASE.PREPARING);
  assert.equal(reduceRun(w, core(ev('state', 1, 'planning', 'enumerating'))).waitingForOtherRun, false);
});

test('progress carries only fractions/counts; startedAtMs is the Panel clock; no ETA keys', () => {
  const s = fold([core(ev('unit', 2, 'running', 'executing'), snap({ seq: 2, status: 'running', phase: 'executing', unitsTotal: 4, unitsEvaluated: 1, fractionProcessed: 0.25, resultsFound: 3, caveatCount: 1 }))]);
  assert.equal(s.startedAtMs, 1000);
  assert.deepEqual({ ...s.progress }, { fraction: 0.25, unitsEvaluated: 1, unitsTotal: 4, unitsFailedOrSkipped: 0, resultsFound: 3, caveatCount: 1 });
  for (const k of Object.keys(s.progress)) assert.doesNotMatch(k, /eta|remaining|rate|throughput/i);
  const p0 = reduceRun(admitted(), { type: 'poll', snapshot: snap({ fractionProcessed: null }) });
  assert.equal(p0.progress.fraction, null, 'fractionProcessed is null while pairSpaceTotal is 0');
});

// ---- REAL engine: the reducer consumes what Core actually emits ----------------------------------------------
function realEngine(unitExecutor) {
  const w = createEngineWorld();
  const clock = createFakeClock({ start: Date.UTC(2026, 8, 26) });
  const engine = createClashTestEngine(w.config({
    unitExecutor, now: clock.now, yieldToScheduler: clock.yieldToScheduler, scheduleTimeout: () => () => {},
  }));
  return { engine, w };
}
function drive(handle) {
  let s = reduceRun(initialRunState(), { type: 'admitted', snapshot: handle.getSnapshot(), atMs: 0 });
  const phases = [s.phase];
  handle.subscribe((e) => { s = reduceRun(s, { type: 'core-event', event: e, snapshot: handle.getSnapshot() }); phases.push(s.phase); });
  return { get state() { return s; }, set state(v) { s = v; }, phases };
}
function gated() {
  const inner = createScriptedExecutor({}, { unscripted: { facts: [] } });
  let open; let started;
  const gate = new Promise((r) => { open = r; });
  const began = new Promise((r) => { started = r; });
  const exec = async (req) => { started(); await gate; return inner(req); };
  return { exec, began, release: () => open() };
}

test('REAL engine: a clean run walks preparing → planning → running → finalizing → done', async () => {
  const { engine, w } = realEngine(createScriptedExecutor({}, { unscripted: { facts: [] } }));
  const h = engine.startRun(w.definition());
  assert.equal(h.getSnapshot().status, 'queued', 'no event at queued; admission snapshot is queued');
  const d = drive(h);
  const summary = await h.done;
  d.state = reduceRun(d.state, { type: 'done', summary });
  assert.deepEqual([...new Set(d.phases)], ['preparing', 'planning', 'running', 'finalizing']);
  assert.equal(d.state.phase, 'done');
  assert.equal(d.state.terminal.status, 'completed');
  assert.equal(d.state.terminal.resultSetPresent, true);
});

test('REAL engine: Stop while running goes through cancelling (stopping) and seals cancelled', async () => {
  const g = gated();
  const { engine, w } = realEngine(g.exec);
  const h = engine.startRun(w.definition());
  const d = drive(h);
  await g.began;
  d.state = reduceRun(d.state, { type: 'stop-requested' });
  const donePromise = h.cancel('user');
  assert.equal(h.getSnapshot().status, 'cancelling');
  g.release();
  const summary = await donePromise;
  d.state = reduceRun(d.state, { type: 'done', summary });
  assert.ok(d.phases.includes('stopping'));
  assert.equal(d.state.terminal.status, 'cancelled');
});

test('REAL engine: Stop while preparing (queued behind another run) withdraws and seals cancelled', async () => {
  const g = gated();
  const { engine, w } = realEngine(g.exec);
  const first = engine.startRun(w.definition());
  await g.began;
  const second = engine.startRun(w.definition({ testId: 'T2' }));
  const d = drive(second);
  let polled = reduceRun(d.state, { type: 'poll', snapshot: second.getSnapshot() });
  assert.equal(polled.waitingForOtherRun, true);
  d.state = reduceRun(polled, { type: 'stop-requested' });
  const summary = await second.cancel('user');
  d.state = reduceRun(d.state, { type: 'done', summary });
  assert.equal(d.state.terminal.status, 'cancelled');
  assert.equal(summary.resultSet.results.length, 0);
  g.release();
  first.cancel('cleanup');
  await first.done;
});

```js
// clashpanel/core/runMachine.js
//
// Spec §7.1-§7.3: the Panel's run state as a PURE reducer over Core facts. Inputs are the real Core
// shapes (clashtest/run/Run.js): the first `state` event is {status:'planning', phase:'enumerating'}
// (no event at `queued`); `unit` events carry {status:'running', phase:'executing'}; `cancelling` is
// committed the moment a RUNNING run is cancelled; a sealed run publishes {status:<terminal>,
// phase:'finalizing'}, then {phase:'terminal', terminal:true, persistence}; a `persistence` event can
// arrive AFTER the terminal one and never changes the run state. `done` is the only way into `done`
// (spec §7.1: results are available only once `await handle.done` resolved). No ETA field exists
// anywhere in this state (PD-13); elapsed time is the controller's own clock minus `startedAtMs`.

export const RUN_PHASE = Object.freeze({
  IDLE: 'idle', PREPARING: 'preparing', PLANNING: 'planning', RUNNING: 'running',
  STOPPING: 'stopping', FINALIZING: 'finalizing', DONE: 'done',
});

const TERMINAL_STATUSES = new Set(['completed', 'cancelled', 'failed', 'invalidated']);
const NON_TERMINAL_PHASES = new Set([
  RUN_PHASE.PREPARING, RUN_PHASE.PLANNING, RUN_PHASE.RUNNING, RUN_PHASE.STOPPING, RUN_PHASE.FINALIZING,
]);

/** RunState = { phase, runId, progress, startedAtMs, terminal, admissionError, waitingForOtherRun,
 *               stopRequested, lastSeq }  — frozen; `progress` has NO eta/rate/remaining field. */
export function initialRunState() {
  return Object.freeze({
    phase: RUN_PHASE.IDLE, runId: null, progress: null, startedAtMs: null, terminal: null,
    admissionError: null, waitingForOtherRun: false, stopRequested: false, lastSeq: -1,
  });
}

const num = (v) => (Number.isFinite(v) ? v : 0);

/** The only progress the Panel shows: RunProgress fractions/counts (spec §7.1 `running` row). */
function progressOf(snapshot) {
  if (snapshot === null || typeof snapshot !== 'object') return null;
  return Object.freeze({
    fraction: Number.isFinite(snapshot.fractionProcessed) ? snapshot.fractionProcessed : null,
    unitsEvaluated: num(snapshot.unitsEvaluated),
    unitsTotal: num(snapshot.unitsTotal),
    unitsFailedOrSkipped: num(snapshot.unitsFailedOrSkipped),
    resultsFound: num(snapshot.resultsFound),
    caveatCount: num(snapshot.caveatCount),
  });
}

/** Maps one Core (status, phase) pair to a Panel phase, honouring a pending user Stop. */
function phaseFor(status, phase, stopRequested) {
  if (TERMINAL_STATUSES.has(status)) return RUN_PHASE.FINALIZING;   // sealed: `finalizing` or the terminal event
  if (status === 'cancelling') return RUN_PHASE.STOPPING;
  if (stopRequested) return RUN_PHASE.STOPPING;                    // a Stop is never visually undone
  if (status === 'running') return RUN_PHASE.RUNNING;
  if (status === 'planning') return RUN_PHASE.PLANNING;             // Core never publishes phase 'planning'
  if (status === 'queued') return RUN_PHASE.PREPARING;
  return null;                                                      // unknown status: no transition
}

const freeze = (s) => Object.freeze(s);

function describeError(error) {
  if (error === null || typeof error !== 'object') return freeze({ name: 'Error', message: String(error) });
  const out = { name: typeof error.name === 'string' ? error.name : 'Error', message: typeof error.message === 'string' ? error.message : '' };
  for (const k of ['issues', 'issuesTruncated', 'cap', 'active', 'retained', 'held', 'limit', 'queued', 'reason']) {
    if (error[k] !== undefined) out[k] = error[k];
  }
  return freeze(out);
}

export function reduceRun(state, event) {
  const type = event?.type;
  switch (type) {
    case 'admitted': {
      // `startRun` returned a handle; its snapshot is `queued` (binding/enumeration publish nothing, §19-1).
      const snapshot = event.snapshot ?? null;
      return freeze({
        phase: phaseFor(snapshot?.status, snapshot?.phase, false) ?? RUN_PHASE.PREPARING,
        runId: snapshot?.runId ?? event.runId ?? null,
        progress: progressOf(snapshot),
        startedAtMs: Number.isFinite(event.atMs) ? event.atMs : null,
        terminal: null, admissionError: null, waitingForOtherRun: false, stopRequested: false,
        lastSeq: Number.isFinite(snapshot?.seq) ? snapshot.seq : -1,
      });
    }
    case 'admission-failed': {
      // Spec §7.1/§7.6: an admission failure keeps the previous state (idle, or the previous `done`
      // with its results) and only records the error. Ignored while a run of ours is non-terminal.
      if (NON_TERMINAL_PHASES.has(state.phase)) return state;
      return freeze({ ...state, admissionError: describeError(event.error) });
    }
    case 'poll': {
      // The controller re-reads getSnapshot() while `preparing`. A snapshot that is STILL `queued`
      // after admission means preparing persists: Core cannot say whether it is binding/enumerating
      // or queued behind another consumer's run, so the flag is a hedge, never a certainty.
      if (!NON_TERMINAL_PHASES.has(state.phase)) return state;
      const snapshot = event.snapshot ?? null;
      if (Number.isFinite(snapshot?.seq) && snapshot.seq < state.lastSeq) return state;
      const next = { ...state, progress: progressOf(snapshot) ?? state.progress };
      if (state.phase === RUN_PHASE.PREPARING && snapshot?.status === 'queued') next.waitingForOtherRun = true;
      return freeze(next);
    }
    case 'core-event': {
      if (!NON_TERMINAL_PHASES.has(state.phase)) return state;       // idle/done: late events are ignored
      const ev = event.event ?? {};
      if (ev.type !== 'state' && ev.type !== 'unit') return state;   // `persistence` (maybe post-terminal), `progress`: no transition
      if (Number.isFinite(ev.seq) && ev.seq <= state.lastSeq) return state;   // stale/out-of-order delivery
      const mapped = phaseFor(ev.status, ev.phase, state.stopRequested);
      if (mapped === null) return state;
      // `finalizing` is absorbing until `done` (a sealed run never goes back to running/stopping).
      const phase = state.phase === RUN_PHASE.FINALIZING ? RUN_PHASE.FINALIZING : mapped;
      return freeze({
        ...state,
        phase,
        progress: progressOf(event.snapshot) ?? state.progress,
        waitingForOtherRun: phase === RUN_PHASE.PREPARING ? state.waitingForOtherRun : false,
        lastSeq: Number.isFinite(ev.seq) ? ev.seq : state.lastSeq,
      });
    }
    case 'stop-requested': {
      // Stop is enabled in EVERY non-terminal state (spec §14.4, AC-P3); Core absorbs a late cancel.
      if (!NON_TERMINAL_PHASES.has(state.phase)) return state;
      const phase = state.phase === RUN_PHASE.FINALIZING ? RUN_PHASE.FINALIZING : RUN_PHASE.STOPPING;
      return freeze({ ...state, phase, stopRequested: true, waitingForOtherRun: false });
    }
    case 'done': {
      if (state.phase === RUN_PHASE.IDLE || state.phase === RUN_PHASE.DONE) return state;
      const summary = event.summary ?? {};
      return freeze({
        ...state,
        phase: RUN_PHASE.DONE,
        waitingForOtherRun: false,
        // The ACTUAL sealed status (Core precedence failed > invalidated > cancelled > completed):
        // a Stop that sealed `failed` shows failed, never "Stopped" (spec §7.2).
        terminal: freeze({
          status: summary.status,
          persistence: summary.persistence ?? null,
          resultSetPresent: summary.resultSet !== null && summary.resultSet !== undefined,
        }),
      });
    }
    default:
      return state;
  }
}

export function canRun(state) {
  return state.phase === RUN_PHASE.IDLE || state.phase === RUN_PHASE.DONE;
}

export function canStop(state) {
  return NON_TERMINAL_PHASES.has(state.phase);
}

export function isRunActive(state) {
  return NON_TERMINAL_PHASES.has(state.phase);
}
```

### Task 9: Result-set residency

**Tier:** [A] format-agnostic headless

**Files:**
- Create: `clashpanel/core/residency.js`
- Modify: `test/clashpanel/support/fakeEngine.mjs` (Task 3's double: add lease-release failure injection + a live-lease counter; no second fake engine)
- Modify: `test/clashpanel/scaffold.test.mjs` (append `'core/residency.js'` to `EXPECTED_MODULES`)
- Test: `test/clashpanel/core/residency.test.mjs`

**Scope note:** at most one displayed set (spec §7.6). `adopt` is called only for a non-superseded `done`; admission-first ordering (release the previous set only after `startRun` returned a handle) is the controller's (T16) — residency provides the release primitive. `onPersisted` re-reads `engine.getPersistenceState(currentRunId)` instead of trusting its argument, so a superseded run's late `persisted` can never upgrade the wrong set. Nothing here throws to the caller except the programming-error guard in `adopt` (adopting over a still-held set). A release with a failed step is never forgotten: the displayed slot is freed at once (the Panel stops showing it) but `{runId, lease, unsaved}` goes to an internal `stuck` list that every later `release()`/`disposeAll()` retries first; an entry is dropped only once `releaseResultSet` succeeds (non-resident = no-op success). `released` is true only with no errors and no stuck entries.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `engine.retainResultSet(runId) -> {release()}` (one-shot; throws `UnsavedResultSetError` unless `saved`, `ResultNotResidentError` if not resident), `engine.releaseResultSet(runId, {acknowledgeUnsaved?})` (throws `ResultSetRetainedError` while leased, `UnsavedResultSetError` without ack; non-resident = no-op), `engine.getPersistenceState(runId) -> {state,…}|null` (`clashtest/results/residency.js:277-311`, `clashtest/engine.js`); errors by `error.name`. Test-only: Task 3 `createFakeEngine()` (`makeResident`, `setPersistenceState`, `failNextRetain`, `failNextRelease`, `residentRunIds`, `calls`, `order`, strict residency) + the two capabilities added here; real engine via `createEngineWorld` + `startRun(def, {persist:false})` for `skipped`.
- Produces: `createResidency({engine}) -> {adopt(summary) -> {kind:'leased'|'held-unsaved'|'none', notice, errors}, onPersisted(outcome) -> {kind, notice, errors}, current() -> {runId, kind}|null, release({acknowledgeUnsaved}) -> {released, needsAcknowledgement, errors, stuckCount, droppedUnsaved?}, releaseSuperseded(summary) -> {errors, stuckCount} (a failed attempt joins the stuck ledger; never touches the displayed set), disposeAll() -> {droppedUnsaved, errors, stuckCount}}`; `HELD_IN_MEMORY_NOTICE`.

**Depends on:** T1, T3.

// test/clashpanel/core/residency.test.mjs — Task 9 (spec §7.6, AC-P14, PV-3)
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { createResidency, HELD_IN_MEMORY_NOTICE } from '../../../clashpanel/core/residency.js';
import { createFakeEngine } from '../support/fakeEngine.mjs';
import { createClashTestEngine } from '../../../clashtest/index.js';
import { createEngineWorld } from '../../clashtest/support/engineWorld.mjs';
import { createScriptedExecutor } from '../../clashtest/support/scriptedExecutor.mjs';
import { createFakeClock } from '../../clashtest/support/fakeClock.mjs';

const P = {
  saved: { state: 'saved', timedOut: false, attempt: 1 },
  pending: { state: 'pending', timedOut: true, attempt: 1 },
  failed: { state: 'failed', timedOut: false, attempt: 1, error: { name: 'Error', message: 'disk full' } },
  noStore: { state: 'skipped', timedOut: false, attempt: 0, reason: 'no-store' },
  persistFalse: { state: 'skipped', timedOut: false, attempt: 0, reason: 'persist-false' },
};
/** A resident sealed set in the T3 fake engine + the RunSummary Core would resolve `done` with. */
const seal = (engine, runId, persistence) => {
  engine.makeResident(runId, persistence);
  return Object.freeze({ runId, status: 'completed', resultSet: Object.freeze({ runId, results: [] }), persistence });
};
/** What `persisted` settles with once a pending write finishes; the engine's by-id state moves with it. */
const settle = (engine, runId, state) => {
  engine.setPersistenceState(runId, { state, timedOut: false, attempt: 1 });
  return state === 'saved' ? { state } : state === 'failed' ? { state, error: new Error('write failed') } : { state, reason: 'no-store' };
};
const releases = (engine) => engine.calls.releaseResultSet.map(({ runId, opts }) => [runId, opts ?? {}]);
const clean = (engine) => { assert.equal(engine.liveLeaseCount(), 0, 'no leaked lease'); assert.deepEqual(engine.residentRunIds(), [], 'no leaked slot'); };

    assert.deepEqual(r.adopt(seal(engine, 'u', p)), { kind: 'held-unsaved', notice: HELD_IN_MEMORY_NOTICE, errors: [] });
    assert.deepEqual(engine.calls.retainResultSet, [], 'never retains an unsaved set');
    assert.deepEqual(r.release({ acknowledgeUnsaved: false }), { released: false, needsAcknowledgement: true, errors: [], stuckCount: 0 });
    assert.deepEqual(r.current(), { runId: 'u', kind: 'held-unsaved' }, 'still displayed until acknowledged');
    assert.deepEqual(engine.residentRunIds(), ['u']);
    const second = r.release({ acknowledgeUnsaved: true });
    assert.equal(second.released, true);
    assert.equal(second.droppedUnsaved, true);

    clean(engine);
  }
});

test('each release step in its own try: a throwing lease.release does not strand releaseResultSet, and vice versa', () => {
  const e1 = createFakeEngine();
  const r1 = createResidency({ engine: e1 });
  r1.adopt(seal(e1, 'a', P.saved));
  e1.failNextLeaseRelease(new Error('boom'));
  const out1 = r1.release({});
  assert.equal(out1.released, false);
  assert.deepEqual(releases(e1), [['a', {}]], 'releaseResultSet still attempted');
  assert.deepEqual(out1.errors.map((e) => e.name), ['Error', 'ResultSetRetainedError'], 'both failures reported, none thrown');
  assert.equal(r1.current(), null, 'the Panel no longer displays it');
  assert.equal(out1.stuckCount, 1, 'the failed release is remembered, not forgotten');
  assert.equal(e1.liveLeaseCount(), 1);
  const retry = r1.release({});                        // next Clear / Run: the stuck entry is retried first
  assert.deepEqual(retry, { released: true, needsAcknowledgement: false, errors: [], stuckCount: 0 });
  assert.equal(e1.liveLeaseCount(), 0);
  assert.deepEqual(e1.residentRunIds(), [], 'slot recovered');

  const e2 = createFakeEngine();
  const r2 = createResidency({ engine: e2 });
  r2.adopt(seal(e2, 'b', P.saved));
  e2.failNextRelease(Object.assign(new Error('engine refused'), { name: 'EngineDisposedError' }));
  const out2 = r2.release({});
  assert.equal(e2.liveLeaseCount(), 0, 'the lease was released before the throwing step');
  assert.deepEqual(out2.errors.map((e) => e.name), ['EngineDisposedError']);
});

test('a stuck release (one-shot lease.release failure) is recovered by the next Run-replace, Clear or dispose', () => {
  for (const next of ['run-replace', 'clear', 'dispose']) {
    const engine = createFakeEngine();
    const r = createResidency({ engine });
    r.adopt(seal(engine, 'a', P.saved));
    engine.failNextLeaseRelease(new Error('boom'));
    const first = r.release({});
    assert.deepEqual([first.released, first.stuckCount], [false, 1], next);
    assert.deepEqual(engine.residentRunIds(), ['a'], 'still retained after the failed attempt');
    if (next === 'run-replace') {
      r.adopt(seal(engine, 'b', P.saved));             // a new run was displayed meanwhile
      const out = r.release({});
      assert.deepEqual([out.released, out.stuckCount, out.errors.length], [true, 0, 0], next);
    } else if (next === 'clear') {
      assert.equal(r.release({ acknowledgeUnsaved: false }).released, true, next);
    } else {
      assert.deepEqual(r.disposeAll(), { droppedUnsaved: false, errors: [], stuckCount: 0 }, next);
    }
    clean(engine);
  }
});

test('AC-P14 matrix: every persistence state × replace / Clear / dispose / disposal-during-active-run — no throw, no leak', () => {
  const states = { saved: [P.saved], 'pending→saved': [P.pending, 'saved'], 'pending→failed': [P.pending, 'failed'], failed: [P.failed], skipped: [P.noStore] };
  for (const [label, [initial, later]] of Object.entries(states)) {
    for (const path of ['replace', 'clear', 'dispose', 'dispose-during-run']) {
      const engine = createFakeEngine();
      const r = createResidency({ engine });
      const summary = seal(engine, 'run', initial);
      assert.doesNotThrow(() => {
        if (path === 'dispose-during-run') {
          r.disposeAll();                                 // nothing displayed yet; the run is still active
          if (later) settle(engine, 'run', later);
          r.releaseSuperseded(summary);                    // its late done arrives after dispose
          return;
        }
        r.adopt(summary);
        if (later) r.onPersisted(settle(engine, 'run', later));
        if (path === 'dispose') { r.disposeAll(); return; }
        const first = r.release({ acknowledgeUnsaved: false });   // Run / Clear results clicked
        if (first.needsAcknowledgement) r.release({ acknowledgeUnsaved: true });   // user confirmed "discard unsaved?"
      }, `${label} / ${path}`);
      clean(engine);
    }
  }
});

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** `clashpanel/core/residency.js`:

```js
// clashpanel/core/residency.js
//
// Spec §7.6 (verified against clashtest/results/residency.js + engine.js): the Panel holds AT MOST
// ONE displayed set. `retainResultSet(runId)` is a ONE-SHOT lease and throws UnsavedResultSetError
// unless persistence is `saved`; `releaseResultSet(runId, {acknowledgeUnsaved})` throws
// ResultSetRetainedError while a lease is live and UnsavedResultSetError for an unsaved set without
// the acknowledgement; releasing a non-resident id is a no-op. Errors are discriminated by
// `error.name` (spec §13 rule 4). Every engine call sits in its OWN try so no failure strands the
// next step, and nothing here ever throws to the controller (AC-P14).

export const HELD_IN_MEMORY_NOTICE = 'Results are held in memory only.';

const nameOf = (e) => (e && typeof e.name === 'string' ? e.name : 'Error');

export function createResidency({ engine }) {
  if (!engine || typeof engine.retainResultSet !== 'function' || typeof engine.releaseResultSet !== 'function'
      || typeof engine.getPersistenceState !== 'function') {
    throw new TypeError('createResidency: engine must expose retainResultSet, releaseResultSet and getPersistenceState');
  }
  /** @type {null | { runId: string, kind: 'leased'|'held-unsaved', lease: {release(): void}|null }} */
  let held = null;

  const readState = (runId) => {
    try { return engine.getPersistenceState(runId)?.state ?? null; } catch { return null; }
  };

  /** Try to turn a saved set into a lease; any refusal leaves it engine-held (never throws). */
  function tryLease(runId, errors) {
    try {
      return { kind: 'leased', lease: engine.retainResultSet(runId) };
    } catch (e) {
      errors.push(e);
      if (nameOf(e) === 'ResultNotResidentError') return { kind: 'none', lease: null };
      return { kind: 'held-unsaved', lease: null };               // UnsavedResultSetError or anything else
    }
  }

  function adopt(summary) {
    if (held !== null) throw new Error('residency.adopt: release the previously displayed set first');
    const errors = [];
    const runId = summary?.runId ?? summary?.resultSet?.runId ?? null;
    if (summary?.resultSet === null || summary?.resultSet === undefined || runId === null) {
      return { kind: 'none', notice: null, errors };             // fallback seal failed: nothing resident
    }
    const state = summary.persistence?.state;
    if (state === 'saved') {
      const r = tryLease(runId, errors);
      if (r.kind !== 'none') held = { runId, kind: r.kind, lease: r.lease };
      return { kind: r.kind, notice: r.kind === 'held-unsaved' ? HELD_IN_MEMORY_NOTICE : null, errors };
    }
    held = { runId, kind: 'held-unsaved', lease: null };
    // `pending` (persistTimeoutMs elapsed): v1 shows nothing extra unless it later fails (spec §7.6).
    return { kind: 'held-unsaved', notice: state === 'pending' ? null : HELD_IN_MEMORY_NOTICE, errors };
  }

  /** `handle.persisted` settled. The authoritative state is re-read BY ID for the CURRENT set, so a
   *  superseded run's late outcome can never upgrade or annotate the wrong set. */
  function onPersisted(/* outcome — informational only */) {
    if (held === null || held.kind !== 'held-unsaved') return { kind: held?.kind ?? 'none', notice: null, errors: [] };
    const errors = [];
    const state = readState(held.runId);
    if (state === 'saved') {
      const r = tryLease(held.runId, errors);
      if (r.kind === 'none') { held = null; return { kind: 'none', notice: null, errors }; }
      held = { runId: held.runId, kind: r.kind, lease: r.lease };
      return { kind: r.kind, notice: null, errors };
    }
    if (state === 'failed' || state === 'skipped') return { kind: 'held-unsaved', notice: HELD_IN_MEMORY_NOTICE, errors };
    return { kind: 'held-unsaved', notice: null, errors };
  }

  function current() {
    return held === null ? null : { runId: held.runId, kind: held.kind };
  }

  /** Sets whose release had a failed step: {runId, lease|null, unsaved}. Never forgotten until the engine
   *  confirms the slot is gone (releaseResultSet succeeded — a non-resident id is a no-op success). */
  const stuck = [];

  /** One attempt at both steps for an entry; returns true when the slot is confirmed released. */
  function attemptRelease(entry, errors) {
    if (entry.lease !== null) {
      try { entry.lease.release(); entry.lease = null; } catch (e) { errors.push(e); }
    }
    try {
      engine.releaseResultSet(entry.runId, entry.unsaved ? { acknowledgeUnsaved: true } : {});
      return true;
    } catch (e) {
      errors.push(e);
      return nameOf(e) === 'ResultNotResidentError';         // defensive: gone is gone
    }
  }

  /** Retry every previously stuck release first (each in its own try). */
  function retryStuck(errors) {
    for (const entry of [...stuck]) {
      const attemptErrors = [];
      if (attemptRelease(entry, attemptErrors)) stuck.splice(stuck.indexOf(entry), 1);   // recovered: errors of a success are moot
      else errors.push(...attemptErrors);
    }
  }

  const result = (errors, extra = {}) => ({
    released: errors.length === 0 && stuck.length === 0, needsAcknowledgement: false, errors, stuckCount: stuck.length, ...extra,
  });

  /** Release path (replace / Clear results / dispose). Step (1) lease.release(), step (2)
   *  releaseResultSet(runId, {acknowledgeUnsaved}) — each in its own try (spec §7.6 (3)). A release with a
   *  failed step is kept in `stuck` and retried by every later release()/disposeAll(). */
  function release({ acknowledgeUnsaved = false } = {}) {
    const errors = [];
    retryStuck(errors);
    if (held === null) return result(errors);
    const { runId, kind, lease } = held;
    let unsaved = false;
    if (kind === 'held-unsaved') {
      unsaved = readState(runId) !== 'saved';                    // pending→saved may have landed unobserved
      if (unsaved && acknowledgeUnsaved !== true) {
        return { released: false, needsAcknowledgement: true, errors, stuckCount: stuck.length };   // keep holding; ask once
      }
    }
    held = null;                                                  // the Panel stops displaying it regardless
    const entry = { runId, lease, unsaved };
    const own = [];
    if (!attemptRelease(entry, own)) stuck.push(entry);
    errors.push(...own);
    return result(errors, { droppedUnsaved: unsaved });
  }

  /** A superseded run's late `done`: release its own set without displaying it. The user action
   *  that superseded it (Run / New test / Clear / dispose) is the acknowledgement. */
  function releaseSuperseded(summary) {
    const errors = [];
    const runId = summary?.runId ?? summary?.resultSet?.runId ?? null;
    const out = () => ({ errors, stuckCount: stuck.length });
    if (summary?.resultSet === null || summary?.resultSet === undefined || runId === null) return out();
    if (held !== null && held.runId === runId) return out();       // never touch the displayed set here
    const unsaved = (readState(runId) ?? summary.persistence?.state) !== 'saved';
    const entry = { runId, lease: null, unsaved };
    if (!attemptRelease(entry, errors)) stuck.push(entry);          // retried by the next release()/disposeAll()
    return out();
  }

  /** Dispose: no user to ask, so an unsaved set is acknowledged and the drop is REPORTED (spec §7.6). */
  function disposeAll() {
    const r = release({ acknowledgeUnsaved: true });
    return { droppedUnsaved: r.droppedUnsaved === true, errors: r.errors, stuckCount: r.stuckCount };
  }

  return Object.freeze({ adopt, onPersisted, current, release, releaseSuperseded, disposeAll });
}
```
