- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** `clashpanel/core/resultIndex.js`:

```js
// clashpanel/core/resultIndex.js
//
// Spec §8.1: built ONCE per displayed set. It holds REFERENCES to the frozen `results[]` records
// (never copies) plus the Panel's own Map<resultId, canonicalIndex> (Core exports no `getResult`
// and no id helpers, spec §19-11). Soft/Hard comes from the sealed `definition.mode`; a
// pre-resolution seal has `definition: null` (and no results) ⇒ not Soft, no clearance.
// `provenance.models[].elementCount` is deliberately NOT read (G-EC, AC-P12).

export function buildResultIndex(resultSet) {
  if (resultSet === null || typeof resultSet !== 'object' || !Array.isArray(resultSet.results)) {
    throw new TypeError('buildResultIndex: a sealed ResultSet with a results array is required');
  }
  const results = resultSet.results;
  const count = results.length;
  const byId = new Map();
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 1) {
    const id = results[i].resultId;
    if (!byId.has(id)) byId.set(id, i);                   // resultIds are unique in a sealed set; first wins defensively
  }
  const definition = resultSet.definition ?? null;
  const mode = typeof definition?.mode === 'string' ? definition.mode : null;
  const isSoft = mode === 'clearance';
  const clearance = isSoft && Number.isFinite(definition.clearance) ? definition.clearance : null;
  const models = Object.freeze((resultSet.provenance?.models ?? []).map((m) => Object.freeze({
    modelKey: m.modelKey, modelVersion: m.modelVersion, bindingGeneration: m.bindingGeneration,
  })));
  return Object.freeze({
    resultSet,
    count,
    at(i) { return Number.isInteger(i) && i >= 0 && i < count ? results[i] : undefined; },
    indexOfResultId(resultId) { const i = byId.get(resultId); return i === undefined ? -1 : i; },
    models,
    mode,
    clearance,
    isSoft,
  });
}
```

### Task 11: Run report (axes, headlines, claim gaps, empty statements, §13 error mapping, banners, diagnostics)

**Tier:** [A] format-agnostic headless

**Files:**
- Create: `clashpanel/core/runReport.js`
- Modify: `test/clashpanel/scaffold.test.mjs` (append `'core/runReport.js'` to `EXPECTED_MODULES`)
- Test: `test/clashpanel/core/runReport.test.mjs`

**Scope note:** `explainNoClashGaps` mirrors `clashtest/results/claim.js:51-63` conjunct for conjunct (minus `noResults`). The `knownDigestVersion` conjunct needs `DIGEST_VERSION`, which the barrel does not export, so it is read from Core's own claim result (`qualifiers` contains `{kind:'digest-version'}` exactly when it failed) — the Panel never restates the constant. A DIFFERENTIAL test pins agreement with the real pure `assessNoClashClaim` over every `sealedSet`/`sealFakeRun` kind and over single-conjunct flips of `claimableSet()`. `emptyStatement` is the ONE pure claim gate (review H1): a clearance sentence needs BOTH `claim.allowed === true` (Core is the authority for the claim) AND the completed live `freshness.state === 'current'`, evaluated over ONE `(claim, freshness)` pair that the caller passes together (T17 owns committing that pair atomically — see its scope note); a missing half is *pending*, any other combination is a non-claim, and `freshness` is read once so the gate and the gap list can never disagree. No Core default number (e.g. `maxCollisionInstancesPerEpoch`) is restated in wording; the result-cap value is read from the sealed `provenance.runOptions.maxResultsPerRun`.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: sealed `outcome{status,coverage,integrity,freshness,reasons[]}` (reasons spelled `unit:<cause>`, `planning:<cause>`, `cancel-requested`, `placement-changed`, `engine-disposed` — `clashtest/run/settlement.js:116-125`), `ledger{pairSpaceTotal,emptyOperand,unresolvedSelections,unreachablePopulation,hierarchyInternal[{modelKey,rootCount,ownerCount}],planningGaps[{phase,cause}],units[{outcome,cause}]}`, `provenance{hierarchyInternalAcceptance,runOptions.maxResultsPerRun}`, `diagnostics.truncated`; `engine.assessNoClashClaim` result `{allowed,unqualified,qualifiers}`; `engine.getFreshness` result `{state,reasons}`; Core error names/fields (`clashtest/errors.js`: `ResultCapacityError{cap,active[],retained[],held[{runId,persistence}]}`). Planning causes per `clashtest/planning/ElementEnumerator.js:46-49`; unit causes per `clashtest/execution/UnitExecutor.js:36-40`. Test-only: `assessNoClashClaim` + error classes from `clashtest/index.js`; `sealedSet`, `sealFakeRun`, `resealed`, `claimableSet` from `resultSetFixtures.mjs`.
- Produces: `STATEMENTS`; `describeAxes(outcome, freshness|null)`; `explainNoClashGaps(resultSet, {freshness?, claim?} = {})`; `scopeSummary(resultSet, modelName?)`; `emptyStatement({resultSet, claim, freshness, modelName?}) -> {kind,text,lines}|null` (null when results exist or no set; `kind` is `'claim'`/`'qualified-claim'` ONLY for `claim.allowed === true` ∧ `freshness.state === 'current'`, `'non-claim'` with `STATEMENTS.CLAIM_PENDING` when either half is `null`, `'stale'` for a completed stale/unverifiable freshness, otherwise `'non-claim'`); `runHeadline({status,total,coverage,resultSet?})`; `mapSealedFailure(resultSet|null) -> {headline,details,retainedNote}`; `unitGapLines(resultSet)`; `mapAdmissionError(error, {heldRunId?} = {}) -> {text, action:null|'release-and-retry'}`; `bannersFor({terminal,resultSet,freshness,setupChanged,persistence}) -> Banner[]`; `diagnosticsExport(resultSet|null) -> string`.

**Depends on:** T1; T8 (the `terminal` shape consumed by `bannersFor`).

test('H1 claim gate: a clearance sentence needs claim.allowed === true AND a completed freshness.state === "current" (whole matrix)', async () => {
  const cleanSet = await sealedSet('completed-clean');                       // empty results, completed/full/clean
  const ALLOWED = { allowed: true, unqualified: true, qualifiers: [], exclusions: [], proofMethod: 'bracketed-digest' };
  const QUALIFIED = { allowed: true, unqualified: false, qualifiers: [{ kind: 'hierarchy-internal-accepted' }], exclusions: [] };
  const DENIED = { allowed: false, unqualified: false, qualifiers: [], exclusions: [] };
  const claims = { allowed: ALLOWED, qualified: QUALIFIED, denied: DENIED, pending: null };
  const freshnesses = {
    current: CURRENT,
    stale: { state: 'stale', reasons: ['scope-drift'] },
    unverifiable: { state: 'unverifiable', reasons: [] },
    pending: null,
    empty: {},                                                              // malformed reads fail closed
    unknownState: { state: 'fresh', reasons: [] },
    noReasons: { state: 'current' },
  };
  for (const [cn, claim] of Object.entries(claims)) {
    for (const [fn, freshness] of Object.entries(freshnesses)) {
      const s = emptyStatement({ resultSet: cleanSet, claim, freshness });
      const mayClaim = claim !== null && claim.allowed === true && fn === 'current';
      assert.equal(['claim', 'qualified-claim'].includes(s.kind), mayClaim, `${cn} × ${fn}: kind ${s.kind}`);
      if (!mayClaim) for (const str of strings(s)) assert.doesNotMatch(str, /No clashes/, `${cn} × ${fn}: ${str}`);
    }
  }
  const kindOf = (claim, freshness) => emptyStatement({ resultSet: cleanSet, claim, freshness });
  assert.equal(kindOf(ALLOWED, CURRENT).text, STATEMENTS.CLAIM);                                 // allowed + current ⇒ allowed wording
  assert.equal(kindOf(QUALIFIED, CURRENT).text, STATEMENTS.QUALIFIED_CLAIM);
  const allowedStale = kindOf(ALLOWED, freshnesses.stale);                                       // allowed + stale ⇒ forbidden
  assert.deepEqual([allowedStale.kind, allowedStale.text, allowedStale.lines], ['stale', STATEMENTS.NON_CLAIM, [STATEMENTS.STALE, 'Reason: scope-drift']]);
  assert.equal(kindOf(ALLOWED, freshnesses.unverifiable).kind, 'stale');
  assert.equal(kindOf(ALLOWED, null).text, STATEMENTS.CLAIM_PENDING);                            // freshness not read yet ⇒ pending, not a claim
  assert.equal(kindOf(null, CURRENT).text, STATEMENTS.CLAIM_PENDING);                            // claim not read yet ⇒ pending
  assert.equal(kindOf(DENIED, CURRENT).text, STATEMENTS.NON_CLAIM);                              // disallowed + current ⇒ forbidden
  assert.equal(kindOf(ALLOWED, freshnesses.empty).kind, 'non-claim');
});

test('AC-P2: no output of any runReport function contains a bare "No clashes" across all fixtures × claim states', async () => {
  const produced = [];

      produced.push(describeAxes(set.outcome, fresh), mapSealedFailure(set), bannersFor({ terminal: { status: set.outcome.status, resultSetPresent: true }, resultSet: set, freshness: fresh, setupChanged: true, persistence: { state: 'failed' } }));
      for (const status of ['completed', 'cancelled', 'failed', 'invalidated']) produced.push(runHeadline({ status, total: set.results.length, coverage: set.outcome.coverage, resultSet: set }));
    }

  for (const s of strings(produced)) assert.doesNotMatch(s, BARE_NO_CLASHES, s);

});

test('§13 rows: planning failure, enumeration-failed likely causes, mid-planning unload (either cause), duplicate rows', async () => {

  assert.deepEqual(dup.details, ["The model's element ownership could not be mapped consistently."], 'residual M2: one line');
});

    [new UnsupportedSchemaVersionError({ type: 'definition', schemaVersion: 9 }), /definition version/],

    [new InvalidOptionsError({ reason: 'unknown-key' }), /run options/],
    [new RunQueueFullError({ limit: 8, queued: 8 }), /too many runs are waiting/],
    [new EngineDisposedError(), /shut down/],
  ];
  for (const [error, re] of rows) {
    const m = mapAdmissionError(error, { heldRunId: 'mine' });
    assert.match(m.text, re, error.name);
    assert.equal(m.action, null, error.name);
  }
  const blockedByMe = [
    new ResultCapacityError({ cap: 4, active: [], retained: ['mine'], held: [] }),
    new ResultCapacityError({ cap: 4, active: [], retained: [], held: [{ runId: 'mine', persistence: 'skipped' }] }),
  ];
  for (const e of blockedByMe) assert.deepEqual({ ...mapAdmissionError(e, { heldRunId: 'mine' }) }, { text: 'The clash engine is at capacity. Clear previous results and try again.', action: 'release-and-retry' });
  const other = new ResultCapacityError({ cap: 4, active: ['x'], retained: ['y'], held: [] });
  assert.equal(mapAdmissionError(other, { heldRunId: 'mine' }).action, null);
  assert.equal(mapAdmissionError(blockedByMe[0]).action, null, 'no held set ⇒ nothing to release');
  const hostile = '<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>';
  assert.equal(mapAdmissionError(Object.assign(new Error(hostile), { name: 'WeirdError' })).text, `The run could not be started: ${hostile}`, 'untrusted text passes through as a plain string');
});

test('bannersFor: no-result-set, failed, stale (live reasons, plain text), setup changed, held-unsaved; axes badges', async () => {
  const none = bannersFor({ terminal: { status: 'failed', resultSetPresent: false }, resultSet: null });

  const failed = bannersFor({ terminal: { status: 'failed', resultSetPresent: true }, resultSet: await sealFakeRun('failed') });
  assert.deepEqual(failed.map((x) => [x.id, x.kind, x.text]), [['failed', 'error', 'The test could not be planned.'], ['stale', 'warning', STATEMENTS.STALE]]);

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** `clashpanel/core/runReport.js`:

```js
// clashpanel/core/runReport.js
//
// Panel-owned wording (spec §7.3, §7.5, §13; SPEC §20). Pure functions over SEALED data only.
// Rules: (1) never the bare phrase "No clashes" — the only sentences that start with it are the two
// §7.5 claim statements, emitted only when Core's `assessNoClashClaim` said `allowed` AND the completed live
// freshness of the SAME (claim, freshness) pair is `current` (review H1); (2) the gap
// list is RECOMPUTED here from `outcome` + `ledger` because Core's claim result does not say which
// conjunct failed (it mirrors clashtest/results/claim.js:51-63 conjunct for conjunct); (3) every
// string is plain text — untrusted text (error messages, model names, reasons) passes through
// unchanged and the UI inserts it with textContent (AC-P13); (4) `provenance.models[].elementCount`
// is never read (G-EC, AC-P12); (5) Core errors are discriminated by `error.name` (§13 rule 4).

export const STATEMENTS = Object.freeze({
  CLAIM: 'No clashes found in the evaluated scope.',
  QUALIFIED_CLAIM: 'No clashes found, excluding the hierarchy-internal pairs recorded in ledger.hierarchyInternal.',
  NON_CLAIM: '0 clashes reported — this is not a clearance.',
  CLAIM_PENDING: '0 clashes reported — checking whether this is a clearance…',
  STALE: 'Results describe a previous model/placement state.',
  NO_CONFIRMATION: 'The clash engine did not confirm a clearance for this run.',
  ENGINE_FAILED: 'The clash engine failed. Details are available to copy.',
  NO_RESULT_SET: 'The clash engine failed and produced no result set. Details are available to copy.',
  MODEL_CHANGED: 'The model changed during the run — results are partial and stale',
  HELD_IN_MEMORY: 'Results are held in memory only.',
  SETUP_CHANGED: 'The test setup changed since this run — run it again to see results for the new setup.',
  DIAGNOSTICS_TRUNCATED: 'Diagnostic detail was truncated',
});

const plural = (n, one, many) => `${n} ${n === 1 ? one : many}`;
const fmtInt = (n) => (Number.isFinite(n) ? Math.trunc(n).toLocaleString('en-US') : String(n));
const list = (v) => (Array.isArray(v) ? v : []);

// ---- axes -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** The three always-visible badges (spec §7.3). `freshness` is the live {state,reasons} from
 *  engine.getFreshness, or null while the check is pending (then the at-seal value is shown). */
export function describeAxes(outcome, freshness) {
  const coverage = outcome?.coverage === 'full' ? 'full' : 'partial';
  const integrity = outcome?.integrity === 'clean' ? 'clean' : 'caveated';
  const live = freshness && typeof freshness.state === 'string' ? freshness.state : null;
  const value = live ?? (typeof outcome?.freshness === 'string' ? outcome.freshness : 'unverifiable');
  return Object.freeze({
    coverage: Object.freeze({ value: coverage, label: `Coverage: ${coverage}` }),
    integrity: Object.freeze({ value: integrity, label: `Integrity: ${integrity}` }),
    freshness: Object.freeze({
      value,
      label: live === null ? `Freshness: ${value} (at seal) — checking freshness…` : `Freshness: ${value}`,
      pending: live === null,
    }),
  });
}

// ---- no-clash gap explanation (mirror of clashtest/results/claim.js conjuncts) -------------------------

const FRESHNESS_STATES = ['current', 'stale', 'unverifiable'];
function freshnessState(f) {
  if (typeof f === 'string') return FRESHNESS_STATES.includes(f) ? f : null;
  if (f === null || typeof f !== 'object') return null;
  return FRESHNESS_STATES.includes(f.state) && Array.isArray(f.reasons) ? f.state : null;
}

const NOT_COMPLETED_TEXT = {
  cancelled: 'The run was stopped before it finished.',
  failed: 'The run failed before it finished.',
  invalidated: 'The model changed during the run.',
};

/**
 * Every failed conjunct of the §8.3 claim predicate EXCEPT `noResults` (results are positives, not a
 * gap), in claim.js order. `freshness` defaults to the at-seal `outcome.freshness`; pass the live
 * engine.getFreshness value when known. The digest-version conjunct cannot be evaluated here (the
 * known DIGEST_VERSION is not exported from the barrel), so it is read from Core's own claim result
 * when supplied (`qualifiers` carries `{kind:'digest-version'}` exactly when that conjunct failed).
 */
export function explainNoClashGaps(resultSet, { freshness, claim = null } = {}) {
  const outcome = resultSet?.outcome ?? {};
  const ledger = resultSet?.ledger ?? {};
  const provenance = resultSet?.provenance ?? {};
  const gaps = [];
  const add = (code, text) => gaps.push(Object.freeze({ code, text }));
  if (outcome.status !== 'completed') add('not-completed', NOT_COMPLETED_TEXT[outcome.status] ?? 'The run did not complete.');
  if (outcome.coverage !== 'full') add('partial-coverage', 'Coverage is partial — some parts of the scope were not evaluated.');
  if (outcome.integrity !== 'clean') add('caveated', 'Integrity is caveated — some evaluated parts carry caveats.');
  const fs = freshnessState(freshness === undefined ? outcome.freshness : freshness);
  if (fs !== 'current') {
    add('stale', fs === 'stale' ? STATEMENTS.STALE : 'Freshness could not be verified against the current models.');
  }
  if (claim !== null && list(claim.qualifiers).some((q) => q?.kind === 'digest-version')) {
    add('unknown-digest-version', 'The result set uses a digest version this engine does not know, so it cannot support a clearance.');
  }
  if (!(Number.isSafeInteger(ledger.pairSpaceTotal) && ledger.pairSpaceTotal > 0)) {
    add('zero-pair-space', 'There was nothing to compare — the evaluated pair space is empty.');
  }
  if (ledger.emptyOperand === true) add('empty-operand', 'Set A or Set B resolved to no elements.');
  const unresolved = list(ledger.unresolvedSelections).length;
  if (unresolved > 0) add('unresolved-selection', `${plural(unresolved, 'selection entry', 'selection entries')} could not be resolved.`);
  const unreachable = list(ledger.unreachablePopulation).length;
  if (unreachable > 0) add('unreachable-population', `Some elements could not be reached through the model's element tree (${plural(unreachable, 'record', 'records')}).`);
  const hierarchy = list(ledger.hierarchyInternal);
  if (hierarchy.length > 0 && (provenance.hierarchyInternalAcceptance ?? null) === null) {
    add('hierarchy-internal', 'Some pairs lie inside one element hierarchy (a parent and its own child) and were not evaluated.');
  }
  return gaps;
}

// ---- empty-result statements (spec §7.5) -----------------------------------------------------------------

function selectionText(selection, modelName) {
  const parts = list(selection?.entries).map((e) => (e?.kind === 'model'
    ? `whole model ${modelName(e.modelKey)}`
    : `${plural(list(e?.dbIds).length, 'element', 'elements')} of ${modelName(e?.modelKey)}`));
  return parts.length > 0 ? parts.join(', ') : 'nothing';
}

/** Scope summary shown under the claim (from the SEALED definition only). */
export function scopeSummary(resultSet, modelName = (k) => String(k)) {
  const d = resultSet?.definition ?? null;
  if (d === null) return [];
  return [`Set A: ${selectionText(d.selectionA, modelName)}`, `Set B: ${selectionText(d.selectionB, modelName)}`];
}

/**
 * The empty-results statement. `claim` = engine.assessNoClashClaim result (null while pending);
 * `freshness` = live engine.getFreshness result (null while pending). Returns null when there are
 * results (those are positives, spec §7.5 row 4) or no set at all.
 *
 * CLAIM GATE (review H1). Engine.getFreshness and engine.assessNoClashClaim each recompute live freshness, so
 * the two results can disagree (claim.allowed at t1, stale at t2). This function is the single, pure decision
 * over ONE pair — the caller (T17's controller snapshot) passes both halves committed together, never one half
 * from an earlier read:
 *   claim === null || freshness === null          ⇒ pending (STATEMENTS.CLAIM_PENDING)
 *   claim.allowed === true ∧ state === 'current'  ⇒ claim / qualified-claim   (the ONLY clearance wording)
 *   completed stale | unverifiable                ⇒ 'stale' non-claim (even if claim.allowed was true)
 *   anything else (disallowed, malformed read)    ⇒ non-claim
 * `freshness` is interpreted ONCE (`liveState`), so the gate and the gap list can never see different values.
 */
export function emptyStatement({ resultSet, claim = null, freshness = null, modelName = (k) => String(k) }) {
  if (!resultSet || list(resultSet.results).length > 0) return null;
  const make = (kind, text, lines) => Object.freeze({ kind, text, lines: Object.freeze(lines) });
  const liveState = freshnessState(freshness);
  if (claim !== null && claim.allowed === true && liveState === 'current') {
    return claim.unqualified === true
      ? make('claim', STATEMENTS.CLAIM, scopeSummary(resultSet, modelName))
      : make('qualified-claim', STATEMENTS.QUALIFIED_CLAIM, list(resultSet.ledger?.hierarchyInternal).map(
        (h) => `${modelName(h.modelKey)}: ${plural(h.rootCount, 'root', 'roots')}, ${plural(h.ownerCount, 'owner', 'owners')}`));
  }
  const gaps = explainNoClashGaps(resultSet, { freshness: freshness ?? undefined, claim });   // pending ⇒ explain from the at-seal value
  if (claim === null || freshness === null) return make('non-claim', STATEMENTS.CLAIM_PENDING, gaps.map((g) => g.text));
  if (liveState === 'stale' || liveState === 'unverifiable') {
    return make('stale', STATEMENTS.NON_CLAIM, [STATEMENTS.STALE,
      ...list(freshness.reasons).filter((r) => typeof r === 'string').map((r) => `Reason: ${r}`),
      ...gaps.filter((g) => g.code !== 'stale').map((g) => g.text)]);
  }
  const lines = gaps.map((g) => g.text);
  return make('non-claim', STATEMENTS.NON_CLAIM, lines.length > 0 ? lines : [STATEMENTS.NO_CONFIRMATION]);
}

// ---- sealed failures (spec §13) -----------------------------------------------------------------------

const UNEXPECTED = new Set(['internal-error', 'world-disposed']);
const PLANNING_TEXT = {
  'model-not-bound': 'A model in the test is not loaded or not registered.',
  'element-unresolvable': 'An element in the selection no longer exists.',
  'owner-mapping-mismatch': "The model's element ownership could not be mapped consistently.",
  'hierarchy-overlap': 'Set A and Set B contain a parent and its own child.',
  'plan-too-large': 'The test is too large to plan — narrow the selections.',
  'test-unavailable': 'The test definition was unavailable.',
  'definition-invalid': 'The test definition was rejected.',
  'schema-unsupported': 'The test uses a definition version this engine does not support.',
  'migration-failed': 'The test definition could not be migrated.',
  cancelled: 'The run was stopped while it was being planned.',
};
const ENUMERATION_LIKELY_CAUSES = Object.freeze([
  "Couldn't read the model's element tree.",
  'Likely causes (not confirmed by the engine): the model is still loading; the whole model is larger than the collision engine accepts in one pass; an element exceeds the extraction bounds.',
  'Action: wait for the model to finish loading, or narrow the scope.',
]);
const UNIT_CAUSE_TEXT = {
  'extraction-limit': 'an element exceeded the extraction bounds',
  'capacity-exceeded': 'collision capacity was exceeded',
  'unit-cap': 'the run reached its unit limit',
  'object-tree-unavailable': "the model's element tree was unavailable",
  'target-too-large': 'the target was too large',
  'model-evicted': 'a model was unloaded',
  'stale-placement': 'the model placement kept changing',
  'scope-drift': 'the model changed',
  'scope-unverifiable': 'the model state could not be verified',
  'input-changed': 'the model moved',
  'result-cap': 'the result limit was reached',
  'internal-error': 'an internal error occurred',
  'world-disposed': 'the collision world was disposed',
  cancelled: 'the run was stopped',
  'run-failed': 'the run failed',
};
const NOT_EVALUATED = new Set(['failed', 'skipped', 'discarded', 'not-run']);

function causesOf(resultSet) {
  const ledger = resultSet?.ledger ?? {};
  const planning = [...new Set(list(ledger.planningGaps).map((g) => g?.cause).filter((c) => typeof c === 'string'))];
  const units = list(ledger.units).filter((u) => NOT_EVALUATED.has(u?.outcome));
  const reasons = list(resultSet?.outcome?.reasons);
  const unitCauses = new Set(units.map((u) => u.cause).filter((c) => typeof c === 'string'));
  for (const r of reasons) if (typeof r === 'string' && r.startsWith('unit:')) unitCauses.add(r.slice(5));
  for (const r of reasons) if (typeof r === 'string' && r.startsWith('planning:') && !planning.includes(r.slice(9))) planning.push(r.slice(9));
  return { planning, units, unitCauses };
}

/** "N parts could not be evaluated (cause)" lines, one per distinct cause, in cause order. */
export function unitGapLines(resultSet) {
  const byCause = new Map();
  for (const u of causesOf(resultSet).units) {
    const c = typeof u.cause === 'string' ? u.cause : 'unknown';
    byCause.set(c, (byCause.get(c) ?? 0) + 1);
  }
  return [...byCause.keys()].sort().map((c) => `${plural(byCause.get(c), 'part', 'parts')} could not be evaluated (${UNIT_CAUSE_TEXT[c] ?? c}).`);
}

function resultCapHeadline(resultSet) {
  const cap = resultSet?.provenance?.runOptions?.maxResultsPerRun;
  return `Too many clashes — stopped at the result limit (${Number.isFinite(cap) ? fmtInt(cap) : 'the run\'s result limit'}).`;
}

function failedDetails(resultSet) {
  const { planning, unitCauses } = causesOf(resultSet);
  if (planning.some((c) => UNEXPECTED.has(c)) || [...unitCauses].some((c) => UNEXPECTED.has(c))) {
    return { headline: STATEMENTS.ENGINE_FAILED, details: [] };
  }
  if (unitCauses.has('result-cap')) {
    const soft = resultSet?.definition?.mode === 'clearance';
    return {
      headline: resultCapHeadline(resultSet),
      details: [
        'Retained results come from whole parts evaluated before the limit.',
        soft
          ? 'Action: narrow the selection, or reduce the clearance — a larger clearance broadens matching and can reproduce or worsen the failure.'
          : 'Action: narrow the selection.',
      ],
    };
  }
  if (planning.includes('enumeration-failed')) {
    const others = planning.filter((c) => c !== 'enumeration-failed').map((c) => PLANNING_TEXT[c] ?? c);
    return { headline: ENUMERATION_LIKELY_CAUSES[0], details: [...ENUMERATION_LIKELY_CAUSES.slice(1), ...others] };
  }
  if (planning.length > 0) {
    // Duplicate rows (e.g. two owner-mapping-mismatch gaps, frozen-Core residual M2) collapse to one line.
    return { headline: 'The test could not be planned.', details: planning.map((c) => PLANNING_TEXT[c] ?? c) };
  }
  return { headline: 'The run failed.', details: [] };
}

/** Headline for a finished run (spec §7.3). `resultSet` refines `failed` by cause (§13); pass
 *  `resultSet: null` when Core's fallback seal failed. */
export function runHeadline({ status, total, coverage, resultSet }) {
  const n = Number.isFinite(total) ? total : 0;
  switch (status) {
    case 'completed':
      return `Completed — ${plural(n, 'clash', 'clashes')}${coverage === 'partial' ? ' (partial coverage)' : ''}`;
    case 'cancelled':
      return n > 0 ? `Stopped — partial results (${fmtInt(n)})` : 'Stopped before any results';
    case 'invalidated':
      return STATEMENTS.MODEL_CHANGED;
    case 'failed':
      if (resultSet === null) return STATEMENTS.NO_RESULT_SET;
      return resultSet ? failedDetails(resultSet).headline : 'The run failed.';
    default:
      return 'The run ended.';
  }
}

/** §13 table for a sealed set: headline by status/cause, detail lines (planning causes, unit-level
 *  gaps, truncated diagnostics) and a note about retained results. */
export function mapSealedFailure(resultSet) {
  if (!resultSet) return Object.freeze({ headline: STATEMENTS.NO_RESULT_SET, details: Object.freeze([]), retainedNote: null });
  const status = resultSet.outcome?.status;
  const total = list(resultSet.results).length;
  let headline;
  let details = [];
  if (status === 'failed') ({ headline, details } = failedDetails(resultSet));
  else headline = runHeadline({ status, total, coverage: resultSet.outcome?.coverage, resultSet });
  if (status === 'cancelled' && total === 0) {
    const planningCancel = causesOf(resultSet).planning.includes('cancelled');
    if (planningCancel) details = [PLANNING_TEXT.cancelled];
  }
  const unitLines = unitGapLines(resultSet);
  const allDetails = [...details, ...unitLines];
  if (resultSet.diagnostics?.truncated === true) allDetails.push(STATEMENTS.DIAGNOSTICS_TRUNCATED);
  const partialish = status !== 'completed' || resultSet.outcome?.coverage !== 'full';
  const retainedNote = total > 0 && partialish
    ? `${plural(total, 'clash', 'clashes')} found ${status === 'completed' ? '' : 'before the run ended '}are valid; parts that were not evaluated are unknown.`
    : null;
  return Object.freeze({ headline, details: Object.freeze(allDetails), retainedNote });
}

// ---- admission errors (startRun threw; spec §7.1, §13) -------------------------------------------------

/** `heldRunId` = the runId of the set the Panel currently holds (null if none). The Release-and-retry
 *  action is offered ONLY when a ResultCapacityError names that set among its blockers. */
export function mapAdmissionError(error, { heldRunId = null } = {}) {
  const name = typeof error?.name === 'string' ? error.name : '';
  const out = (text, action = null) => Object.freeze({ text, action });
  switch (name) {
    case 'InvalidTestDefinitionError':
      return out('The test setup is invalid — fix the highlighted fields and run again.');
    case 'UnsupportedSchemaVersionError':
      return out('The test uses a definition version this clash engine does not support.');
    case 'StoreNotConfiguredError':
      return out('This run needs a store that the clash engine does not have configured.');
    case 'InvalidOptionsError':
      return out('The clash engine rejected the run options.');
    case 'ResultCapacityError': {
      const blockers = [...list(error.active), ...list(error.retained), ...list(error.held).map((h) => h?.runId)];
      return heldRunId !== null && blockers.includes(heldRunId)
        ? out('The clash engine is at capacity. Clear previous results and try again.', 'release-and-retry')
        : out('The clash engine is at capacity: its result slots are held by other runs. Try again after they are released.');
    }
    case 'RunQueueFullError':
      return out('The clash engine is at capacity: too many runs are waiting. Try again when they finish.');
    case 'EngineDisposedError':
      return out('The clash engine has been shut down. Reload the page to run tests again.');
    default: {
      const msg = typeof error?.message === 'string' && error.message !== '' ? `: ${error.message}` : '.';
      return out(`The run could not be started${msg}`);
    }
  }
}

// ---- banners -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Banner = {id, kind:'info'|'warning'|'error', text, details?}. `terminal` = runMachine terminal;
 *  `persistence` = the displayed set's current persistence `{state}` (null if unknown). */
export function bannersFor({ terminal, resultSet, freshness = null, setupChanged = false, persistence = null }) {
  const banners = [];
  const push = (id, kind, text, details) => banners.push(Object.freeze({ id, kind, text, ...(details && details.length ? { details: Object.freeze(details) } : {}) }));
  if (terminal && terminal.resultSetPresent === false) push('no-result-set', 'error', STATEMENTS.NO_RESULT_SET);
  if (resultSet) {
    const status = resultSet.outcome?.status;
    const report = mapSealedFailure(resultSet);
    if (status === 'failed') push('failed', 'error', report.headline, report.details);
    if (status === 'invalidated') push('invalidated', 'warning', STATEMENTS.MODEL_CHANGED, report.details);
    if (status === 'cancelled') push('cancelled', 'info', report.headline, report.details);
    if (status === 'completed' && resultSet.outcome?.coverage !== 'full') {
      push('partial', 'warning', 'Coverage is partial — results cover only the parts that were evaluated.',
        [...unitGapLines(resultSet), ...(report.retainedNote ? [report.retainedNote] : [])]);
    }
    const live = freshnessState(freshness);
    const effective = live ?? freshnessState(resultSet.outcome?.freshness);
    if (effective === 'stale' || effective === 'unverifiable') {
      const reasons = live !== null ? list(freshness.reasons).filter((r) => typeof r === 'string') : [];
      push('stale', 'warning', STATEMENTS.STALE, [...reasons.map((r) => `Reason: ${r}`), 'Run the test again to refresh.']);
    }
  }
  if (setupChanged === true) push('setup-changed', 'info', STATEMENTS.SETUP_CHANGED);
  if (persistence && (persistence.state === 'failed' || persistence.state === 'skipped') && resultSet) {
    push('held-unsaved', 'info', STATEMENTS.HELD_IN_MEMORY);
  }
  return banners;
}

// ---- diagnostics export (spec §8.4, §13) -------------------------------------------------------------

/** Plain JSON of `outcome`, `ledger.planningGaps` and `diagnostics` (its `truncated` flag preserved). */
export function diagnosticsExport(resultSet) {
  if (!resultSet) return JSON.stringify({ resultSet: null }, null, 2);
  return JSON.stringify({
    runId: resultSet.runId ?? null,
    outcome: resultSet.outcome ?? null,
    planningGaps: resultSet.ledger?.planningGaps ?? [],
    diagnostics: resultSet.diagnostics ?? null,
  }, null, 2);
}
```

```js
// clashpanel/core/filters.js
//
// Spec §10.1: every v1 filter is a Panel-side PURE predicate over the frozen `results[]` — no Core
// derivation per interaction (AC-P4). The only Core-derived input is the cached `caveated` mask
// (one derivations.filter per run, owned by the controller). Passes run in LIST_CHUNK_SIZE chunks
// with a scheduler yield between chunks and a supersession check per chunk; text debounce is the
// controller's job. Output: ascending canonical indexes in a Uint32Array (bounded memory).
import { LIST_CHUNK_SIZE } from './constants.js';

/** Shown when the "unverified" filter is on but the caveated mask is pending or failed (plain text). */
export const FILTER_MASK_UNAVAILABLE_TEXT = 'The “unverified” filter couldn\'t be evaluated for this run — turn it off to continue.';

export const EMPTY_FILTER_SPEC = Object.freeze({
  text: '', models: Object.freeze([]), elementOnly: null, maxGap: null, unverified: false, hasLocation: false,
});

export function isFilterActive(spec) {
  if (!spec) return false;
  return (typeof spec.text === 'string' && spec.text.trim() !== '')
    || (Array.isArray(spec.models) && spec.models.length > 0)
    || spec.elementOnly != null
    || Number.isFinite(spec.maxGap)
    || spec.unverified === true
    || spec.hasLocation === true;
}

/** Max gap input (Soft only): a finite number ≥ 0 and ≤ the run's clearance. Increasing the
 *  clearance needs a rerun (setup-changed), so values above it are rejected, never silently clamped. */
export function parseMaxGap(text, clearance) {
  const raw = typeof text === 'string' ? text.trim() : '';
  if (raw === '') return { value: null, error: null };
  const n = Number(raw);
  if (!Number.isFinite(n) || n < 0) return { value: null, error: 'Enter a number of 0 or more.' };
  if (Number.isFinite(clearance) && n > clearance) {
    return { value: null, error: `Max gap cannot exceed the run's clearance (${clearance}); run again with a larger clearance instead.` };
  }
  return { value: n, error: null };
}

export function createRecordPredicate(spec, { caveatedIds = null, labelText = () => '' } = {}) {
  const needle = typeof spec?.text === 'string' ? spec.text.trim().toLowerCase() : '';
  const digits = needle.startsWith('#') ? needle.slice(1) : needle;
  const numeric = /^\d+$/.test(digits);
  const models = Array.isArray(spec?.models) && spec.models.length > 0 ? new Set(spec.models) : null;
  const el = spec?.elementOnly ?? null;
  const maxGap = Number.isFinite(spec?.maxGap) ? spec.maxGap : null;
  const unverified = spec?.unverified === true;
  const hasLocation = spec?.hasLocation === true;
  if (unverified && !(caveatedIds instanceof Set)) {
    throw new TypeError('createRecordPredicate: the unverified filter needs the caveated mask (runFilterPass reports mask-missing)');
  }
  const sideText = (ref) => (numeric && String(ref.dbId).includes(digits)) || labelText(ref).includes(needle);
  return (record) => {
    const { first, second } = record.pair;
    if (models !== null && !models.has(first.modelKey) && !models.has(second.modelKey)) return false;
    if (el !== null && !((first.modelKey === el.modelKey && first.dbId === el.dbId)
      || (second.modelKey === el.modelKey && second.dbId === el.dbId))) return false;
    if (maxGap !== null && record.mode === 'clearance' && !(record.evidence.distance <= maxGap)) return false;
    if (unverified && !caveatedIds.has(record.resultId)) return false;
    if (hasLocation && record.flags?.witnessUnavailable === true) return false;
    if (needle !== '' && !sideText(first) && !sideText(second)) return false;
    return true;
  };
}

/** Sliced pass over the index. Returns the matching canonical indexes (ascending); 'superseded' as soon as
 *  isCurrent() is false at a chunk boundary (or before the fast path); 'mask-missing' when the unverified
 *  filter is on but the caveated mask is pending or failed — NEVER an empty result in that case. */
export async function runFilterPass({ index, spec, caveatedIds = null, labelText, scheduler, isCurrent = () => true }) {
  const count = index.count;
  if (!isCurrent()) return 'superseded';
  if (spec?.unverified === true && !(caveatedIds instanceof Set)) return 'mask-missing';
  if (!isFilterActive(spec)) {                               // fast path: everything, canonical order
    const all = new Uint32Array(count);
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 1) all[i] = i;
    return all;
  }
  const predicate = createRecordPredicate(spec, { caveatedIds, labelText });
  const out = new Uint32Array(count);
  let n = 0;
  for (let start = 0; start < count; start += LIST_CHUNK_SIZE) {
    if (!isCurrent()) return 'superseded';
    const end = Math.min(count, start + LIST_CHUNK_SIZE);
    for (let i = start; i < end; i += 1) if (predicate(index.at(i))) { out[n] = i; n += 1; }
    if (end < count) await scheduler.yield();
  }
  if (!isCurrent()) return 'superseded';
  return out.slice(0, n);                                    // a copy: the full-size scratch buffer is dropped
}
```

// test/clashpanel/core/grouping.test.mjs — Task 13 (spec §10.2, AC-P4)
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { computeElementGroups, filterGroups, sortGroups, matchIdsFrom, groupCountText, MULTI_VALUED_NOTE, GROUPING_UNAVAILABLE_TEXT } from '../../../clashpanel/core/grouping.js';
import { buildResultIndex } from '../../../clashpanel/core/resultIndex.js';
import { createDerivationQueue } from '../../../clashpanel/core/derivationQueue.js';
import { createGeneration } from '../../../clashpanel/core/generation.js';
import { DERIVATION_BUSY_MAX_RETRIES, DERIVATION_BUSY_RETRY_MS } from '../../../clashpanel/core/constants.js';
import { createFakeScheduler } from '../support/fakeScheduler.mjs';
import { createClashTestEngine, GroupingTooLargeError, DerivationBusyError } from '../../../clashtest/index.js';
import { createEngineWorld } from '../../clashtest/support/engineWorld.mjs';
import { createFakeClock } from '../../clashtest/support/fakeClock.mjs';
import { sealedSet } from '../../clashtest/support/resultSetFixtures.mjs';

// Hand-built multi-valued set: r0 (A1–B9), r1 (A2–B9), r2 (A1–B8). Element B9 holds r0+r1, A1 holds r0+r2.
const ref = (modelKey, dbId) => ({ modelKey, dbId });
const rec = (id, a, b) => ({ resultId: id, pair: { first: a, second: b }, mode: 'volume-overlap', evidence: { witness: null }, flags: {}, unitId: 'u' });
const SET = { runId: 'run-g', results: [rec('r0', ref('A', 1), ref('B', 9)), rec('r1', ref('A', 2), ref('B', 9)), rec('r2', ref('A', 1), ref('B', 8))], definition: { mode: 'volume-overlap' }, provenance: { models: [] } };
const coreGroups = () => ({ facets: [{ facetId: 'element', params: {}, multiValued: true }], unavailable: [], total: 3, memberships: 6, groups: [
  { groupId: 'gA1', path: ['gA1'], facetId: 'element', params: {}, value: ref('A', 1), count: 2, members: ['r0', 'r2'] },
  { groupId: 'gA2', path: ['gA2'], facetId: 'element', params: {}, value: ref('A', 2), count: 1, members: ['r1'] },
  { groupId: 'gB8', path: ['gB8'], facetId: 'element', params: {}, value: ref('B', 8), count: 1, members: ['r2'] },
  { groupId: 'gB9', path: ['gB9'], facetId: 'element', params: {}, value: ref('B', 9), count: 2, members: ['r0', 'r1'] },
] });
/** Drives the fake scheduler's retry timers (Task 7 busy back-off) until `p` settles; bounded. */
async function settleWithTimers(p, scheduler) {
  let done = false;
  p.then(() => { done = true; }, () => { done = true; });
  for (let i = 0; i < 10 * (DERIVATION_BUSY_MAX_RETRIES + 1) && !done; i += 1) {
    await new Promise((r) => setImmediate(r));
    if (!done) await scheduler.advance(DERIVATION_BUSY_RETRY_MS);
  }
  return p;
}
function world(groupBy) {
  const calls = [];
  const engine = { derivations: { groupBy: async (set, facets, opts) => { calls.push([set, facets, Object.keys(opts)]); return groupBy(calls.length); } } };
  const scheduler = createFakeScheduler();
  const generation = createGeneration();
  const queue = createDerivationQueue({ scheduler, generation });
  return { engine, calls, scheduler, generation, queue };
}

test('one groupBy(set, [\'element\'], {signal}) per (generation, spec); a second request is served from the queue cache', async () => {
  const w = world(() => coreGroups());
  const a = await computeElementGroups({ queue: w.queue, engine: w.engine, resultSet: SET });
  const b = await computeElementGroups({ queue: w.queue, engine: w.engine, resultSet: SET });
  assert.equal(a.status, 'ok');
  assert.deepEqual(b, a);
  assert.equal(w.calls.length, 1);
  assert.equal(w.calls[0][0], SET);
  assert.deepEqual(w.calls[0][1], ['element']);
  assert.deepEqual(w.calls[0][2], ['signal'], 'closed options bag: signal only');
  w.generation.bump();
  await computeElementGroups({ queue: w.queue, engine: w.engine, resultSet: SET });
  assert.equal(w.calls.length, 2, 'a new generation computes again');
});

});

  assert.match(GROUPING_UNAVAILABLE_TEXT['too-large'], /showing the flat list/);

});

```js
// clashpanel/core/grouping.js
//
// Spec §10.2: Group by Element is ONE Core call — engine.derivations.groupBy(set, ['element'],
// {signal}) — per (generation, spec), through the single-flight derivation queue (Task 7), cached
// as a table. Everything after it (filter intersection, n-of-m counts, re-sorting) is Panel-side
// presentation. The `element` facet is multi-valued: a clash is listed under BOTH of its elements,
// so group counts do not sum to the result count. GroupingTooLargeError / DerivationBusyError (after
// the queue's bounded retries) / any other error ⇒ "grouping unavailable, showing the flat list".

export const GROUPING_UNAVAILABLE_TEXT = Object.freeze({
  'too-large': 'Grouping unavailable for a set this large — showing the flat list.',
  error: 'Grouping is unavailable right now — showing the flat list.',
});
export const MULTI_VALUED_NOTE = 'Each clash is listed under both of its elements, so group counts do not add up to the number of clashes.';

export async function computeElementGroups({ queue, engine, resultSet, priority = 3 }) {
  const outcome = await queue.submit({
    key: `groupBy:element:${resultSet.runId}`,
    priority,
    job: (signal) => engine.derivations.groupBy(resultSet, ['element'], { signal }),
  });
  if (outcome.status === 'superseded') return { status: 'superseded' };
  if (outcome.status !== 'ok') {
    return { status: 'unavailable', reason: outcome.error?.name === 'GroupingTooLargeError' ? 'too-large' : 'error' };
  }
  const raw = outcome.value;
  if (!raw || !Array.isArray(raw.groups) || (Array.isArray(raw.unavailable) && raw.unavailable.length > 0)) {
    return { status: 'unavailable', reason: 'error' };
  }
  const groups = raw.groups.map((g) => Object.freeze({
    groupId: g.groupId, ref: g.value, count: g.count, memberIds: g.members,   // Core arrays referenced, not copied
  }));
  return { status: 'ok', table: Object.freeze({ groups: Object.freeze(groups), memberships: raw.memberships, total: raw.total }) };
}

/** Result-id set of a filter pass (the mask intersected with group members). */
export function matchIdsFrom(matching, index) {
  const ids = new Set();
  for (let k = 0; k < matching.length; k += 1) ids.add(index.at(matching[k]).resultId);
  return ids;
}

/** `matchIds` null = no filter active. Groups whose filtered count is 0 are dropped only then. */
export function filterGroups(table, { matchIds = null, index }) {
  const out = [];
  for (const g of table.groups) {
    const memberIndexes = [];
    for (const id of g.memberIds) {
      if (matchIds !== null && !matchIds.has(id)) continue;
      const i = index.indexOfResultId(id);
      if (i >= 0) memberIndexes.push(i);
    }
    // No sort: Core pushes members while walking results[] in canonical order (derive/groupBy.js `place`),
    // so memberIndexes is already ascending (pinned against the real groupBy in the test).
    if (matchIds !== null && memberIndexes.length === 0) continue;
    out.push(Object.freeze({ groupId: g.groupId, ref: g.ref, count: g.count, filteredCount: memberIndexes.length, memberIndexes }));
  }
  return out;
}

/** 'core' keeps Core order (ElementRef order); 'count-desc' by filtered count; 'label' by labelOf(ref).
 *  Stable: ties keep Core order. Returns a new array. */
export function sortGroups(groups, sortKey, labelOf = () => '') {
  const withPos = groups.map((g, pos) => ({ g, pos }));
  if (sortKey === 'count-desc') withPos.sort((a, b) => (b.g.filteredCount - a.g.filteredCount) || (a.pos - b.pos));
  else if (sortKey === 'label') {
    const labels = withPos.map(({ g }) => String(labelOf(g.ref)).toLowerCase());
    withPos.sort((a, b) => (labels[a.pos] < labels[b.pos] ? -1 : labels[a.pos] > labels[b.pos] ? 1 : a.pos - b.pos));
  }
  return withPos.map(({ g }) => g);
}

/** Header count text "n of m" (filtered of total). */
export function groupCountText(group) {
  return group.filteredCount === group.count ? `${group.count}` : `${group.filteredCount} of ${group.count}`;
}
```

### Task 14: Ordered list, sorting, pagination, occurrence navigation

**Tier:** [A] format-agnostic headless

**Files:**
- Create: `clashpanel/core/orderedList.js`
- Modify: `test/clashpanel/scaffold.test.mjs` (append `'core/orderedList.js'` to `EXPECTED_MODULES`)
- Test: `test/clashpanel/core/orderedList.test.mjs`

**Scope note:** the controller (T18) stores the selected OCCURRENCE `{groupId, resultId}` and `navScope`; this module answers position/page/neighbor questions against one immutable index. Group sorts (`group-count`, `group-label`) are applied to the `groups` input via T13's `sortGroups` before building; `sortKey` here is the member/flat order (`default` | `gap-asc`, the latter only when `index.isSoft`). `storage` exposes the typed arrays for the bounded-memory assertions (T21 reuses it). `navScope` is honoured only while that group is expanded; otherwise navigation falls back to the rendered whole list, so `navNeighbor` never returns an unrendered occurrence. Index construction is synchronous and one-shot per user action — NOT sliced: the typed-array fill is linear; the gap sort and group sort are comparison sorts (O(n log n)); their duration on large sets is a PG-3 measurement item with no further complexity or "never blocks" claim (only predicate/label passes are sliced).

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `ResultIndex` (T10: `at`, `indexOfResultId`, `count`, `isSoft`); `FilteredGroups` from T13 `filterGroups`/`sortGroups`; `matching: Uint32Array` from T12 `runFilterPass`.
- Produces: `buildOrderedIndex({view, matching, index, sortKey, groups?, expanded?}) -> {view, length, resultCount, storage:{kinds:Uint8Array|null, canonical:Uint32Array, groupOrdinals:Uint32Array|null}, entryAt(i), positionOf(occurrence), navNeighbor(occurrence|null, 1|-1, navScope|null) -> Occurrence|null}`; `pageSlice(ordered, page, pageSize)`; `pageOfPosition(position, pageSize) -> number (-1 if not in list)`; `clampPage(page, length, pageSize)`.

**Depends on:** T10, T12, T13.

```js
// clashpanel/core/orderedList.js
//
// Spec §10.3, §12.1-§12.3: one immutable ORDERED INDEX per (filter, sort, grouping, expansion)
// state — typed arrays only (O(n) memory, no per-record objects); entries are materialized on
// demand for the one rendered page. Flat view = canonical indexes (default = Core order; gap-asc =
// a stable permutation by evidence.distance, Soft only, ties by canonical index). Grouped view =
// [group header, its members if expanded, …]. Selection identity for the list is the OCCURRENCE
// {groupId, resultId} (§12.2): positions/pages are computed from THAT occurrence, never from the
// first occurrence of the resultId. Prev/Next never wrap; a selection outside the list steps to
// the first (Next) or last (Prev) result entry.

const KIND_RESULT = 0;
const KIND_GROUP = 1;

/** Stable gap-ascending permutation of `canon` (canonical indexes); non-clearance records last. */
function gapSorted(canon, index) {
  const m = canon.length;
  const pos = new Uint32Array(m);
  const dist = new Float64Array(m);
  for (let k = 0; k < m; k += 1) {
    pos[k] = k;
    const d = index.at(canon[k])?.evidence?.distance;
    dist[k] = Number.isFinite(d) ? d : Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
  }
  // A comparison sort (O(n log n)), synchronous and one-shot per user action (not sliced); its duration on a
  // large set is a PG-3 measurement item — no "never blocks" claim. The canonical-index tie-break makes it stable.
  pos.sort((a, b) => (dist[a] - dist[b]) || (canon[a] - canon[b]));
  const out = new Uint32Array(m);
  for (let k = 0; k < m; k += 1) out[k] = canon[pos[k]];
  return out;
}

function orderMembers(memberIndexes, index, sortKey) {
  const canon = Uint32Array.from(memberIndexes);
  return sortKey === 'gap-asc' && index.isSoft ? gapSorted(canon, index) : canon;
}

export function buildOrderedIndex({ view, matching, index, sortKey = 'default', groups = [], expanded = new Set() }) {
  const gapSort = sortKey === 'gap-asc' && index.isSoft === true;
  if (view !== 'grouped') return buildFlat(gapSort ? gapSorted(matching, index) : matching, index);
  return buildGrouped(groups, expanded, index, sortKey);
}

function buildFlat(order, index) {
  const length = order.length;
  let inverse = null;                                         // canonical -> position, built lazily once
  const positionOfCanonical = (c) => {
    if (inverse === null) {
      inverse = new Int32Array(index.count).fill(-1);
      for (let p = 0; p < length; p += 1) inverse[order[p]] = p;
    }
    return c >= 0 && c < inverse.length ? inverse[c] : -1;
  };
  const occurrenceAt = (p) => ({ groupId: null, resultId: index.at(order[p]).resultId });
  const positionOf = (occ) => (occ ? positionOfCanonical(index.indexOfResultId(occ.resultId)) : -1);
  return Object.freeze({
    view: 'flat',
    length,
    resultCount: length,
    storage: Object.freeze({ kinds: null, canonical: order, groupOrdinals: null }),
    entryAt(i) { return i >= 0 && i < length ? { kind: 'result', canonicalIndex: order[i], groupId: null } : undefined; },
    positionOf,
    navNeighbor(occ, dir) {
      if (length === 0) return null;
      const p = positionOf(occ);
      if (p === -1) return occurrenceAt(dir > 0 ? 0 : length - 1);
      const q = p + (dir > 0 ? 1 : -1);
      return q >= 0 && q < length ? occurrenceAt(q) : null;
    },
  });
}

function buildGrouped(groups, expanded, index, sortKey) {
  const memberOrders = groups.map((g) => orderMembers(g.memberIndexes, index, sortKey));
  let length = groups.length;
  for (let gi = 0; gi < groups.length; gi += 1) if (expanded.has(groups[gi].groupId)) length += memberOrders[gi].length;
  const kinds = new Uint8Array(length);
  const canonical = new Uint32Array(length);
  const groupOrdinals = new Uint32Array(length);
  const headerPos = new Map();                                 // groupId -> header position (O(groups))
  const ordinalOf = new Map();
  let p = 0;
  let resultCount = 0;
  for (let gi = 0; gi < groups.length; gi += 1) {
    const g = groups[gi];
    headerPos.set(g.groupId, p);
    ordinalOf.set(g.groupId, gi);
    kinds[p] = KIND_GROUP; groupOrdinals[p] = gi; p += 1;
    if (!expanded.has(g.groupId)) continue;
    const members = memberOrders[gi];
    for (let k = 0; k < members.length; k += 1) {
      kinds[p] = KIND_RESULT; canonical[p] = members[k]; groupOrdinals[p] = gi; p += 1; resultCount += 1;
    }
  }
  const occurrenceAt = (q) => ({ groupId: groups[groupOrdinals[q]].groupId, resultId: index.at(canonical[q]).resultId });
  function positionOf(occ) {
    if (!occ) return -1;
    const c = index.indexOfResultId(occ.resultId);
    if (c < 0) return -1;
    if (occ.groupId === null || occ.groupId === undefined) {  // selected in the flat view: first rendered occurrence
      for (let q = 0; q < length; q += 1) if (kinds[q] === KIND_RESULT && canonical[q] === c) return q;
      return -1;
    }
    const h = headerPos.get(occ.groupId);
    if (h === undefined || !expanded.has(occ.groupId)) return -1;
    const n = memberOrders[ordinalOf.get(occ.groupId)].length;
    for (let q = h + 1; q <= h + n; q += 1) if (canonical[q] === c) return q;
    return -1;
  }
  function navNeighbor(occ, dir, navScope = null) {
    const step = dir > 0 ? 1 : -1;
    // Prev/Next inside the group the user is reading — ONLY while that group is expanded (rendered); a
    // collapsed/unknown scope falls back to the whole list so the result is always a rendered occurrence.
    if (navScope !== null && ordinalOf.has(navScope) && expanded.has(navScope)) {
      const members = memberOrders[ordinalOf.get(navScope)];
      if (members.length === 0) return null;
      const c = occ ? index.indexOfResultId(occ.resultId) : -1;
      let k = -1;
      for (let j = 0; j < members.length; j += 1) if (members[j] === c) { k = j; break; }
      const at = (j) => ({ groupId: navScope, resultId: index.at(members[j]).resultId });
      if (k === -1) return at(step > 0 ? 0 : members.length - 1);
      const j = k + step;
      return j >= 0 && j < members.length ? at(j) : null;
    }
    const p0 = positionOf(occ);
    if (p0 === -1) {                                           // not in the list: first / last result entry
      for (let q = step > 0 ? 0 : length - 1; q >= 0 && q < length; q += step) if (kinds[q] === KIND_RESULT) return occurrenceAt(q);
      return null;
    }
    for (let q = p0 + step; q >= 0 && q < length; q += step) if (kinds[q] === KIND_RESULT) return occurrenceAt(q);
    return null;                                               // no wrap
  }
  return Object.freeze({
    view: 'grouped',
    length,
    resultCount,
    storage: Object.freeze({ kinds, canonical, groupOrdinals }),
    entryAt(i) {
      if (!(i >= 0 && i < length)) return undefined;
      const groupId = groups[groupOrdinals[i]].groupId;
      return kinds[i] === KIND_GROUP ? { kind: 'group', groupId } : { kind: 'result', canonicalIndex: canonical[i], groupId };
    },
    positionOf,
    navNeighbor,
  });
}

export function clampPage(page, length, pageSize) {
  const count = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(length / pageSize));
  if (!Number.isFinite(page)) return 0;
  return Math.min(count - 1, Math.max(0, Math.trunc(page)));
}

export function pageOfPosition(position, pageSize) {
  return position >= 0 ? Math.floor(position / pageSize) : -1;   // -1: not in the list ⇒ the page does not jump
}

export function pageSlice(ordered, page, pageSize) {
  const p = clampPage(page, ordered.length, pageSize);
  const out = [];
  for (let i = p * pageSize, end = Math.min(ordered.length, (p + 1) * pageSize); i < end; i += 1) out.push(ordered.entryAt(i));
  return out;
}
```

// test/clashpanel/support/settle.mjs
// Deterministic settling for controller tests: alternates macrotask turns (setImmediate — lets promise chains and
// real-engine timers progress) with `scheduler.advance(0)` (releases fake-scheduler work due "now", e.g. a yield
// that the fake implements as a 0 ms timer). Never advances fake time beyond 0 and asserts nothing about
// wall-clock duration.
const turn = () => new Promise((resolve) => setImmediate(resolve));

export async function settle(scheduler, rounds = 30) {
  for (let i = 0; i < rounds; i += 1) {
    await turn();
    if (scheduler && typeof scheduler.advance === 'function') await scheduler.advance(0);
  }
}

/** Settles until `promise` resolves (or rejects); throws if it is still pending after `maxRounds`. */
export async function drain(scheduler, promise, maxRounds = 20000) {
  let state = 'pending';
  let value;
  let error;
  promise.then((v) => { state = 'fulfilled'; value = v; }, (e) => { state = 'rejected'; error = e; });
  for (let i = 0; i < maxRounds && state === 'pending'; i += 1) await settle(scheduler, 1);
  if (state === 'pending') throw new Error(`drain: promise still pending after ${maxRounds} rounds`);
  if (state === 'rejected') throw error;
  return value;
}

/** Settles until `predicate()` is truthy; throws after `maxRounds` (a bounded ROUND count, not a time limit). */
export async function until(scheduler, predicate, maxRounds = 20000) {
  for (let i = 0; i < maxRounds; i += 1) {
    if (predicate()) return;
    await settle(scheduler, 1);
  }
  throw new Error(`until: condition not met after ${maxRounds} rounds`);
}

// test/clashpanel/core/resolve.test.mjs — spec §9.1, AC-P7/AC-P8
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { resolveSide, resolveResult } from '../../../clashpanel/core/resolve.js';

const modelA = { name: 'A' };
const modelB = { name: 'B' };
const provenance = Object.freeze({
  models: Object.freeze([
    Object.freeze({ modelKey: 'mA', modelVersion: 'v1', bindingGeneration: 3, placementGeneration: 0 }),
    Object.freeze({ modelKey: 'mB', modelVersion: 'v1', bindingGeneration: 1, placementGeneration: 0 }),
  ]),
});

function world({ bindings, scene = [modelA, modelB], names = { mA: 'Architecture', mB: 'Structure' } } = {}) {
  const calls = { bindingFor: [] };
  const table = bindings ?? {
    mA: { modelKey: 'mA', model: modelA, modelVersion: 'v1', bindingGeneration: 3 },
    mB: { modelKey: 'mB', model: modelB, modelVersion: 'v1', bindingGeneration: 1 },
  };
  const engine = {
    registry: {
      bindingFor(key) { calls.bindingFor.push(key); return table[key] ?? null; },
      register() { throw new Error('register must never be called'); },
      unregister() { throw new Error('unregister must never be called'); },
    },
  };
  const catalog = {
    list: () => scene.map((model) => ({ modelKey: model === modelA ? 'mA' : 'mB', displayName: 'x', model, loaded: true })),
    displayNameFor: (key) => names[key] ?? null,
  };
  return { engine, catalog, calls, table };
}

const ref = (modelKey, dbId) => ({ modelKey, dbId });
const record = { resultId: 'r1', pair: { first: ref('mA', 1), second: ref('mB', 10) } };

test('live only when binding, generation, version and scene membership all agree', () => {
  const { engine, catalog } = world();
  const side = resolveSide({ ref: ref('mA', 7), provenance, engine, catalog });
  assert.equal(side.state, 'live');
  assert.equal(side.model, modelA);
  assert.equal(side.dbId, 7);
  assert.equal(side.modelKey, 'mA');
});

test('null binding => not-registered (unloaded and unregistered are indistinguishable)', () => {
  const { engine, catalog } = world({ bindings: { mB: { model: modelB, modelVersion: 'v1', bindingGeneration: 1 } } });
  assert.deepEqual({ ...resolveSide({ ref: ref('mA', 1), provenance, engine, catalog }) },
    { state: 'unavailable', reason: 'not-registered', modelKey: 'mA', dbId: 1 });
});

test('AC-P8: a reload (new generation) never resolves live, even with an equal version and the new model in scene', () => {
  const reloaded = { name: 'A-reloaded' };
  const { engine, catalog } = world({
    bindings: { mA: { model: reloaded, modelVersion: 'v1', bindingGeneration: 4 }, mB: { model: modelB, modelVersion: 'v1', bindingGeneration: 1 } },
    scene: [reloaded, modelB],
  });
  assert.equal(resolveSide({ ref: ref('mA', 1), provenance, engine, catalog }).reason, 'reloaded-since-run');
});

test('AC-P8: same generation but a different modelVersion => version-mismatch', () => {
  const { engine, catalog } = world({
    bindings: { mA: { model: modelA, modelVersion: 'v2', bindingGeneration: 3 }, mB: { model: modelB, modelVersion: 'v1', bindingGeneration: 1 } },
  });
  assert.equal(resolveSide({ ref: ref('mA', 1), provenance, engine, catalog }).reason, 'version-mismatch');
});

test('a registered, lease-valid model that left the scene (hideModel) => not-in-scene (identity compare)', () => {
  const { engine, catalog } = world({ scene: [modelB, { name: 'A' } /* equal shape, different object */] });
  assert.equal(resolveSide({ ref: ref('mA', 1), provenance, engine, catalog }).reason, 'not-in-scene');
});

test('empty provenance.models (planning-failed seal) => not-registered, registry not consulted', () => {
  const { engine, catalog, calls } = world();
  const side = resolveSide({ ref: ref('mA', 1), provenance: { models: [] }, engine, catalog });
  assert.equal(side.reason, 'not-registered');
  assert.deepEqual(calls.bindingFor, []);
});

test('throwing bindingFor / catalog.list never escape (fail closed)', () => {
  const engine = { registry: { bindingFor() { throw new Error('boom'); } } };
  const { catalog } = world();
  assert.equal(resolveSide({ ref: ref('mA', 1), provenance, engine, catalog }).reason, 'not-registered');
  const { engine: okEngine } = world();
  const badCatalog = { list() { throw new Error('boom'); }, displayNameFor: () => null };
  assert.equal(resolveSide({ ref: ref('mA', 1), provenance, engine: okEngine, catalog: badCatalog }).reason, 'not-in-scene');
});

test('resolveResult: both live / one live with the "<name> is not loaded" note / none live', () => {
  const both = world();
  const r1 = resolveResult({ record, provenance, engine: both.engine, catalog: both.catalog });
  assert.deepEqual([r1.anyLive, r1.allLive, r1.notes], [true, true, []]);

  const one = world({ scene: [modelA] });
  const r2 = resolveResult({ record, provenance, engine: one.engine, catalog: one.catalog });
  assert.deepEqual([r2.anyLive, r2.allLive], [true, false]);
  assert.deepEqual(r2.notes, ['Structure is not loaded']);
  assert.equal(r2.sides[0].state, 'live');
  assert.equal(r2.sides[1].reason, 'not-in-scene');

  const none = world({ scene: [] });
  const r3 = resolveResult({ record, provenance, engine: none.engine, catalog: none.catalog });
  assert.deepEqual([r3.anyLive, r3.allLive, r3.notes], [false, false, []]);
});

test('lazy: resolution reflects registry changes made after an earlier resolve (nothing cached)', () => {
  const w = world();
  assert.equal(resolveSide({ ref: ref('mA', 1), provenance, engine: w.engine, catalog: w.catalog }).state, 'live');
  delete w.table.mA;                         // host unregistered mA (wireModelUnload)
  assert.equal(resolveSide({ ref: ref('mA', 1), provenance, engine: w.engine, catalog: w.catalog }).reason, 'not-registered');
});

test('the unavailable note falls back to "Model <key>" when the host has no display name', () => {
  const w = world({ scene: [modelA], names: {} });
  assert.deepEqual(resolveResult({ record, provenance, engine: w.engine, catalog: w.catalog }).notes, ['Model mB is not loaded']);
});

// test/clashpanel/core/labels.test.mjs — spec §8.2, §10.1, §12.4, AC-P13 (raw strings; UI escapes)
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { createLabelResolver, fallbackModelName, readNodeName } from '../../../clashpanel/core/labels.js';
import { LABEL_CACHE_MAX, LIST_CHUNK_SIZE } from '../../../clashpanel/core/constants.js';
import { createFakeScheduler } from '../support/fakeScheduler.mjs';
import { drain } from '../support/settle.mjs';

function fakeModel(names, counter = { reads: 0 }) {
  return {
    counter,
    getObjectTree() {
      return { getNodeName(dbId) { counter.reads += 1; return names[dbId]; } };
    },
  };
}

function setup({ live = {}, names = { mA: 'Architecture', mB: 'Structure' } } = {}) {
  const scheduler = createFakeScheduler();
  const catalog = { displayNameFor: (key) => names[key] ?? null };
  const liveModels = { ...live };
  const labels = createLabelResolver({ catalog, resolveLiveModel: (key) => liveModels[key] ?? null, scheduler });
  return { labels, scheduler, liveModels };
}

function indexOf(records) {
  return { count: records.length, at: (i) => records[i] };
}

test('model names: host display name, else "Model <first 8 chars>"', () => {
  const { labels } = setup();
  assert.equal(labels.modelName('mA'), 'Architecture');
  assert.equal(labels.modelName('0123456789abcdef'), 'Model 01234567');
  assert.equal(fallbackModelName('short'), 'Model short');
  const throwing = createLabelResolver({ catalog: { displayNameFor() { throw new Error('x'); } }, resolveLiveModel: () => null, scheduler: createFakeScheduler() });
  assert.equal(throwing.modelName('mZ'), 'Model mZ');
});

test('RF-2: duplicate display names are disambiguated by a stable key suffix; unique, empty and blank names behave', () => {
  const hostile = '<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>';
  const names = { 'k-0001-3f2a': 'Model', 'k-0002-9c1d': 'Model', mU: 'Unique', h1: hostile, h2: hostile, blank: '   ', empty: '' };
  const catalog = {
    list: () => ['k-0001-3f2a', 'k-0002-9c1d', 'mU', 'h1', 'h2', 'blank', 'empty'].map((modelKey) => ({ modelKey, displayName: names[modelKey], model: {}, loaded: true })),
    displayNameFor: (key) => names[key] ?? null,
  };
  const labels = createLabelResolver({ catalog, resolveLiveModel: () => null, scheduler: createFakeScheduler() });
  assert.equal(labels.modelName('k-0001-3f2a'), 'Model · …3f2a');
  assert.equal(labels.modelName('k-0002-9c1d'), 'Model · …9c1d');
  assert.equal(labels.modelName('mU'), 'Unique');                          // unique names never change
  assert.equal(labels.modelName('h1'), `${hostile} · …h1`);                // raw text, still distinguishable
  assert.equal(labels.modelName('h2'), `${hostile} · …h2`);
  assert.equal(labels.modelName('blank'), 'Model blank');                  // blank ⇒ the existing fallback
  assert.equal(labels.modelName('empty'), 'Model empty');
  assert.equal(labels.modelName('k-0001-3f2a'), labels.modelName('k-0001-3f2a'));   // deterministic
  // Suffix collision ⇒ the full key; a model known only from the displayed run (unloaded) still counts.
  const n2 = { 'a-xx-1234': 'Pipe', 'b-yy-1234': 'Pipe', gone: 'Solo', here: 'Solo' };
  const c2 = { list: () => [{ modelKey: 'a-xx-1234' }, { modelKey: 'b-yy-1234' }, { modelKey: 'here' }], displayNameFor: (k) => n2[k] ?? null };
  const known = [];
  const l2 = createLabelResolver({ catalog: c2, resolveLiveModel: () => null, scheduler: createFakeScheduler(), knownModelKeys: () => known });
  assert.equal(l2.modelName('a-xx-1234'), 'Pipe · …a-xx-1234');
  assert.equal(l2.modelName('here'), 'Solo');
  known.push('gone');
  l2.invalidateNames();
  assert.equal(l2.modelName('here'), 'Solo · …here');
  assert.equal(l2.modelName('gone'), 'Solo · …gone');
});

test('element label: live model name via getObjectTree().getNodeName, else #dbId', () => {
  const { labels, liveModels } = setup({ live: { mA: fakeModel({ 1: 'Wall-102' }) } });
  assert.equal(labels.elementLabel({ modelKey: 'mA', dbId: 1 }), 'Wall-102');
  assert.equal(labels.elementLabel({ modelKey: 'mA', dbId: 2 }), '#2');        // tree has no name
  assert.equal(labels.elementLabel({ modelKey: 'mB', dbId: 10 }), '#10');      // model not live
  delete liveModels.mA;                                                         // unloaded afterwards
  assert.equal(labels.elementLabel({ modelKey: 'mA', dbId: 1 }), '#1');        // cached name is not shown for an unloaded model
});

test('getObjectTree/getNodeName failures are guarded', () => {
  assert.equal(readNodeName({ getObjectTree() { throw new Error('not ready'); } }, 1), null);
  assert.equal(readNodeName({ getObjectTree: () => null }, 1), null);
  assert.equal(readNodeName({}, 1), null);
  assert.equal(readNodeName({ getObjectTree: () => ({ getNodeName: () => '' }) }, 1), null);
});

test('AC-P13: markup-bearing names are returned verbatim (escaping is the UI\'s job via textContent)', () => {
  const hostile = '<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>';
  const { labels } = setup({ live: { mA: fakeModel({ 1: hostile }) }, names: { mA: '<b>Arch</b>' } });
  assert.equal(labels.elementLabel({ modelKey: 'mA', dbId: 1 }), hostile);
  assert.equal(labels.modelName('mA'), '<b>Arch</b>');
});

test('LRU: repeated labels read the tree once; the cache never exceeds LABEL_CACHE_MAX', () => {
  const counter = { reads: 0 };
  const names = new Proxy({}, { get: (_t, k) => `E${String(k)}` });
  const { labels } = setup({ live: { mA: fakeModel(names, counter) } });
  labels.elementLabel({ modelKey: 'mA', dbId: 1 });
  labels.elementLabel({ modelKey: 'mA', dbId: 1 });
  assert.equal(counter.reads, 1);
  for (let dbId = 2; dbId <= LABEL_CACHE_MAX + 1; dbId += 1) labels.elementLabel({ modelKey: 'mA', dbId });
  const before = counter.reads;
  labels.elementLabel({ modelKey: 'mA', dbId: 1 });                         // evicted (least recently used) => re-read
  assert.equal(counter.reads, before + 1);
  labels.elementLabel({ modelKey: 'mA', dbId: LABEL_CACHE_MAX + 1 });       // most recent => still cached
  assert.equal(counter.reads, before + 1);
});

test('a reloaded model (new object, same key) never reuses the old object\'s cached names', () => {
  const { labels, liveModels } = setup({ live: { mA: fakeModel({ 1: 'Old' }) } });
  assert.equal(labels.elementLabel({ modelKey: 'mA', dbId: 1 }), 'Old');
  liveModels.mA = fakeModel({ 1: 'New' });
  assert.equal(labels.elementLabel({ modelKey: 'mA', dbId: 1 }), 'New');
});

test('searchText: model name + dbId always; element name only after warm(); forgetModel drops it', async () => {
  const { labels, scheduler } = setup({ live: { mA: fakeModel({ 1: 'Wall-102' }), mB: fakeModel({ 10: 'Duct-88' }) } });
  const records = [{ resultId: 'r1', pair: { first: { modelKey: 'mA', dbId: 1 }, second: { modelKey: 'mB', dbId: 10 } } }];
  assert.equal(labels.searchText({ modelKey: 'mA', dbId: 1 }), 'architecture  1');
  assert.equal(await drain(scheduler, labels.warm(indexOf(records))), true);
  assert.equal(labels.searchText({ modelKey: 'mA', dbId: 1 }), 'architecture wall-102 1');
  assert.equal(labels.searchText({ modelKey: 'mB', dbId: 10 }), 'structure duct-88 10');
  labels.forgetModel('mB');
  assert.equal(labels.searchText({ modelKey: 'mB', dbId: 10 }), 'structure  10');
  labels.reset();
  assert.equal(labels.searchText({ modelKey: 'mA', dbId: 1 }), 'architecture  1');
});

test('warm() is sliced by LIST_CHUNK_SIZE with one yield per slice, and a superseded pass never commits', async () => {
  const n = LIST_CHUNK_SIZE * 2 + 5;
  const records = Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({ resultId: `r${i}`, pair: { first: { modelKey: 'mA', dbId: i }, second: { modelKey: 'mA', dbId: i + 1 } } }));
  const { labels, scheduler } = setup({ live: { mA: fakeModel(new Proxy({}, { get: (_t, k) => `N${String(k)}` })) } });
  const before = scheduler.yieldCount;
  assert.equal(await drain(scheduler, labels.warm(indexOf(records))), true);
  assert.equal(scheduler.yieldCount - before, Math.ceil(n / LIST_CHUNK_SIZE));

  let current = true;
  const pending = labels.warm(indexOf(records.map((r) => ({ ...r, pair: { first: { modelKey: 'mA', dbId: r.pair.first.dbId + 100000 }, second: r.pair.second } }))), { isCurrent: () => current });
  current = false;                                   // generation moved on before the first slice ran
  assert.equal(await drain(scheduler, pending), false);
  assert.equal(labels.searchText({ modelKey: 'mA', dbId: 100000 }), 'architecture  100000'); // old index kept, new one never swapped in
  assert.match(labels.searchText({ modelKey: 'mA', dbId: 0 }), /n0/);
});
