```js
// clashpanel/ui/render/selected.js — Region 5 SELECTED CLASH (spec §9.2–§9.6, §14.4).
// A disabled action shows its reason BOTH as the control's title and as visible text (Isolate is disabled with a
// reason whenever the §9.5 prerequisite does not hold). No theming, no scene-selection change: the view only dispatches.
import { el, rebuild } from '../dom.js';
import { INTENT } from '../../core/intents.js';

function sideBlock(doc, n, side, dispatch) {
  const plainId = `#${side.dbId}`;
  const text = side.label === plainId ? `${side.modelName} · ${plainId}` : `${side.modelName} · ${side.label} · ${plainId}`;
  return el(doc, 'div', { class: `clash-detail-side clash-detail-side-${n}` }, [
    el(doc, 'span', { class: 'clash-detail-term', text: `Element ${n}: ` }),
    el(doc, 'span', { class: 'clash-detail-value', text }),
    el(doc, 'button', {
      attrs: { type: 'button', 'data-key': `selected-only-${n}` },
      text: 'Show only this element',
      on: { click: () => dispatch({ type: INTENT.FILTER_ELEMENT, ref: { modelKey: side.modelKey, dbId: side.dbId } }) },
    }),
  ]);
}

function reasonText(doc, reason) {
  return reason ? el(doc, 'span', { class: 'clash-reason', text: ` ${reason}` }) : null;
}

function toggle(doc, key, label, action, onChange) {
  const disabled = !action.enabled;
  return el(doc, 'label', { class: `clash-${key}`, attrs: { title: disabled && action.reason ? action.reason : null } }, [
    el(doc, 'input', {
      attrs: { type: 'checkbox', 'data-key': key, disabled, title: disabled && action.reason ? action.reason : null },
      props: { checked: Boolean(action.checked) },
      on: { change: (e) => onChange(e.target.checked) },
    }),
    el(doc, 'span', { text: label }),
    disabled ? reasonText(doc, action.reason) : null,
  ]);
}

export function renderSelected(root, selected, dispatch, doc) {
  rebuild(root, doc, () => {
    if (!selected) {
      root.appendChild(el(doc, 'p', { class: 'clash-selected-empty', text: 'No clash selected. Select a result to see its details.' }));
      return;
    }
    const a = selected.actions;
    root.appendChild(el(doc, 'div', { class: 'clash-selected', attrs: { 'data-result-id': selected.resultId } }, [
      el(doc, 'p', { class: 'clash-selected-title', text: `Clash #${selected.ordinal}` }),
      sideBlock(doc, 1, selected.side1, dispatch),
      sideBlock(doc, 2, selected.side2, dispatch),
      selected.gap !== null && selected.gap !== undefined ? el(doc, 'p', { class: 'clash-selected-gap', text: `Gap ${selected.gap}` }) : null,
      el(doc, 'p', { class: 'clash-selected-location', text: selected.hasLocation ? '● Location available' : 'No location recorded for this clash' }),
      selected.liveness !== 'live' ? el(doc, 'p', { class: 'clash-selected-liveness', text: `Model state: ${selected.liveness}` }) : null,
      selected.notes.length > 0 ? el(doc, 'ul', { class: 'clash-selected-notes' }, selected.notes.map((n) => el(doc, 'li', { text: n }))) : null,
      selected.hiddenByFilters ? el(doc, 'p', { class: 'clash-hidden-note', text: 'This clash is hidden by the current filters.' }) : null,
      el(doc, 'div', { class: 'clash-actions' }, [
        el(doc, 'button', {
          attrs: { type: 'button', 'data-key': 'action-focus', disabled: !a.focus.enabled, title: !a.focus.enabled && a.focus.reason ? a.focus.reason : null },
          text: 'Focus',
          on: { click: () => dispatch({ type: INTENT.ACTION_FOCUS }) },
        }),
        !a.focus.enabled ? reasonText(doc, a.focus.reason) : null,
        toggle(doc, 'action-isolate', 'Isolate', a.isolate, (value) => dispatch({ type: INTENT.ACTION_ISOLATE, value })),
        toggle(doc, 'action-markers', 'Markers', a.markers, (value) => dispatch({ type: INTENT.ACTION_MARKERS, value })),
        toggle(doc, 'action-focus-on-select', 'Focus on select', { enabled: true, checked: a.focusOnSelect.checked, reason: null },
          (value) => dispatch({ type: INTENT.ACTION_FOCUS_ON_SELECT, value })),
        el(doc, 'button', {
          attrs: { type: 'button', 'data-key': 'action-back-to-all', disabled: !a.backToAll.enabled },
          text: 'Back to all',
          on: { click: () => dispatch({ type: INTENT.ACTION_BACK_TO_ALL }) },
        }),
      ]),
    ]));
  });
}
```

```js
// clashpanel/ui/render/panel.js — the five regions in FIXED order (spec §14.3):
// 1 TEST SETUP → 2 RUN / STATUS → 3 FILTERS / GROUPING → 4 RESULTS → 5 SELECTED CLASH. No tabs, no saved views.
// Section elements are created once and reused, so the aria-live status node inside Region 2 survives re-renders.
// Tab order is DOM order (no positive tabindex anywhere); every action is a native button/input/select.
import { el, instanceNs } from '../dom.js';
import { renderSetup } from './setup.js';
import { renderRun } from './run.js';
import { renderFilters } from './filters.js';
import { renderResults } from './results.js';
import { renderSelected } from './selected.js';

export const REGIONS = Object.freeze([
  Object.freeze({ id: 'setup', heading: '1 TEST SETUP', part: 'setup', render: renderSetup }),
  Object.freeze({ id: 'run', heading: '2 RUN / STATUS', part: 'run', render: renderRun }),
  Object.freeze({ id: 'filters', heading: '3 FILTERS / GROUPING', part: 'filters', render: renderFilters }),
  Object.freeze({ id: 'results', heading: '4 RESULTS', part: 'results', render: renderResults }),
  Object.freeze({ id: 'selected', heading: '5 SELECTED CLASH', part: 'selected', render: renderSelected }),
]);

function ensureSection(root, doc, region, index) {
  let section = null;
  for (const child of root.children) {
    if (child.getAttribute('data-region') === region.id) { section = child; break; }
  }
  if (!section) {
    section = el(doc, 'section', { class: `clash-region clash-region-${region.id}`, attrs: { 'data-region': region.id, 'aria-label': region.heading } }, [
      el(doc, 'h2', { class: 'clash-region-heading', text: region.heading }),
      el(doc, 'div', { class: 'clash-region-body' }),
    ]);
  }
  if (root.children[index] !== section) root.insertBefore(section, root.children[index] ?? null);
  return section.querySelector(':scope > .clash-region-body');
}

// Minimal layout rules so untrusted text can never widen the panel (RF-5): long unbroken names wrap anywhere and
// no flex/grid/fieldset child keeps an intrinsic min-content width. Inserted once per document as plain text of a
// <style> element (textContent — no markup parsing); the host loads no extra file.
export const PANEL_STYLE_ID = 'clash-panel-style';
export const PANEL_CSS = [
  '.clash-panel-root{box-sizing:border-box;max-width:100%;min-width:0;overflow-x:hidden}',
  '.clash-panel-root *{box-sizing:border-box;min-width:0;max-width:100%;overflow-wrap:anywhere;word-break:break-word}',
  '.clash-panel-root fieldset{min-inline-size:0;margin:0}',
  '.clash-panel-root select,.clash-panel-root input[type=text],.clash-panel-root input[type=search]{width:100%}',
  '.clash-panel-root ul,.clash-panel-root dl{padding-left:1em;margin:0}',
  '.clash-panel-root .clash-row{display:block}',
].join('\n');

function ensureStyle(doc) {
  if (doc.getElementById(PANEL_STYLE_ID)) return;
  const style = el(doc, 'style', { attrs: { id: PANEL_STYLE_ID }, text: PANEL_CSS });
  (doc.head ?? doc.documentElement).appendChild(style);
}

export function renderPanel(root, vm, dispatch, doc) {
  ensureStyle(doc);
  if (!root.classList.contains('clash-panel-root')) root.classList.add('clash-panel-root');
  instanceNs(root);   // one radio-name namespace for all five regions of this panel
  REGIONS.forEach((region, index) => {
    const body = ensureSection(root, doc, region, index);
    region.render(body, vm[region.part], dispatch, doc);
  });
}
```

**Scope note:** the subclass overrides `initialize()` only and declares **no class fields** (a field initializer runs after the base constructor, which already called `initialize()`); it builds title bar + close button with the documented `createTitleBar`/`createCloseButton`/`initializeMoveHandlers` and finds its body via `container.querySelector`, never via a `this` field. The base constructor calls `setVisible(false)` before the shell adds its ONE visibility listener, so construction dispatches nothing. **Construction is transactional:** `new PanelClass(...)` (which may throw from `initialize()`/`initializeMoveHandlers()` AFTER the base constructor appended its container, returning no instance), the body lookup, `addVisibilityListener`, `subscribe` and the first render all run inside one guarded block; any throw marks the shell disposed (a registered listener becomes inert), unsubscribes, `uninitialize()`s a constructed panel, removes every child the attempt added to `parentContainer`, and rethrows. Tests inject failures into `initializeMoveHandlers()` and `addVisibilityListener()` (no container, no subscription, no listener; plan-time negative control: without the child sweep the first case fails) and mount two shells at once (Soft/Element in one leaves the other's radios unchanged; negative control: a fixed radio name fails). The listener checks `disposed` (there is no remove-listener). `dispose()` unsubscribes, then `uninitialize()` once (nested `try/finally`), and afterwards `show/hide/toggle` are no-ops (never `setVisible` after `uninitialize`). **Signature refinement (see Notes):** `createPanelShell` takes `parentContainer` (the composition passes `viewer.container`) instead of `viewer`, so the shell has no 3D-host reference at all (AC-P21). No token `viewer` appears anywhere under `clashpanel/ui/`.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `Autodesk.Viewing.UI.DockingPanel` (constructor `(parentContainer, id, title, options)`, `initialize`, `createTitleBar(text)`, `createCloseButton()`, `initializeMoveHandlers(el)`, `setVisible(bool)`, `isVisible()`, `addVisibilityListener(cb)`, `uninitialize()`; undocumented members per catalog §1, live = PG-1); `renderPanel` (T30); `INTENT.PANEL_SHOWN/PANEL_HIDDEN`; `PanelController` port `{ getViewModel, subscribe, dispatch }` (catalog §4).
- Produces: `createClashDockingPanelClass(Autodesk) -> class extends Autodesk.Viewing.UI.DockingPanel` (TypeError if absent); `createPanelShell({ Autodesk, parentContainer, controller, id, title?, doc? }) -> Object.freeze({ show(), hide(), toggle(), isVisible(): boolean, dispose(): void })` (TypeError on missing controller methods / non-element parent / empty id; a throwing `subscribe`/first render uninitializes the panel and rethrows). `fakeController.mjs` (browser-side): `createFakeController(vm) -> { getViewModel, subscribe, dispatch, dispose, set(vm), dispatched, subscriberCount() }`.

```js
// test/clashpanel/dom/support/fakeController.mjs
//
// BROWSER-SIDE PanelController double for the shell tests (Task 31): the PanelController port of plan catalog §4
// (getViewModel/subscribe/dispatch/dispose) over a caller-supplied ViewModel. `set(vm)` notifies subscribers
// exactly like the real controller does on a state change. No Node imports.
export function createFakeController(initialVm) {
  let vm = initialVm;
  const subscribers = new Set();
  const dispatched = [];
  return {
    dispatched,
    subscriberCount: () => subscribers.size,
    getViewModel: () => vm,
    subscribe(cb) {
      if (typeof cb !== 'function') throw new TypeError('subscribe: callback required');
      subscribers.add(cb);
      return () => { subscribers.delete(cb); };
    },
    dispatch(intent) {
      dispatched.push(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(intent)));
      return Promise.resolve();
    },
    dispose: () => Promise.resolve(),
    set(next) {
      vm = next;
      for (const cb of [...subscribers]) cb(vm);
    },
  };
}
```

```js
// clashpanel/ui/ClashDockingPanel.js — the ONE small adapter that owns the DockingPanel (spec §14.2 PD-19).
//
// Thin by construction (AC-P21): it creates the panel, renders controller.getViewModel() into the panel body on
// every controller notification, and turns DOM events / visibility changes into intents. It holds NO workflow or
// domain state (no draft, run, results, filters, grouping, selection, page, residency, restore state) and has no
// reference to the 3D host: the parent container is passed in by the composition root.
//
// Verified DockingPanel constraints (plan catalog §1; live lifecycle = gate G3/PG-1):
//   * subclass ONLY through initialize(); the base constructor calls initialize() BEFORE a subclass's own fields
//     exist, so this class declares NO fields and finds its body through the container, not through `this`;
//   * the base constructor calls setVisible(false) after initialize(), BEFORE our listener is added;
//   * addVisibilityListener has no remove counterpart: exactly ONE listener, gated by `disposed`;
//   * never setVisible after uninitialize() (the container is null then).
import { INTENT } from '../core/intents.js';
import { renderPanel } from './render/panel.js';

const BODY_CLASS = 'clash-panel-body';

export function createClashDockingPanelClass(Autodesk) {
  const Base = Autodesk?.Viewing?.UI?.DockingPanel;
  if (typeof Base !== 'function') {
    throw new TypeError('createClashDockingPanelClass: Autodesk.Viewing.UI.DockingPanel is required');
  }
  return class ClashDockingPanel extends Base {
    initialize() {
      const doc = this.container.ownerDocument;
      this.title = this.createTitleBar(this.titleLabel || this.container.id);
      this.container.appendChild(this.title);
      this.closer = this.createCloseButton();
      this.container.appendChild(this.closer);
      this.initializeMoveHandlers(this.title);
      const body = doc.createElement('div');
      body.className = BODY_CLASS;
      this.container.appendChild(body);
    }
  };
}

function assertController(controller) {
  for (const name of ['getViewModel', 'subscribe', 'dispatch']) {
    if (typeof controller?.[name] !== 'function') throw new TypeError(`createPanelShell: controller.${name} is required`);
  }
}

export function createPanelShell({ Autodesk, parentContainer, controller, id, title, doc } = {}) {
  assertController(controller);
  if (typeof parentContainer?.appendChild !== 'function') throw new TypeError('createPanelShell: parentContainer must be a DOM element');
  if (typeof id !== 'string' || id === '') throw new TypeError('createPanelShell: id is required');
  const PanelClass = createClashDockingPanelClass(Autodesk);
  const document_ = doc ?? parentContainer.ownerDocument;

  let disposed = false;
  let panel = null;
  let body = null;
  let unsubscribe = null;
  const dispatch = (intent) => (disposed ? Promise.resolve() : controller.dispatch(intent));
  const render = (vm) => { if (!disposed && body !== null) renderPanel(body, vm, dispatch, document_); };
  const onVisibility = (shown) => {
    if (disposed) return;
    controller.dispatch({ type: shown ? INTENT.PANEL_SHOWN : INTENT.PANEL_HIDDEN });
  };

  // Transactional construction: the base constructor appends its container BEFORE initialize() runs, so a throw
  // from initialize()/initializeMoveHandlers() (no instance returned), the body lookup, addVisibilityListener,
  // subscribe or the first render must leave NOTHING behind — no container, no subscription, no live listener.
  const childrenBefore = new Set(parentContainer.children);
  try {
    panel = new PanelClass(parentContainer, id, title ?? 'Clash Detection', {});
    body = panel.container.querySelector(`:scope > .${BODY_CLASS}`);
    if (body === null) throw new Error('createPanelShell: panel body was not created');
    panel.addVisibilityListener(onVisibility);
    unsubscribe = controller.subscribe(render);
    render(controller.getViewModel());
  } catch (error) {
    disposed = true;   // a listener that did get registered is inert from here on
    try { if (unsubscribe) unsubscribe(); } catch { /* rollback continues */ }
    unsubscribe = null;
    try { if (panel !== null) panel.uninitialize(); } catch { /* rollback continues */ }
    for (const child of [...parentContainer.children]) {
      if (!childrenBefore.has(child)) {
        try { parentContainer.removeChild(child); } catch { /* rollback continues */ }
      }
    }
    throw error;
  }

  return Object.freeze({
    show() { if (!disposed) panel.setVisible(true); },
    hide() { if (!disposed) panel.setVisible(false); },
    toggle() { if (!disposed) panel.setVisible(!panel.isVisible()); },
    isVisible() { return !disposed && panel.isVisible(); },
    dispose() {
      if (disposed) return;
      disposed = true;
      try {
        if (unsubscribe) unsubscribe();
      } finally {
        unsubscribe = null;
        panel.uninitialize();
      }
    },
  });
}
```

The E2E tolerates either default of the Markers toggle (it turns it on if off) but asserts spec §9.6 rows it exercises: Back to all clears markers + selection; Hide clears markers and **keeps** the selection; dispose during a run cancels with `'panel-disposed'`; "Copy diagnostics" writes the controller-resolved JSON string to a stubbed clipboard. **Overlay scenes are instance-scoped:** `createClashPanel` passes `names = {overlayMarkers: `clash-panel-markers:${id}`, overlayOutlines: `clash-panel-outlines:${id}`}` (never shared hard-coded names); a test runs TWO panels (ids `panel-a`/`panel-b`) on one fake viewer — Back to all and dispose of one leave the other's scene meshes intact (plan-time negative control: shared names make it fail). **Construction rollback:** a `createClashPanel` that fails mid-construction — (a) in the shell (`initializeMoveHandlers` throws) or (b) in the controller (a non-engine port) — leaves no DOM node, no catalog subscription, no viewer listener, no overlay mesh/scene and makes no theming call, asserted together after the asynchronous teardown of what was already built. **Release failures surface:** with the fake engine's `releaseResultSet` failing (`engine.options.failRelease`), `dispose()` rejects with an `AggregateError` containing that error, after every step ran (zero meshes, zero listeners, panel removed). **Dispose waits for a held run:** with Part 3's contract (`controller.dispose()` resolves only after the active run's `done` settled, its set released and the bridge disposed), a test holds the fake engine's cancel (`engine.options.holdCancel = true`), asserts `dispose()` is still pending after the task queue drains, then finishes the run and asserts zero Panel meshes, zero listeners, zero leases and a release call for that run (negative control: a controller that does not await `done` makes it fail). `dispose()` order: shell → controller → bridge, each in `try/finally`, all run even if one throws; rejects with `AggregateError` after all ran (see Notes). README is documentation only (no test asserts its wording).

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `createPanelController({ engine, catalog, bridge, scheduler })` from `./core/index.js` (catalog §4; `scheduler` undefined ⇒ its default); `createViewerBridge({ viewerApi, THREE, names })` (`./viewer/ViewerBridge.js`, catalog §5); `createViewerApi(viewer, { events: { BEFORE_MODEL_UNLOAD, MODEL_REMOVED } })` (`./viewer/viewerApi.js`); `createPanelShell` (T31); bridge `dispose(): Promise<void>`; controller `dispose(): Promise<void>`.
- Produces: `createClashPanel({ Autodesk, viewer, THREE, engine, catalog, scheduler?, doc?, events, id? = 'clash-detection-panel', title? = 'Clash Detection' }) -> Object.freeze({ show, hide, toggle, isVisible, dispose(): Promise<void>, controller })`; TypeError when `viewer` is not an object, `id` is empty, or either event name is missing (before anything is created). Overlay scene names are instance-scoped: `clash-panel-markers:<id>` / `clash-panel-outlines:<id>`. `dispose()` resolves after shell, controller (which awaits the active run's `done` and resolves `{released, errors}`, never rejecting) and bridge; `AggregateError` after all steps if any step threw, the controller reported `errors`, or `released` was `false`. `inPageFakes.mjs`: `createFakeThree`, `createFakeModel`, `createFakeViewer` (+ `sceneMeshes()`), `createFakeCatalog`, `makeResultSet`, `hardResults`, `createFakeEngine` (+ `options.holdCancel`, `options.failRelease`), `createWorld`.
- **Depends on:** T18/T19 (core barrel; the dispose-awaits-`done` contract), T22–T26 (bridge, viewerApi), T31.

```js
// test/clashpanel/dom/support/inPageFakes.mjs
//
// BROWSER-SIDE doubles for the end-to-end fake-port slice (Task 32). Deliberately NOT the Node fakes of Task 3
// (test/clashpanel/support/*.mjs): those are outside the harness's served roots and may use Node APIs. These
// import nothing. They model only the port surfaces of plan catalog §1/§3/§5:
//   * engine: EnginePort members + controllable RunHandle (events `{type,...payload}` as clashtest/run/emitter.js)
//     + AC-P20 tripwires (register/unregister/invalidateModelPlacement/wireModelUnload throw);
//   * catalog: ModelCatalog (list/displayNameFor/keyOfModel/onChange/measurementBasis) with listener counting;
//   * viewer: a Viewer3D-shaped object (public overlays API, MESH FIRST then scene name; aggregate isolation;
//     fitToView; aggregate selection; add/removeEventListener with counting; theming methods THROW and record);
//   * THREE: an r71-shaped subset (Vector3 has NO setScalar) with dispose counters.
// engine.options.holdCancel = true makes cancel() NOT settle the run (a slow engine); the test then calls finish().
// If T22/T26's viewerApi.js reads a Viewer member not modelled here, add that member HERE (read-only, recorded),
// mirroring test/clashpanel/support/fakeViewer.mjs — never loosen an assertion of the test instead.

export function createFakeThree() {
  const counters = { geometryDisposed: 0, materialDisposed: 0 };
  class Vector3 {
    constructor(x = 0, y = 0, z = 0) { this.x = x; this.y = y; this.z = z; }
    set(x, y, z) { this.x = x; this.y = y; this.z = z; return this; }
    copy(v) { this.x = v.x; this.y = v.y; this.z = v.z; return this; }
    clone() { return new Vector3(this.x, this.y, this.z); }
  }
  class BufferGeometry {
    constructor() { this.points = null; }
    setFromPoints(points) { this.points = points; return this; }
    dispose() { counters.geometryDisposed += 1; }
  }
  class SphereGeometry extends BufferGeometry { constructor(r, w, h) { super(); this.parameters = { r, w, h }; } }
  class BoxGeometry extends BufferGeometry { constructor(x, y, z) { super(); this.parameters = { x, y, z }; } }
  class EdgesGeometry extends BufferGeometry { constructor(g) { super(); this.source = g; } }
  class Material { constructor(opts = {}) { Object.assign(this, opts); } dispose() { counters.materialDisposed += 1; } }
  class MeshBasicMaterial extends Material {}
  class LineBasicMaterial extends Material {}
  class Object3D {
    constructor() { this.position = new Vector3(); this.scale = new Vector3(1, 1, 1); this.visible = true; this.renderOrder = 0; }
  }
  class Mesh extends Object3D { constructor(geometry, material) { super(); this.geometry = geometry; this.material = material; } }
  class Line extends Object3D { constructor(geometry, material) { super(); this.geometry = geometry; this.material = material; } }
  class LineSegments extends Line {}
  class Box3 { constructor(min = new Vector3(), max = new Vector3()) { this.min = min; this.max = max; } }
  return { counters, REVISION: '71', Vector3, BufferGeometry, SphereGeometry, BoxGeometry, EdgesGeometry, MeshBasicMaterial, LineBasicMaterial, Object3D, Mesh, Line, LineSegments, Box3 };
}

export function createFakeModel(modelKey) {
  const tree = {
    getRootId: () => 1,
    getNodeName: (dbId) => `${modelKey}-element-${dbId}`,
    getNodeBox: (dbId, out) => { out[0] = dbId; out[1] = 0; out[2] = 0; out[3] = dbId + 1; out[4] = 1; out[5] = 1; return out; },
  };
  return { modelKey, getObjectTree: () => tree, getInstanceTree: () => tree, isLoadDone: () => true, getData: () => ({}) };
}

export function createFakeViewer(models) {
  const container = document.createElement('div');
  container.id = 'fake-viewer-container';
  document.body.appendChild(container);
  const scenes = new Map();
  const listeners = new Map();
  const calls = [];
  let isolation = [];
  const themingCall = (name) => () => { calls.push([name]); throw new Error('theming forbidden'); };
  const viewer = {
    container,
    calls,
    getAllModels: () => models.slice(),
    getAggregateIsolation: () => isolation.map((e) => ({ model: e.model, ids: e.ids.slice() })),
    getAggregateHiddenNodes: () => [],
    setAggregateIsolation(list) { calls.push(['setAggregateIsolation', list.length]); isolation = list.map((e) => ({ model: e.model, ids: [...e.ids] })); },
    getAggregateSelection: () => [],
    fitToView(...args) { calls.push(['fitToView', Array.isArray(args[0]) ? args[0].length : null]); },
    overlays: {
      hasScene: (name) => scenes.has(name),
      addScene(name) { if (typeof name !== 'string') throw new TypeError('scene name'); if (!scenes.has(name)) scenes.set(name, new Set()); return true; },
      addMesh(mesh, sceneName) {
        if (typeof sceneName !== 'string') throw new TypeError('addMesh(mesh, sceneName): scene name must be a string');
        if (!scenes.has(sceneName)) return false;
        scenes.get(sceneName).add(mesh);
        calls.push(['addMesh', sceneName]);
        return true;
      },
      removeMesh(mesh, sceneName) {
        if (typeof sceneName !== 'string') throw new TypeError('removeMesh(mesh, sceneName): scene name must be a string');
        const set = scenes.get(sceneName);
        return set ? set.delete(mesh) : false;
      },
      removeScene(name) { return scenes.delete(name); },
    },
    addEventListener(type, fn) { if (!listeners.has(type)) listeners.set(type, new Set()); listeners.get(type).add(fn); },
    removeEventListener(type, fn) { listeners.get(type)?.delete(fn); },
    fire(type, payload) { for (const fn of [...(listeners.get(type) ?? [])]) fn({ type, ...payload }); },
    listenerCount: () => [...listeners.values()].reduce((n, s) => n + s.size, 0),
    meshCount: () => [...scenes.values()].reduce((n, s) => n + s.size, 0),
    sceneMeshes: () => Object.fromEntries([...scenes].map(([name, s]) => [name, s.size])),
    setThemingColor: themingCall('setThemingColor'),
    clearThemingColors: themingCall('clearThemingColors'),
  };
  return viewer;
}

export function createFakeCatalog(entries) {
  const subscribers = new Set();
  const byModel = new Map(entries.map((e) => [e.model, e.modelKey]));
  return {
    list: () => entries.map((e) => ({ modelKey: e.modelKey, displayName: e.displayName, model: e.model, loaded: true })),
    displayNameFor: (key) => entries.find((e) => e.modelKey === key)?.displayName ?? null,
    keyOfModel: (model) => byModel.get(model) ?? null,
    onChange(cb) { subscribers.add(cb); return () => { subscribers.delete(cb); }; },
    measurementBasis: () => ({ state: 'unverified', reason: 'no verified measurement basis in this fake' }),
    listenerCount: () => subscribers.size,
  };
}

const RUN_OPTIONS = Object.freeze({ maxResultsPerRun: 100000 });

export function makeResultSet({ runId, definition, status = 'completed', results }) {
  return {
    schemaVersion: 1, runId,
    testRef: { testId: definition?.testId ?? 'fake-test', revision: definition?.revision ?? 1, semanticDigest: null },
    definition: definition ?? null, derivedFromRunId: null,
    outcome: { status, coverage: status === 'completed' ? 'full' : 'partial', integrity: 'clean', freshness: 'current', environmentSensitive: false, environmentSensitiveCauses: [], reasons: [] },
    provenance: {
      registrySessionId: 'fake-session', libraryVersion: 'fake', broadPhase: 'fake', determinismClass: 'deterministic',
      runOptions: RUN_OPTIONS,
      models: ['mA', 'mB'].map((modelKey) => ({ modelKey, modelVersion: 'v1', scopeKinds: ['model'], elementCount: 0, scopeDigests: {}, bindingGeneration: 1, placementGeneration: 1 })),
      scopeProof: null, admissionBaseline: null, hierarchyInternalAcceptance: null, libraryExclusions: [], placementVerified: true,
      startedAt: 0, finishedAt: 1,
    },
    ledger: {
      planExists: true, pairSpaceTotal: 4, emptyOperand: false, units: [], rootOwners: [], unresolvedSelections: [],
      unreachablePopulation: [], hierarchyInternal: [], planningGaps: [], exclusions: [], warnings: [], budgetExhausted: false, firstRefusalUnitId: null,
    },
    results,
    diagnostics: { diagnostics: [], truncated: false, total: 0, countsByReason: [] },
    statistics: {}, digests: {}, sealed: true,
  };
}

export function hardResults() {
  const r = (i, a, b, point) => ({
    resultId: `r${i}`, pair: { first: { modelKey: 'mA', dbId: a }, second: { modelKey: 'mB', dbId: b } },
    mode: 'volume-overlap', evaluatedAs: 'volume-overlap',
    evidence: { witness: point ? { kind: 'point', point } : null }, flags: point ? {} : { witnessUnavailable: true }, unitId: '1.0',
  });
  return [r(1, 1, 10, [1, 2, 3]), r(2, 2, 10, [4, 5, 6]), r(3, 2, 11, null)];
}

function createHandle(runId, definition, persistenceById, options) {
  const listeners = new Set();
  let seq = 0;
  let snapshot = {
    runId, status: 'queued', phase: 'queued', seq: 0, unitsTotal: 0, unitsEvaluated: 0, unitsFailedOrSkipped: 0,
    pairSpaceTotal: 0, pairSpaceEvaluated: 0, pairSpaceProcessed: 0, fractionEvaluated: 0, fractionProcessed: null,
    resultsFound: 0, caveatCount: 0, caveatUnclassified: 0, currentUnitId: null, elapsedMs: 0,
  };
  let settle;
  let settlePersisted;
  let settled = false;
  const done = new Promise((res) => { settle = res; });
  const persisted = new Promise((res) => { settlePersisted = res; });
  const emit = (type, payload) => {
    const event = Object.freeze({ type, ...payload });
    for (const fn of [...listeners]) { try { fn(event); } catch { /* swallowed, as the engine does */ } }
  };
  const control = {
    cancelReasons: [],
    listenerCount: () => listeners.size,
    progress({ unitsEvaluated, unitsTotal, resultsFound }) {
      seq += 1;
      const f = unitsTotal > 0 ? unitsEvaluated / unitsTotal : 0;
      snapshot = { ...snapshot, status: 'running', phase: 'executing', seq, unitsEvaluated, unitsTotal, pairSpaceTotal: unitsTotal, pairSpaceEvaluated: unitsEvaluated, pairSpaceProcessed: unitsEvaluated, fractionEvaluated: f, fractionProcessed: f, resultsFound };
      emit('state', { seq, status: 'running', phase: 'executing' });
    },
    finish({ status = 'completed', results = hardResults(), persistence = { state: 'saved', timedOut: false, attempt: 1 } } = {}) {
      if (settled) return;
      settled = true;
      seq += 1;
      const resultSet = makeResultSet({ runId, definition, status, results });
      persistenceById.set(runId, persistence);
      snapshot = { ...snapshot, status, phase: 'terminal', seq, resultsFound: results.length };
      emit('state', { seq, status, phase: 'terminal', terminal: true, persistence });
      settle({ runId, status, resultSet, persistence });
      settlePersisted(persistence.state === 'saved' ? { state: 'saved' } : { state: 'skipped', reason: persistence.reason ?? 'not-saved' });
    },
  };
  const handle = Object.freeze({
    runId,
    getSnapshot: () => ({ ...snapshot }),
    subscribe(fn) {
      if (typeof fn !== 'function') throw new TypeError('listener must be a function');
      const box = (e) => fn(e);
      listeners.add(box);
      return () => { listeners.delete(box); };
    },
    cancel(reason) {
      control.cancelReasons.push(reason ?? null);
      if (!settled) {
        seq += 1;
        if (options.holdCancel === true) {   // an engine that finishes the run LATER (the test calls finish())
          snapshot = { ...snapshot, status: 'cancelling', seq };
          emit('state', { seq, status: 'cancelling', phase: snapshot.phase });
          return done;
        }
        snapshot = { ...snapshot, status: 'cancelling', seq };
        emit('state', { seq, status: 'cancelling', phase: snapshot.phase });
        queueMicrotask(() => control.finish({ status: 'cancelled', results: [], persistence: { state: 'skipped', timedOut: false, attempt: 0, reason: 'cancelled' } }));
      }
      return done;
    },
    done,
    persisted,
  });
  control.handle = handle;
  return control;
}

export function createFakeEngine({ bindings }) {
  const calls = [];
  const handles = [];
  const persistenceById = new Map();
  const leases = new Set();
  let n = 0;
  const options = { holdCancel: false, failRelease: false };
  const forbidden = (name) => () => { calls.push([name]); throw new Error(`AC-P20: ${name} must never be called by the Panel`); };
  return {
    calls, handles, options,
    activeLeases: () => leases.size,
    validateTest(def) { calls.push(['validateTest']); return { issues: [], issuesTruncated: false }; },
    startRun(def) {
      n += 1;
      const control = createHandle(`run-${n}`, def, persistenceById, options);
      calls.push(['startRun', control.handle.runId]);
      handles.push(control);
      return control.handle;
    },
    retainResultSet(runId) {
      calls.push(['retainResultSet', runId]);
      const lease = { runId };
      leases.add(lease);
      let released = false;
      return { release() { if (released) return; released = true; leases.delete(lease); calls.push(['lease.release', runId]); } };
    },
    releaseResultSet(runId, opts) {
      calls.push(['releaseResultSet', runId, opts ?? null]);
      if (options.failRelease === true) throw new Error(`release failed for ${runId}`);
    },
    getPersistenceState: (runId) => persistenceById.get(runId) ?? null,
    getFreshness: async () => ({ state: 'current', reasons: [] }),
    assessNoClashClaim: async (set) => ({ allowed: false, unqualified: false, qualifiers: [], exclusions: [], proofMethod: null }),
    derivations: {
      async summarize(set) {
        calls.push(['summarize']);
        return {
          runId: set.runId, status: set.outcome.status, environmentSensitive: false,
          axes: { coverage: set.outcome.coverage, integrity: set.outcome.integrity, freshness: 'current', freshnessAtSeal: 'current' },
          totalResults: set.results.length, resultsByMode: [], resultsByPairModels: [], resultsByCrossModel: [], resultsCaveated: 0,
          unitOutcomes: [], planningGaps: [], gapWeight: 0,
          caveats: { total: 0, completenessAffectingUpperBound: 0, omittedReasonOccurrences: 0, unclassifiedOccurrences: 0, countsByReason: [] },
        };
      },
      async filter(set) { calls.push(['filter']); return { matches: [], count: 0, total: set.results.length, unavailable: [] }; },
      async groupBy(set) {
        calls.push(['groupBy']);
        const groups = new Map();
        for (const r of set.results) {
          for (const ref of [r.pair.first, r.pair.second]) {
            const id = `element:${ref.modelKey}:${ref.dbId}`;
            if (!groups.has(id)) groups.set(id, { groupId: id, path: [id], facetId: 'element', params: {}, value: { modelKey: ref.modelKey, dbId: ref.dbId }, count: 0, members: [] });
            const g = groups.get(id);
            g.count += 1;
            g.members.push(r.resultId);
          }
        }
        const list = [...groups.values()];
        return { facets: ['element'], unavailable: [], total: set.results.length, memberships: list.reduce((s, g) => s + g.count, 0), groups: list };
      },
    },
    registry: { bindingFor: (key) => bindings.get(key) ?? null },
    register: forbidden('register'),
    unregister: forbidden('unregister'),
    invalidateModelPlacement: forbidden('invalidateModelPlacement'),
    wireModelUnload: forbidden('wireModelUnload'),
  };
}

/** One call builds the whole fake world used by the E2E test. */
export function createWorld() {
  const modelA = createFakeModel('mA');
  const modelB = createFakeModel('mB');
  const entries = [
    { modelKey: 'mA', displayName: 'Architecture', model: modelA },
    { modelKey: 'mB', displayName: 'Structure', model: modelB },
  ];
  const bindings = new Map(entries.map((e) => [e.modelKey, Object.freeze({ modelKey: e.modelKey, model: e.model, modelVersion: 'v1', lease: null, bindingGeneration: 1, placementGeneration: 1 })]));
  return {
    THREE: createFakeThree(),
    viewer: createFakeViewer([modelA, modelB]),
    catalog: createFakeCatalog(entries),
    engine: createFakeEngine({ bindings }),
    events: { BEFORE_MODEL_UNLOAD: 'beforeModelUnload', MODEL_REMOVED: 'modelRemoved' },
  };
}
```

```js
// test/clashpanel/dom/composition.dom.mjs — createClashPanel end-to-end over fake ports in Chromium (Task 32).
// Real core controller + real ViewerBridge/viewerApi + real UI, fake engine/catalog/viewer/THREE (inPageFakes.mjs).
// Event-driven waits only (page.waitForFunction on view-model / fake state); no fixed sleeps, no timing assertions.
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { withPage } from './support/harness.mjs';

async function boot(page) {
  await page.evaluate(async () => {
    const fakes = await import('/test/clashpanel/dom/support/inPageFakes.mjs');
    const { createClashPanel } = await import('/clashpanel/index.js');
    const world = fakes.createWorld();
    const panel = createClashPanel({
      Autodesk: window.Autodesk, viewer: world.viewer, THREE: world.THREE,
      engine: world.engine, catalog: world.catalog, events: world.events,
    });
    window.__e2e = { world, panel, vmOf: () => panel.controller.getViewModel() };
    panel.show();
  });
}

async function waitVm(page, predicateSource) {
  // predicateSource: a function (vm) => boolean, serialized; evaluated against the controller's current view-model.
  await page.waitForFunction(`(${predicateSource})(window.__e2e.vmOf())`);
}

async function configureAndRun(page) {
  await page.click('#clash-detection-panel [data-key="setup-A-mA"]');
  await waitVm(page, (vm) => vm.setup.models.some((m) => m.modelKey === 'mA' && m.inA));
  await page.click('#clash-detection-panel [data-key="setup-B-mB"]');
  await waitVm(page, (vm) => vm.setup.models.some((m) => m.modelKey === 'mB' && m.inB));
  await waitVm(page, (vm) => vm.setup.validation.state === 'ready' && vm.run.canRun === true);
  await page.click('#clash-detection-panel [data-key="run-start"]');
  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__e2e.world.engine.handles.length === 1);
}

async function finishRun(page) {
  await page.evaluate(() => window.__e2e.world.engine.handles[0].progress({ unitsEvaluated: 1, unitsTotal: 2, resultsFound: 2 }));
  await waitVm(page, (vm) => vm.run.state === 'running' && vm.run.canStop === true && vm.run.progress !== null);
  const during = await page.evaluate(() => ({
    rows: document.querySelectorAll('#clash-detection-panel .clash-row').length,
    progress: document.querySelector('#clash-detection-panel progress')?.getAttribute('aria-valuenow') ?? null,
    stop: document.querySelector('#clash-detection-panel [data-key="run-stop"]').disabled,
  }));
  await page.evaluate(() => window.__e2e.world.engine.handles[0].finish());
  await waitVm(page, (vm) => vm.run.state === 'done' && vm.results.state === 'list' && vm.results.rows.length === 3);
  return during;
}

async function selectFirstRowWithMarkers(page) {
  await page.click('#clash-detection-panel .clash-row >> nth=0');
  await waitVm(page, (vm) => vm.selected !== null && vm.selected.resultId === 'r1');
  const markersOn = await page.evaluate(() => window.__e2e.vmOf().selected.actions.markers.checked);
  if (!markersOn) {
    await page.check('#clash-detection-panel [data-key="action-markers"]');
    await waitVm(page, (vm) => vm.selected.actions.markers.checked === true);
  }
  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__e2e.world.viewer.meshCount() > 0);
}

test('E2E: setup by clicks → Run → progress → done → list → select presents markers → Back to all → dispose leaves nothing', () => withPage(async ({ page }) => {
  await boot(page);
  await configureAndRun(page);
  const during = await finishRun(page);
  assert.deepEqual(during, { rows: 0, progress: '50', stop: false }); // AC-P3: no list during a run; Stop enabled

  const listed = await page.evaluate(() => ({
    rows: [...document.querySelectorAll('#clash-detection-panel .clash-row')].map((li) => li.getAttribute('aria-selected')),
    counts: document.querySelector('#clash-detection-panel .clash-counts')?.textContent ?? null,
  }));
  assert.deepEqual(listed.rows, ['false', 'false', 'false']);
  assert.match(listed.counts, /^3 clashes/);

  // Copy diagnostics: the real controller resolves the full plain-JSON string; the UI writes it to the clipboard.
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    window.__copied = [];
    Object.defineProperty(navigator, 'clipboard', { configurable: true, value: { writeText: async (t) => { window.__copied.push(t); } } });
  });
  await page.click('#clash-detection-panel [data-key="diagnostics-copy"]');
  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__copied.length === 1);
  const copied = await page.evaluate(() => JSON.parse(window.__copied[0]));
  assert.equal(typeof copied, 'object');
  assert.notEqual(copied, null);
  // Run details (spec §8.4) from the real view-model render as a native <details> of label/value rows.
  const details = await page.evaluate(() => ({
    rows: document.querySelectorAll('#clash-detection-panel .clash-run-details dt').length,
    vmRows: window.__e2e.vmOf().run.details?.lines.length ?? 0,
  }));
  assert.ok(details.vmRows > 0);
  assert.equal(details.rows, details.vmRows);

  await selectFirstRowWithMarkers(page);
  const selected = await page.evaluate(() => ({
    ariaSelected: document.querySelector('#clash-detection-panel .clash-row[aria-selected="true"]')?.getAttribute('data-key') ?? null,
    detail: document.querySelector('#clash-detection-panel .clash-selected')?.getAttribute('data-result-id') ?? null,
    addMesh: window.__e2e.world.viewer.calls.filter((c) => c[0] === 'addMesh').length,
  }));
  assert.ok(selected.ariaSelected.endsWith('r1'));
  assert.equal(selected.detail, 'r1');
  assert.ok(selected.addMesh >= 1);

  await page.click('#clash-detection-panel [data-key="action-back-to-all"]');
  await waitVm(page, (vm) => vm.selected === null);
  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__e2e.world.viewer.meshCount() === 0);

  await selectFirstRowWithMarkers(page);
  await page.evaluate(() => window.__e2e.panel.dispose());
  const after = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const { world } = window.__e2e;
    return {
      meshes: world.viewer.meshCount(),
      viewerListeners: world.viewer.listenerCount(),
      catalogListeners: world.catalog.listenerCount(),
      runListeners: world.engine.handles[0].listenerCount(),
      leases: world.engine.activeLeases(),
      panelInDom: document.getElementById('clash-detection-panel') !== null,
      theming: world.viewer.calls.filter((c) => /Theming/.test(c[0])).length,
      forbidden: world.engine.calls.filter((c) => ['register', 'unregister', 'invalidateModelPlacement', 'wireModelUnload'].includes(c[0])).length,
      showAfterDispose: (() => { window.__e2e.panel.show(); return window.__e2e.panel.isVisible(); })(),
    };
  });
  assert.deepEqual(after, {
    meshes: 0, viewerListeners: 0, catalogListeners: 0, runListeners: 0, leases: 0,
    panelInDom: false, theming: 0, forbidden: 0, showAfterDispose: false,
  });
}));

test('dispose during a HELD run stays pending until the engine finishes it, then leaves no mesh, listener or retained set', () => withPage(async ({ page }) => {
  await boot(page);
  await configureAndRun(page);
  await page.evaluate(() => window.__e2e.world.engine.handles[0].progress({ unitsEvaluated: 1, unitsTotal: 4, resultsFound: 1 }));
  await waitVm(page, (vm) => vm.run.state === 'running');
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    const { world, panel } = window.__e2e;
    world.engine.options.holdCancel = true;
    window.__disposeState = 'pending';
    window.__dispose = panel.dispose().then(() => { window.__disposeState = 'resolved'; }, (e) => { window.__disposeState = `rejected:${e?.name}`; });
  });
  // let every queued task/microtask run; the run is still held, so dispose must still be pending
  for (let i = 0; i < 5; i += 1) await page.evaluate(() => new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, 0)));
  const held = await page.evaluate(() => ({ state: window.__disposeState, reasons: window.__e2e.world.engine.handles[0].cancelReasons }));
  assert.equal(held.state, 'pending');
  assert.ok(held.reasons.includes('panel-disposed'), JSON.stringify(held.reasons));
  await page.evaluate(async () => {
    window.__e2e.world.engine.handles[0].finish({ status: 'cancelled' });   // saved, with results: a set to release
    await window.__dispose;
  });
  const r = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const { world } = window.__e2e;
    return {
      state: window.__disposeState,
      meshes: world.viewer.meshCount(),
      viewerListeners: world.viewer.listenerCount(),
      catalogListeners: world.catalog.listenerCount(),
      runListeners: world.engine.handles[0].listenerCount(),
      leases: world.engine.activeLeases(),
      released: world.engine.calls.some((c) => (c[0] === 'releaseResultSet' || c[0] === 'lease.release') && c[1] === 'run-1'),
    };
  });
  assert.deepEqual(r, { state: 'resolved', meshes: 0, viewerListeners: 0, catalogListeners: 0, runListeners: 0, leases: 0, released: true });
}));

test('two panels on ONE viewer own instance-scoped overlay scenes: clearing/disposing one leaves the other intact', () => withPage(async ({ page }) => {
  await page.evaluate(async () => {
    const fakes = await import('/test/clashpanel/dom/support/inPageFakes.mjs');
    const { createClashPanel } = await import('/clashpanel/index.js');
    const { INTENT } = await import('/clashpanel/core/intents.js');
    const world = fakes.createWorld();
    const make = (id) => createClashPanel({ Autodesk: window.Autodesk, viewer: world.viewer, THREE: world.THREE, engine: world.engine, catalog: world.catalog, events: world.events, id });
    window.__two = { world, INTENT, a: make('panel-a'), b: make('panel-b') };
  });
  const drive = async (name, handleIndex) => {
    const vm = `window.__two.${name}.controller.getViewModel()`;
    await page.evaluate(async (n) => {
      const { INTENT } = window.__two;
      const c = window.__two[n].controller;
      await c.dispatch({ type: INTENT.SETUP_TOGGLE_MODEL, side: 'A', modelKey: 'mA' });
      await c.dispatch({ type: INTENT.SETUP_TOGGLE_MODEL, side: 'B', modelKey: 'mB' });
    }, name);
    await page.waitForFunction(`${vm}.run.canRun === true`);
    await page.evaluate((n) => window.__two[n].controller.dispatch({ type: window.__two.INTENT.RUN_START }), name);
    await page.waitForFunction(`window.__two.world.engine.handles.length === ${handleIndex + 1}`);
    await page.evaluate((i) => window.__two.world.engine.handles[i].finish(), handleIndex);
    await page.waitForFunction(`${vm}.results.state === 'list'`);
    await page.evaluate((n) => window.__two[n].controller.dispatch({ type: window.__two.INTENT.NAV_SELECT, resultId: 'r1', groupId: null }), name);
    await page.waitForFunction(`${vm}.selected !== null`);
    if (!(await page.evaluate(`${vm}.selected.actions.markers.checked`))) {
      await page.evaluate((n) => window.__two[n].controller.dispatch({ type: window.__two.INTENT.ACTION_MARKERS, value: true }), name);
    }
    await page.waitForFunction(`(window.__two.world.viewer.sceneMeshes()['clash-panel-markers:${name === 'a' ? 'panel-a' : 'panel-b'}'] ?? 0) > 0`);
  };
  await drive('a', 0);
  await drive('b', 1);
  const scenes = () => page.evaluate(() => window.__two.world.viewer.sceneMeshes());
  const both = await scenes();
  assert.ok(both['clash-panel-markers:panel-a'] > 0 && both['clash-panel-markers:panel-b'] > 0, JSON.stringify(both));
  const bCount = both['clash-panel-markers:panel-b'];

  await page.evaluate(() => window.__two.a.controller.dispatch({ type: window.__two.INTENT.ACTION_BACK_TO_ALL }));
  await page.waitForFunction(() => (window.__two.world.viewer.sceneMeshes()['clash-panel-markers:panel-a'] ?? 0) === 0);
  assert.equal((await scenes())['clash-panel-markers:panel-b'], bCount);

  await page.evaluate(() => window.__two.a.dispose());
  const afterA = await scenes();
  assert.equal(afterA['clash-panel-markers:panel-b'], bCount);
  assert.equal(await page.evaluate(() => document.getElementById('panel-b') !== null && document.getElementById('panel-a') === null), true);

  await page.evaluate(() => window.__two.b.dispose());
  const r = await page.evaluate(() => ({ meshes: window.__two.world.viewer.meshCount(), listeners: window.__two.world.viewer.listenerCount() }));
  assert.deepEqual(r, { meshes: 0, listeners: 0 });
}));

test('construction rollback: createClashPanel failing mid-construction leaves no DOM node, subscription, viewer listener or overlay', () => withPage(async ({ page }) => {
  const r = await page.evaluate(async () => {
    const fakes = await import('/test/clashpanel/dom/support/inPageFakes.mjs');
    const { createClashPanel } = await import('/clashpanel/index.js');
    const out = {};
    // (a) the shell fails (DockingPanel initialize path throws after the base constructor appended its container)
    {
      const world = fakes.createWorld();
      const proto = window.Autodesk.Viewing.UI.DockingPanel.prototype;
      const original = proto.initializeMoveHandlers;
      proto.initializeMoveHandlers = () => { throw new RangeError('shell failed'); };
      let error = null;
      try { createClashPanel({ Autodesk: window.Autodesk, viewer: world.viewer, THREE: world.THREE, engine: world.engine, catalog: world.catalog, events: world.events, id: 'rb-a' }); } catch (e) { error = e.message; }
      proto.initializeMoveHandlers = original;
      out.a = { error, world };
    }
    // (b) the controller fails (the engine port is not an engine)
    {
      const world = fakes.createWorld();
      let error = null;
      try { createClashPanel({ Autodesk: window.Autodesk, viewer: world.viewer, THREE: world.THREE, engine: {}, catalog: world.catalog, events: world.events, id: 'rb-b' }); } catch (e) { error = e.name; }
      out.b = { error, world };
    }
    window.__rb = out;
    return { a: out.a.error, b: out.b.error };
  });
  assert.deepEqual(r, { a: 'shell failed', b: 'TypeError' });
  // teardown of the already-created controller/bridge is asynchronous: wait for it, then assert everything at once
  await page.waitForFunction(() => ['a', 'b'].every((k) => window.__rb[k].world.viewer.listenerCount() === 0 && window.__rb[k].world.catalog.listenerCount() === 0));
  const state = await page.evaluate(() => Object.fromEntries(['a', 'b'].map((k) => {
    const { world } = window.__rb[k];
    return [k, {
      panels: document.querySelectorAll(`#rb-${k}, .docking-panel`).length,
      containerChildren: world.viewer.container.children.length,
      viewerListeners: world.viewer.listenerCount(),
      catalogListeners: world.catalog.listenerCount(),
      meshes: world.viewer.meshCount(),
      scenes: Object.keys(world.viewer.sceneMeshes()).length,
      theming: world.viewer.calls.filter((c) => /Theming/.test(c[0])).length,
    }];
  })));
  const clean = { panels: 0, containerChildren: 0, viewerListeners: 0, catalogListeners: 0, meshes: 0, scenes: 0, theming: 0 };
  assert.deepEqual(state, { a: clean, b: clean });
}));
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

```js
// clashpanel/index.js — composition root of the Viewer Clash Panel (spec §5.1). The ONLY module that sees all
// three layers: headless core (controller), the ViewerBridge (the only 3D-scene mutator) and the thin UI shell.
// It receives every port by injection; it registers no model, derives no key, wires no unload, invalidates no
// placement (host responsibilities, PD-18/OQ-1 — see clashpanel/README.md). Toolbar button / extension
// registration are HOST shell code (gate H1), not part of this package.
import { createPanelController } from './core/index.js';
import { createViewerBridge } from './viewer/ViewerBridge.js';
import { createViewerApi } from './viewer/viewerApi.js';
import { createPanelShell } from './ui/ClashDockingPanel.js';

// Overlay scene names are INSTANCE-scoped (derived from the panel id), so two panels on one viewer never share a
// scene: clearing or disposing one can never remove the other's meshes or scenes.
const overlayNamesFor = (id) => Object.freeze({ overlayMarkers: `clash-panel-markers:${id}`, overlayOutlines: `clash-panel-outlines:${id}` });
const DEFAULT_ID = 'clash-detection-panel';
const DEFAULT_TITLE = 'Clash Detection';

function assertEvents(events) {
  if (typeof events?.BEFORE_MODEL_UNLOAD !== 'string' || events.BEFORE_MODEL_UNLOAD === ''
    || typeof events?.MODEL_REMOVED !== 'string' || events.MODEL_REMOVED === '') {
    throw new TypeError('createClashPanel: events.BEFORE_MODEL_UNLOAD and events.MODEL_REMOVED (event names) are required');
  }
}

/**
 * createClashPanel({ Autodesk, viewer, THREE, engine, catalog, scheduler?, doc?, events, id?, title? })
 *   -> { show, hide, toggle, isVisible, dispose(): Promise<void>, controller }
 * dispose(): shell → controller → bridge, each step guaranteed to run even when an earlier one throws; resolves
 * once all three completed, or rejects with an AggregateError listing every failed step (after ALL ran).
 * controller.dispose() cancels an active run ('panel-disposed') and resolves {released, errors} only after that
 * run's `done` has settled, its result set is released and the bridge is disposed; its `errors` (and
 * `released: false`) are folded into the AggregateError above. Await panel.dispose() BEFORE engine.dispose():
 * both are bounded by Core's drain of the in-flight work unit, and unbounded only by an executor that never
 * returns (Core open item O9). There is no Panel-side escape hatch.
 */
export function createClashPanel({ Autodesk, viewer, THREE, engine, catalog, scheduler, doc, events, id = DEFAULT_ID, title = DEFAULT_TITLE } = {}) {
  if (viewer === null || typeof viewer !== 'object') throw new TypeError('createClashPanel: viewer is required');
  assertEvents(events);
  const viewerApi = createViewerApi(viewer, { events: { BEFORE_MODEL_UNLOAD: events.BEFORE_MODEL_UNLOAD, MODEL_REMOVED: events.MODEL_REMOVED } });
  if (typeof id !== 'string' || id === '') throw new TypeError('createClashPanel: id must be a non-empty string');
  const bridge = createViewerBridge({ viewerApi, THREE, names: overlayNamesFor(id) });

  let controller;
  try {
    controller = createPanelController({ engine, catalog, bridge, scheduler });
  } catch (error) {
    void Promise.resolve().then(() => bridge.dispose()).catch(() => {});
    throw error;
  }

  let shell;
  try {
    shell = createPanelShell({ Autodesk, parentContainer: viewer.container, controller, id, title, doc });
  } catch (error) {
    void Promise.resolve()
      .then(() => controller.dispose())
      .catch(() => {})
      .then(() => bridge.dispose())
      .catch(() => {});
    throw error;
  }

  let disposing = null;
  async function disposeAll() {
    const errors = [];
    try {
      await shell.dispose();
    } catch (error) {
      errors.push(error);
    } finally {
      try {
        // controller.dispose() never rejects: it resolves {released, errors} (Part 3); fold both into this result.
        const outcome = await controller.dispose();
        if (Array.isArray(outcome?.errors)) errors.push(...outcome.errors);
        if (outcome?.released === false && !(Array.isArray(outcome?.errors) && outcome.errors.length > 0)) {
          errors.push(new Error('createClashPanel: the controller could not release every result set'));
        }
      } catch (error) {
        errors.push(error);
      } finally {
        try {
          await bridge.dispose();
        } catch (error) {
          errors.push(error);
        }
      }
    }
    if (errors.length > 0) throw new AggregateError(errors, 'createClashPanel: dispose completed with errors');
  }

  return Object.freeze({
    show: () => shell.show(),
    hide: () => shell.hide(),
    toggle: () => shell.toggle(),
    isVisible: () => shell.isVisible(),
    dispose: () => {
      if (disposing === null) disposing = disposeAll();
      return disposing;
    },
    controller,
  });
}
```

`clashpanel/README.md`:

````markdown
# clashpanel — Viewer Clash Panel (host-composition contract)

Governing design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-26-viewer-clash-panel-design.md` (the spec). This package is
the Panel only. It is **not integrated into any host yet**. Every live claim is gated (see "Gates").

## Layers

| Path | Role | May use |
|---|---|---|
| `core/` | headless controller + view-model (all workflow/domain state) | `clashtest/index.js` (error classes only) and siblings; no Autodesk, window, document, THREE |
| `viewer/` | `ViewerBridge`, the only code that changes the 3D scene (overlay markers/outlines, guarded isolation, fit) | the Viewer facade, `THREE` and event names, all injected |
| `ui/` | thin `DockingPanel` shell + DOM renderers of the view-model; text only through `textContent` | DOM, `Autodesk.Viewing.UI.DockingPanel` |
| `index.js` | `createClashPanel(...)` composition | the three layers above |

## Composition

```js
import { createClashPanel } from '/clashpanel/index.js';

const panel = createClashPanel({
  Autodesk,                    // the global namespace; the Panel uses only Autodesk.Viewing.UI.DockingPanel
  viewer,                      // a Viewer3D (GuiViewer3D) instance; the panel mounts into viewer.container
  THREE: window.THREE,         // the Viewer's own r71 THREE, never npm `three`
  engine,                      // the host-built clash-test engine (EnginePort below)
  catalog,                     // the host's read-only ModelCatalog (below)
  events: {
    BEFORE_MODEL_UNLOAD: Autodesk.Viewing.BEFORE_MODEL_UNLOAD_EVENT,
    MODEL_REMOVED: Autodesk.Viewing.MODEL_REMOVED_EVENT,
  },
  // scheduler?  { now, setTimeout, clearTimeout, yield }  default: global timers
  // doc?        Document used for rendering                default: the viewer container's document
});
panel.show(); panel.hide(); panel.toggle(); panel.isVisible();
await panel.dispose();         // shell → controller (cancels an active run 'panel-disposed', waits for its `done`,
                               // releases results, restores guarded isolation, removes Panel markers) → bridge
```

`dispose()` is idempotent (it returns the same promise). It resolves only after the active run's `done` has settled,
its result set is released and the bridge is disposed, so it stays pending while Core drains the in-flight work
unit. **Await `panel.dispose()` before `engine.dispose()`.** Both are bounded by Core's drain of the in-flight unit
and unbounded only by an executor that never returns (Core open item O9); `engine.dispose()` signals runs and then
awaits their drain, it does not force-resolve them, and there is no Panel-side escape hatch. Every step runs even
when an earlier one fails; the controller reports release problems as `{released, errors}` and those are folded in:
if any step failed or a set could not be released, `dispose()` rejects with an `AggregateError` **after** all
steps ran, so the host must `await` it inside `try/catch` (for example in the extension's `unload()`).

Several panels may share one viewer: each gets overlay scenes named after its `id`
(`clash-panel-markers:<id>`, `clash-panel-outlines:<id>`), so clearing or disposing one never touches another's
meshes. Give each panel a distinct `id` (default `clash-detection-panel`).

The toolbar button, the extension class and its registration are **host shell** code, not part of this package
(gate H1).

## Ports the host must supply

### EnginePort (a structural subset of the clash-test engine)

`validateTest`, `startRun`, `retainResultSet`, `releaseResultSet`, `getPersistenceState`, `getFreshness`,
`assessNoClashClaim`, `derivations.{summarize, groupBy, filter}`, `registry.bindingFor`. The Panel narrows whatever
it is given to exactly these members. It **never** calls `registry.register`, `registry.unregister`,
`invalidateModelPlacement`, `wireModelUnload`, or any model-identity derivation (PD-18).

### ModelCatalog (read-only, host-computed)

| Member | Contract |
|---|---|
| `list()` | the models currently in the scene: `[{ modelKey: string \| null, displayName: string, model, loaded: boolean }]`. `modelKey` is `null` when the host has not identified/registered that model. `loaded` means load complete **and** object tree available. |
| `displayNameFor(modelKey)` | `string \| null`; must survive unload (rows of unloaded models keep their name). |
| `keyOfModel(model)` | `string \| null`; a `WeakMap<Model, modelKey>` that survives unload/unregister. |
| `onChange(cb)` | returns an unsubscribe function; fires on model add/remove **and** readiness changes. |
| `measurementBasis(modelKeys)` | `BasisVerdict` or a promise of one: `{ state: 'verified', basisKey }` or `{ state: 'unverified' \| 'incompatible', reason }`. A missing method, a throw, a timeout or any other shape is treated as unverified. Soft (clearance) is available only for one model or a `verified` verdict (PD-17). |

### Host responsibilities (never done by the Panel)

* load the models as **SVF2** (PD-15);
* build the collision world, the engine and the element enumerator;
* register every model with `engine.registry.register(modelKey, model, { modelVersion })`, and register again
  after a reload; the `modelKey`/`modelVersion` derivation is **OQ-1**;
* wire unload with `wireModelUnload` from `clashtest/viewer/index.js`;
* call `invalidateModelPlacement` when a model moves (PR-OQ17);
* supply the measurement-basis evidence behind `measurementBasis` (PR-BASIS);
* serve `/clashtest/**` and `/clashpanel/**` as static JavaScript to the page.

## What the Panel does and does not do in the 3D scene

It adds only its own overlay meshes (scenes `clash-panel-markers:<id>` and `clash-panel-outlines:<id>`), changes aggregate
isolation only when the Isolate toggle is on and the isolation prerequisite holds (restoring it only if nobody
else changed it since), and fits the camera best-effort. It never calls a theming method, never changes the
Viewer selection and never restores the camera.

## Gates (open; nothing here is live-verified)

| Gate | What stays unproven until it closes |
|---|---|
| **PG-4** SVF2 verification of F1–F8 | every model-format-sensitive assumption; the offline suites use fakes only |
| **PG-1** live Viewer API evidence (overlays, isolation, fit, element bounds, DockingPanel lifecycle) on SVF2 | the DOM suite uses a DockingPanel **stub** that mirrors source-observed semantics |
| **OQ-1** modelKey/modelVersion derivation (host) | reload identity; integration acceptance |
| **PR-BASIS / PG-5** measurement-basis evidence | Soft availability for more than one model |
| **PG-2 / PG-3** first live engine run; measurements | any claim about scale; page size stays a presentation constant, not a limit |

## Tests

* `npm test` — the default gate: the offline suites (`npm run test:offline`) and then the DOM suite. Either half
  failing fails it; it needs Playwright's Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium`).
* `npm run test:offline` — the headless core and bridge suites only (Node; never launches a browser).
* `npm run test:clashpanel:dom` — the renderers, the shell and an end-to-end slice in headless Chromium over fake
  ports (`test/clashpanel/dom/`); part of `npm test`, available alone for targeted runs.
````

If the E2E stalls in a `waitForFunction`, the cause is a real core/bridge behavior gap against the spec rows named in the scope note, or a Viewer member `viewerApi.js` reads that `inPageFakes.mjs` does not model — fix the production code, or add the missing read-only member to the fake; never weaken an assertion.

## Gated work — recorded, NOT executable, NOT authorized

These items are **dependencies and gates, not tasks the plan absorbs**. None has RED/GREEN steps, on purpose: each needs evidence or owner decisions that do not exist yet (SVF2 evidence, OQ-1), and each requires its own explicit owner authorization. When a gate opens, the task must be authored (or this plan amended) and reviewed before execution.

### G1: SVF2 verification of the model-format-sensitive assumptions F1–F8 (PG-4) — **[S]**, separate activity

* **What it is.** The bounded live verification that the spec §2.1 assumptions F1–F8 hold for **SVF2/OTG-loaded** models (fragment→owner mapping and object-tree agreement; tree-reachable population = fragment population; readiness order; per-fragment collision reads; population/fragment bounds; unload/reload behaviour; the Viewer API behaviours the ViewerBridge relies on incl. which visibility branch an OTG model takes; dbId identity across `fragList.getDbIds`/object tree/isolate/fit/name/bounds).
* **Why it is not in this plan.** Owner direction: not authorized, and the design chose RQ-1 = (b). Completed T3 evidence is **SVF non-OTG only** (`isOTG: false`) and is never SVF2 evidence.
* **Package scoping (RQ-1).** F1–F6 gate live Adapter/Collision/lifecycle work (H1, H2, G3). F7–F8 gate the live ViewerBridge and dbId handoff (G2, G3).
* **Entry:** explicit owner authorization; an SVF2-loaded fixture with `model.isOTG() === true` recorded as a precondition. **Exit:** a research record under `docs/research/` + independent verification (mirroring the T3 pattern), each of F1–F8 marked verified / failed / not-evidenced. A failure is triaged separately against the Adapter/Core under its own authorization — **not** pre-authorized here.
* **Blocks:** G2, G3, H1 acceptance, and any "v1 supports SVF2" claim. **Does not block:** T1–T33.

### G2: Live ViewerBridge / DockingPanel verification (PG-1) — **[S]**

* **Depends on:** G1 (F7–F8), and Tasks 22–26 and 31 implemented. **Files (when authorized):** `test/acceptance/clashpanel-viewerbridge.acceptance.mjs` (Playwright, never `*.test.mjs`, not in `npm test`, mirrors `clashtest-viewer-adapter.acceptance.mjs`), a research record under `docs/research/`.
* **Live checks the accepted design lists as still open (spec §16):** aggregate `fitToView` union world-bounds for two models; unit scales of the fixture models; **element world-bounds correctness** for the bounds-outline overlay and overlay-scene (`viewer.overlays.*`) rendering on the SVF2 branch; `getNodeName` for a dbId/model just unloaded; `getAggregateIsolation` read-and-compare and `getAggregateHiddenNodes` behaviour; `hideModel` firing `MODEL_REMOVED` but not `BEFORE_MODEL_UNLOAD`; DockingPanel subclass lifecycle (one visibility listener, no `setVisible` after `uninitialize`); `isOTG === true` recorded for every model as a precondition.
* **Degradation contract planned by T23/T25/T26** (once T1–T33 are implemented; it must then be confirmed live, not re-designed): no element bounds ⇒ location marker only; no union framing ⇒ fit first live side; isolation prerequisite unmet ⇒ Isolate disabled, never `setAggregateIsolation([])`.
* **Exit:** each check PASS/FAIL with evidence; **no claim beyond the recorded envelope**.

### G3: Panel live acceptance (PG-2 / PG-3 / PG-5) — **[S] [H]**

* **Depends on:** G2, H1, H2, and T33. **Files (when authorized):** `test/acceptance/clashpanel.acceptance.mjs` + record under `docs/research/`.
* **Scope:** the first-ever engine run over real **SVF2** models through the Panel (the Core README says the engine is verified only with fakes; `test/acceptance/clash-test.acceptance.mjs` does not exist); records measured result counts, planning/run durations and memory **without** asserting or claiming an SLO (G-CAL/G-RESP, PD-13); Soft only where PR-BASIS/PG-5 evidence exists; failures found are triaged against Core/Adapter under separate authorization, **not absorbed by the Panel**.

### H1: Host composition (PR-HOST) — **[H]**

* **Owns (never Panel core):** loading models as SVF2; building `CollisionWorld.fromViewer` / `createViewerElementEnumerator` / `createClashTestEngine`; `wireModelUnload`; registering models and **re-registering after reload**; supplying the read-only `ModelCatalog` (`list/displayNameFor/keyOfModel/onChange/measurementBasis`, readiness events + low-frequency poll while the Panel is visible and a participating model is not ready); serving `/clashtest` and `/clashpanel` statically (today `server.js` serves only `wwwroot` and `/collision`); `wwwroot/extensions/ClashPanelExtension.js` (toolbar `onToolbarCreated` + `ControlGroup` + `Button`, removed in `unload()`, calling `createClashPanel`); registration in `wwwroot/viewer.js`.
* **Entry:** explicit owner authorization; H2 decided. This plan provides the consumable seam (`createClashPanel` + README host contract, Task 32) and stops there.

### H2: OQ-1 / PR-OQ17 / PR-BASIS — **[H]**

* **OQ-1 (OD-8):** `modelKey`/`modelVersion` derivation policy (spec §24; interim option: fresh key per load + host-supplied version witness for live acceptance only). **PR-OQ17:** who calls `invalidateModelPlacement` when a model moves. **PR-BASIS:** host supplies `measurementBasis(modelKeys)` with *evidence* of a common world-coordinate/unit basis (what suffices — e.g. equal `getUnitScale()` plus a verified shared frame, or an evidenced load-time normalization — is settled under PG-5). The reload-digest discrepancy is **not** a Panel prerequisite (spec §11.3).
* **Panel-side stance (planned by T5/T6/T15/T16; not yet implemented):** consume only; missing/stale binding ⇒ Run disabled / rows unavailable; Soft unavailable without a verified basis.
